emails.subject: 💸  Do your first website flip for only $2k
emails.content:
Nano Thought

Networking over everything else.

Who you know can make or break your career. My best deals come from personal connections, and I suspect that many successful people would say the same. The circle you're in determines what opportunities you'll get to partake in.

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Mastering Twitter opens insane doors Sadly, most do the opposite of what they should For the past 18 months, Ive built lifelong relationships, made millions, and gained 58.2k followers along the way Here are 4 pieces of advice that will help you do the same 🧵👇
May 24th 2022
38
Retweets
390
Likes

Twitter has been the best place to network. I've met hundreds of successful, smart people that are now in my network. The best part? Off-market deals are always the best deals, and you can get access to lots of them with the right network.

I often don't have to do much work to find these deals. People who know what I do will pass me opportunities all the time to buy or invest in various websites.

Highly recommend getting on Twitter and documenting what you're working on! You'll be surprised at who will take an interest.

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

I want to highlight a small deal this week to drive home the point that you don't need a massive amount of capital to get started with website flipping. The best part about websites as an asset class is that they don't require huge capital and/or risks to make good money, unlike real estate and stocks.

​Link to Listing​

Using a 40x monthly multiple, this site is probably worth $2,300 or so. But it could go lower, don't forget - its an auction! The reserve price is $1,000, and it probably won't go for much more than that. Let's just say it will sell for $2,000 for the sake of running this hypothetical deal.

This isn't the juiciest flip opportunity I've ever seen, but this could still be a good learning experience for someone starting out.

It already has Ezoic, which is usually the first change I make to increase a site's revenue (if the site is using adsense)

The site itself isn't bad, so I don't see a ton of room for improvement with the layout although we def could make it feel a better more professional with a different theme. There is definitely some low-hanging fruit keyword wise though.

I pulled up Ahrefs and found a bunch of opportunities, like "largest electric griddle":

​

​

There's almost no competition for this keyword but decent volume. The page that's ranking #1 doesn't have any backlinks. Some great content and a few backlinks from relevant sites could take this website to #1 pretty quickly for several low competition keywords. I did a high level look at the backlink profile of the site and competition but make sure to do your own research!

Since there aren't many obvious changes to make besides SEO strategy, I would say this website is more of a buy and hold. You'll make more money over time as those SEO efforts begin to pay off over several months.

However, if you're looking to do more with this site, you could add a lead magnet and collect emails. You could do something like offering a free PDF with recipes if the reader signs up for your email list.

In my experience, you can hope to capture 2% of your audience's email if the lead magnet features the right offer. Over a year, you could build up an email list of about 1,000 people.

Let's say you also increase traffic by 2% a month using your new SEO strategy. By the end of the first year, you're adding about 100 new emails to your list each month.

An email list based on this site's audience might be able to be monetized at a rate of $0.25 per subscriber per month? Its really going to depend on the offer, but it's possible! While it's not a ton, that's an extra $250 or so per month after 12 months, or $3k per year - more than the initial investment of buying the site.

So after a year, you might be able to turn a $2k investment into:

  • $777.90 of ad revenue over the 12 months
  • 794 email subscribers that have earned you $1185.13 over the year
  • Add those up and you got back $1,963.03 over the year
  • A website worth $6500+ (40x monthly average monthly revenue over the last 12 months)

Year one you've generated an 80% return on your initial investment if this played out. Even before you sell it.

Total ROI if this played out as broken down like above would be 323.15% and you would put $8463.03 back in your pocket

Ok fine, you have some costs - hosting for $10 a month or less if you already have some. You get the point.

One potential negative about this site: Note the drop in traffic from December & January, which means the site may have been penalized. I'd want to get the recent data on traffic and make sure that its stayed stable this year and month.

Hope this breakdown was helpful. Again, always do your own research and develop your own frameworks for evaluating deals based on your skills! This is just one of many ways this site could be approached and played out.

Nano Tips

Google released a search algorithm updated on May 25th. This article gives a good summary of the changes. In short, this update is broad and doesn't penalize any specific type of content or websites.

It's Google's regular update to improve the overall function of the search algorithm. Google doesn't give much guidance on these types of updates besides reminding everyone that it's a broad update that will likely affect just about every website's search rankings.

Everyone freaks out about algo updates, but remember: If someone moves down in the rankings, someone else moves up. It's a zero sum game, so not everyone "loses" like a lot of people would make you think.

Just remember to keep building great sites with compelling offers and interesting content, and avoid super black hat techniques and spammy backlinks. Aside from that, I wouldn't spend time obsessing over changes in the algorithm.

Builders Build

Check out the latest episode of Builders Build here. It's all about how to sell products on Amazon with our guest Leslie Hensell, co-founder of Riverbend Consulting.

A lot of the sites I buy use Amazon's affiliate program, but I'm far from an expert on how Amazon works for sellers. Luckily, Lesley is an expert and filled us in.

She has personally helped hundreds of third-party sellers with everything from selling their businesses, to getting their accounts and ASINs (Amazon Standard Identification Number) back up and running. Crazily enough, her clients range from small mom-and-pop brands, all the way to companies doing over $1 billion a year.

​Listen Here​

​

Thanks for reading! I'll hit your inbox next week with another breakdown of a website flip.

Thanks from the Nano Flips team

emails.subject: winter is coming
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}, it’s James here

​

If you’re finding yourself paying more attention to prices at restaurants.
​

Or noticing your rent or mortgage payment more.

​
Or feeling like gas is super expensive.

​

I feel you.

​

We’re dealing with unprecedented times…

​

And I’ll give it to you straight.

​

We’re seeing signs of a real recession on the horizon.
​

And the way I see it?
​

We’ve got 3 major forces affecting us right now…

​

First…

Inflation.

… effectively making your cash worth less with every passing month.

“80% of all US dollars in existence were printed in the last 22 months“ - techstartups.com, DECEMBER 18, 2021​
​

​

Second…

Rising cost of living affecting Rent. Food. Gas.

As a result of

Rising energy prices.

Goods shortages.

Shipping costs.

War in Ukraine.

​
​

And lastly?

We may be looking at both a Dotcom 2.0 scenario in the stock and crypto markets…

“... stock crash – dotcom bust 2.0 is upon us“ — Moneyweek, May 19th 2022

… AND a Housing Bubble

“... US new-home sales just plunged to pandemic-era lows” — Business Insider, May 24th, 2022

​
​

Bottom line?

Cash is worth less and less.

Living costs are rising.

Traditional assets are at risk.

​

Now I’m no fortune teller

But all the signs point to a cold recession in the coming months

And my advice to you is simple.
​

Ask yourself:

​

Would I still be able to pay the bills if I lost my main income? If I was laid off?

​

Do I have multiple streams of income?

​

Can I earn remotely if I had to move?
​

Are my incomes recession proof?
​

If you aren’t sure about the answers that’s okay.
​

Look
​

You’ve still got 6 months till 2022 ends in order to lock-in your income strategy.
​

But that window of opportunity is closing down.

​

So while you still can?
​

Make sure you invest your time, energy and capital into long term assets that’ll increase your monthly income.

​
By the end of 2022, those who will still

​

Spend their days refreshing charts and praying for “green days”

​

Depend on financial youtubers to save them​
​

Or gamble on cryptos​
​

WILL GET LEFT BEHIND

​

World’s simply changing too fast

​

This is your time to build wealth predictably.

​

It’s time to take control of your income strategy.

​

Own Airbnbs rich folks will still pay for in a recession

Own a recession service proof business

Own a digital property

​

… and actively grow your monthly income!​
​

Rooting for ya,

James

​

P.S.
​

In the next email I’ll share my own strategy for navigating this period, are you cool with that?

If not, just click this link, and I won’t message you about it.

emails.subject: “monthly paycheck” without a boss
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}, it’s James here.

We have opened up the Special Edition Nano Flips "Digital Real Estate Empire" Mentorship Program.

And I just gotta say...

CONGRATULATIONS if you locked in your spot already!

HOLD TIGHT!

The magic of flipping is about to get very real.

I’m working through the email questions from some of you right now.

But I just wanted to take a quick break to tell you WHY I like this opportunity so much...

And why I’m so pumped to peel back the curtain for you.

(BTW, if you don't want hear more about this offer, just click here.)

So back when I was 19-20 I’d had a my first exit.

And sure, I blew some cash or whatever...

I was a young guy and that’s kind of a rite of passage at that age.

But then I thought I’d go and give this “digital nomad” thing a try.

So I was traveling around Thailand, Cambodia, Bali, just seeing South East Asia generally.

And let me tell you…

That kind of freedom is something else.

It’s VERY different from a vacation.

Because most people go on vacay and work half the time.

But if you do it right?

You get a long stretch of time to FULLY defragment and work out what YOU really want to FOCUS on in your life.

It’s not something our parents had, just working from anywhere or taking a sabbatical when you need to recharge

I’s a bit more common now, people doing this kind of stuff...

But back then?

It wasn’t something the average person could do.

Real talk: it’s empowering to run things from a laptop while you admire the beautiful view and sip on some fresh coffee.

You’re just thinking… “Hmm shall I go for a massage or shall I make some more money?”

But to do this?

First, you gotta get FREE.

And as I said a couple of emails ago…

If you’re built anything like me…

This sort of life loses its shine quickly.

After about a year I went back to building.

Or I should say...

I went back to helping OTHERS build.

I didn’t want to give up the lifestyle, necessarily.

But I did want to get my hands dirty again.

So I started helping out with mentorship programs.

I helped out with a few, but Google Launchpad was the main one.

Why am I telling you this?

2 reasons, and then I’m going to get back to your emails…

  1. I believe that, with the way the world is changing, faster than ever before… It’s IMPERATIVE to separate yourself from a job and a fixed location ASAP. It’s straightforward to do by learning very simple skills that, once understood, can be easily outsourced. I am going to take you through all of this, step-by-step, in the mentorship program.
    ​
  2. I want to make it clear to anyone “on the fence” about this opportunity that I know EXACTLY what I am doing. I have been successful enough at a young age to not just make big money flipping digital real estate but also to be trusted by Google and now Tech Stars to mentor people in online business.

​Sure, you can go rogue and do some freelancing or consulting (did this too)...

But let me tell you…

Nothing…

NOTHING

Beats owning a business that gives you “monthly paychecks” WITHOUT having to actively do work.

It feels weird at first. You’re always looking for something to do.

But after a while you realize that the money is going to keep rolling in even if you did nothing.

So your focus shifts from

“What tasks do I have to accomplish today?”

To

“How do I raise the rent on my digital property and increase my income even more?”

If you take this opportunity?

You’ll likely find that while the digital nomad life is cool (for a while)

You’ll be too excited by LIFE to spend it all in flip flops.

It would be my honor to be your guide.

If you’re ready…

===> Get all the details and join us here ​

To freeing up your time,

James

P.S. There's no one-click upsell after the page you're going to click on. Everything you need is included. So click right here to get the deets and join us on this adventure.

I really do love America.

I love the IDEA of America.

Waiting to get a raise from their boss.

You can start with less than $100 if you're building from scratch, and maybe $500 or so if you're buying an existing site. I don't know of a better way to build a cash-flowing portfolio of businesses than owning websites.

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

This week we found a great opportunity to build a community and long tail content for a site listed on Motion Invest:

​

​

​

​

This one isn't a huge business, but you could probably grow it steadily and make some good money. Traffic is stable and the site survived the Google core update in May, which rocked many others.

Here's a look at the traffic:

​

This website is an affiliate business in the gun accessories niche, specifically scopes. The great part about a niche like that is that your customer base is very passionate about the subject, which means there's like an opportunity to build a community/newsletter around your site.

I also like that the traffic is nice and spread out, the top page accounts for less than 9% of the overall traffic.

Communities/newsletters are secret weapons for content sites. Build an engaged community around your subject matter, even if it's small, and you'll do well. You can find free content contributors and will have a way to get people coming back to you again and again. This might be a newsletter or something like a Facebook Group.

If you take a look at the analytics above, you'll see a pretty good foundation to work with. The average time on page is pretty high, meaning the existing audience is fairly engaged with the content already. Would be great to lower that bounce rate though!

The site makes its money from 2 sources: Amazon and Ezoic.

Right now, the site is definitely not optimized. Some of the display ad spots aren't set up properly; a few of them are cut off on the margin, and others take up way too much space. The first thing I'd do is clean up the design of the website so that the ads display properly. That should increase income right away. The team at Ezoic could help you do this. Or if you increased traffic, taking the site to MediaVine or Adthrive would be a great idea.

Besides that, I'd immediately create a newsletter/or FB group and implement a popup that asks visitors to sign up. If we could convert 2% of website visitors to the newsletter, we'd start adding 144 subscribers per month (based on the past 6 month average of site visitors).

Here's how this flip could look:

Investment:

  • $14,102 purchase
  • $485 monthly profit (based on May numbers)
  • 29.07x monthly profit multiple

Value Add:

  • Increase monthly profit from Ezoic by 25% through optimization and traffic increase (from $71 to $88.75+)
  • Increase monthly profit from Amazon by 25% optimization and traffic increase (from $414 to $517.5)
  • Create email newsletter or community and convert 2% of website visitors
    • After 6 months, you'd have 950 subscribers (assuming moderate website traffic growth of ~2% per month)
    • You can monetize newsletters at around $0.25 per subscriber per month - or $237.50 by month 6

By month 6, you should have an asset producing $843.75 per month - an annual run rate of $10,125!

Let's keep the math super simple for this one, and assume you don't even make more money as it grows in the first 6 months, but that at month 6, is when your optimizations come into changing the revenue (Amazon, Ezoic, and the newsletter/community). You would have collected $2910 in rev for the first 6 months, and $5062.50 in next 6 months.

...And you now have an asset worth $24,527.81 assuming you could sell for the same multiple you bought the site for.

The Return:

  • $7,972.50 in revenue collected
  • $24,527.81 sale of website
  • $32,500.31 Total Return
  • -$14,102 purchase (and lets just say - $3600 for the year in content/links/hosting) = $14798.31 Net Profit
  • 104.93% return in 12 months

Of course, this is just a hypothetical scenario. Always do your own research and evaluate each opportunity based on your skillset! I kept the math simple on this one to break down a scenario, obviously it could be more or less.

Lets note somethings to be careful of with the site:

  • backlink profile is weak
  • low domain rank with Ahrefs - probably need to aggressively work on a link building strategy to keep its rankings and keep it growing.
  • Strong competitors in the space
  • site hasn't been around that long
  • Not TONS of opportunities to increase revenue without really increasing traffic

​

Nano Tips

Everyone seems to be worried about SEO for websites they want to flip. Keep in mind that there is more than one way to grow a site.

Email, social, Facebook groups, Quora, syndication deals etc all exist.

Don't lean on just one channel - become a great growth hacker and CMO and you wont be stuck relying only on SEO for traffic. If you're not great at SEO, then don't spend all day banging your head against the wall.

Figure out what your marketing strengths are, and use that skill to grow whatever website you buy.

Try not to rely on just one source of traffic!

​

Builders Build

Last week on the pod, we did a 1-year recap on Colin’s wife’s eCommerce business acquisition, Glowless.

On this episode we recap where the business started, what was executed on in the first year, and where it’s going in the next 12 months. Topics include:

  • Product cost down and packaging overhaul
  • SEO successes
  • Email automation
  • Conversion rate optimization
  • Tik Tok organic and paid
  • The offer: Starter kits? Recurring?

​

​

​Listen Here​

Thanks for reading! I'll hit your inbox next week with another breakdown of a website flip.

Thanks from the Nano Flips team

(James)

Check out 2 newsletters from my best friends Oren and Colin

Product People - Learn the art of building CPG brands with Oren Schauble: https://go.orenjohn.com/cpg/​

emails.subject: 💸  Making $5,700 a month with facts about Turkey?
emails.content:
Nano Thought

I love buying all types of assets. I've bought rental properties and I always dollar cost average into ETFs.

But there's a reason my best investments are my own websites: I have control.

Now this doesn't mean that I always make a ton of money on every deal. There are definitely losses. A site could get hit with a penalty and lose its ranking, causing traffic to plummet. It's happened to me before.

But at least when I buy a website, I'm in control of the asset. I can determine what changes to make in order to grow cash flow and the value of my investment. Can't say the same about ETFs.

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
The difference between investing in Real Estate and websites is that my websites have never needed a new $15,000 furnace.
June 27th 2022
17
Retweets
271
Likes

One other great thing about investing in websites: A website never needs an emergency $15,000 repair. If a website I buy ends up becoming broken beyond repair, I can always sell it to someone who wants to rebuild it. Just the domains alone are worth real money. This really helps limit the downside.

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

​
Stumbled on this interesting website for sale: Turkpidya, a Turkish encyclopedia. From the listing: "In a nutshell, Turkpidya describes everything about Turkey to the rest of the globe, including tourism, economy, wholesale, retail, culture and history."

This is a larger flip then we usually talk about here: About $3,200 in monthly profit and an asking price of $130,000.

​​​

​Link to Listing​

Here are a few of the pros:

  1. High authority: SemRush score of 46
  2. First and only online Turkish encyclopedia
  3. 223,000 pageviews per month (average over previous 6 months)

Here are a few of the cons:

  1. If you don't know much about the country of Turkey, you could have a tough time running this site
  2. Very little traffic from countries like the USA, UK, and Canada
  3. The site is not very old

While you definitely don't need to be an expert in the subject matter of a site you buy, I wouldn't recommend buying a site within a niche you know nothing about. I don't think you absolutely need to know Turkish (it would def help!), though - you can either hire copywriters, or simply write in English and have the content translated automatically (the website currently does this; all of the content is automatically translated into 17 languages depending on where the reader is viewing the site from).

From the listing:

"We have around 20K clicks from Turkpidya to other websites. Only 50% of these clicks are monetised. If you increase this ratio by making more deals and signing up for more affiliate programs, you can easily generate more income."

Even though the site is not very old, I still like what I'm seeing on Ahrefs:

If I were to purchase this site, here are a few of the changes I'd make to increase the cash flow and overall value of the asset over a 12 month holding period:

  1. Switch to Ezoic, AdThrive, or Mediavine if they will take the international traffic (you'll need to check with your preferred ad network to see if they will). I would expect this change to increase revenue by 50% over 12 months.
  2. Fix affiliate links - this change is suggested by the seller in the listing. This should be good for about a 25% pop in revenue.

Let's do some math. Assuming we can successfully implement those changes over 12 months, we'd have a website generating $5,762.75 per month after 12 months.

Assuming the same multiple we hypothetically bought the site at (39.5x monthly profit), the site would now be worth $227,628.

Not even factoring in the cash flow you collected, that's a 75% return on your initial investment.

Factoring in that cash flow, you'd have collected $54,334.50 over 12 months as you scaled profit from about $3,200 a month to $5,762.75.

So let's say you decide to sell the site at the end of 12 months for $227,628. Your total net return would be $151,962 on a $130k investment. Not bad at all.

This example doesn't even assume any organic traffic growth, which would almost certainly happen. You could also add other monetization sources, like dropshipping products and a newsletter.

This is a hypothetical example; always do your own research and account for your skillsets. This flip is a pretty unique one, but it would be a huge win for the right person.

Nano Tips

If you're just starting out, go for the lowest hanging fruit for your content. Don't even worry about search terms above 100 volume on Ahrefs. Just get some content out there!

Picking a niche you like or know a lot about can be a life hack. Keep it simple, and just start with what you know.

​

Builders Build

This week on Builders Build, we talked about how to make your website faster with Shawn O'Neill.

Besides the shocking ROI of a single millisecond improvement, the pod covers causes and benefits, including common culprits such as:

  • sudden growth, which generally results in less communication as people just carry on trying to do their best
  • a lack of focus on site speed or a lack of issues reported about it
  • optimizing too soon with too many addons or plugins
  • over-dynamic pages with tons of media or product
  • lazy-loading addons which sometimes lazy load the user experience, too.

​

​Listen Here​

​

​

Thanks from the Nano Flips team

emails.subject: 💸 Dog Affiliate Site Doing $477/month
emails.content:
Nano Thought

It's no secret that our lives are increasingly being lived online. If you're looking for business opportunities, I'd encourage you to look at business models that work well in the physical world that haven't yet fully transitioned online.

For example: Does your local cleaning service allow customers to book and pay for a cleaning online? If not, there's an opportunity there.

Does your local junk removal company offer online booking, or do they make customers call for a quote?

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Steps to build a lucrative, low-maintenance business: 1. Find a business that does well in the physical world 2. Set up a website and allow users to book/purchase online. 3. Get paid for a flat fee for all the online bookings you send the business That’s it.
July 7th 2022
9
Retweets
170
Likes

This tweet explains just one of the possible business models, but there are several options: Generate leads and send them to an existing business for a fee, start your own business using tech as your competitive advantage, or buy an existing business that isn't using technology like they should. Or even start a consulting business and help those companies take orders and payment online. There are infinite possibilities.

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

​I'm back with another dog website, but this one's a bigger flip than the dog frisbee site I wrote about a while ago.

It's an affiliate site about dog products that does $477 a month in profit.

​​​

​Link to Listing​

Here are a few things that stick out in the listing:

  • 293 blog posts currently on the site
  • Recently declining traffic as current owner hasn't published new content lately
  • In May, 86% of revenue was from Ezoic and 14% was from Amazon affiliates
  • Includes an active Facebook page

And some opportunities the current owner has outlined for this site:

  • More frequent posting of high-quality articles
  • Explore different, higher paying, affiliate platforms
  • Create a focused SEO strategy to target keywords
  • Host paid guest posts
  • Create an email list

Let's break down the math of flipping this site.

The current price is $13,000, but I expect that it will sell for higher. 40x monthly earnings is pretty typical for a content site these days, so let's say the final price is $19,000.

For $19k, you're buying a site that produces $477 a month, or $5,724 per year.

As I've said before, you can make okay money just buying and holding website, but the real profits come from improving the websites so that you can increase cash flow and the final value of the site.

So how do you increase cash flow?

There's a couple primary options: Increase traffic, or increase revenue per user by adding better affiliate programs or new revenue sources.

Basically, you can either bring more users to the site, or you can increase the average revenue per existing user. This is true for all websites.

Of course, it's best to do both. So first, I'd make a plan to increase the amount of content being produced for the site. I'd also audit past content and make sure it's optimized for the products we're offering on the site.

Let's do some math on how we could improve the site:

  • Increase revenue from existing traffic in year 1 by offering new revenue sources: Maybe building an email list and selling products to it by dropshipping them.
    • Let's say we convert 2% of website visitors to an email list, and we monetize those subscribers at a rate of $0.10 per subscriber per month. That means that after 12 months (even if we didn't grow the site at all and base this on the average of the visitors in the last 12 months) we would have 5000+ new email subscribers bringing in $500 a month in revenue.
    • Let's be even more conservative and assume hold this site for 2 years and that after 12 months we don't even continue to grow the email list more than it churns. So you never have more than 5k subscribers AND we dont monetize them until month 12.

If we can implement these changes correctly, that gives us a new profit of $977/month, or $11,724 per year. To be safe? Let's say we have some churn of the list and costs to manage the site. So? $10k a year in net profit.

On a $19k initial investment, those numbers are pretty good. As you ramped up to $977/month in revenue over the course of that first year, you would have made $5,724 during year 1. Year 2? We made $11,724 ($10K).

And now, your site is worth $33,333 using the same multiple you bought the site for (40x the monthly net income average of $10k a year)

So after year 2:

  • Investment of $19k
  • Collected $15,724 in ad revenue from on the site AND the newsletter
  • Site is now worth $33,300+

So let's say we sell this site! ($33,333 + $15,724) - $19,000 = Total profit of $30,057

As always, this is just a hypothetical example. Always do your own research and evaluate opportunities based on your own skills. Site looks decent in Ahrefs but its traffic decline that we can see in the listing recently is something to really look out for!

​

​

Builders Build

This week, the Builders Build team are joined by a young man from Pennsylvania with a dark secret… Meet Miles Longstreth, Amazon FBA specialist.

The most fundamental business of them all is about buying a product and selling it for more than you paid for it. We’re builders and merchants, and we love this niche!

​

​Listen Here​

​In this episode, Miles talks about:

  • His FBA business
  • SellerAmp SAS (Sourcing Analysis Simplified)
  • Building a personal brand
  • Info on products
  • Niche opportunities
  • Sales tax and arbitrage

​

​Link to Listing​

"Opportunity For Growth - Because the owner is focused on other businesses and only uses this website for Amazon and FreezerFit affiliate revenue, any buyer looking to partner with more affiliates, focus more on SEO, implement display ads, collect emails, create a digital product, etc has a great opportunity to increase the monthly revenue substantially. FreezerFit is also growing at a nice rate which should increase monthly Cuisinen affiliate revenue."

With that in mind, one of the first changes I'd make is adding Ezoic for display ads.

With the current level of traffic, I'd expect that adding Ezoic could increase monthly profit by $100 or more if optimized. I would be careful to just have ads in places that wouldn't pull away from your potential affiliate commissions.

This site's starting price on Flippa is $19k, but it will almost certainly sell for more than that. A good rule of thumb is 40x monthly profit, or $44,440. Let's say you buy it and plan to improve the website over 12 months, then sell it.

There are 2 changes I'd plan to institute right away:

  • Add display ads from Ezoic. If done right, this would add $100 a month in monthly cash flow.
  • Add a newsletter. A newsletter is a great way to "own your audience" and increase your revenue by sending offers directly to your users.

Now let's take a look at how those changes would improve our cash flow and the value of the website.

For this example, let's assume zero traffic growth. Of course, I'd want to have a strategy to increase traffic for any site I bought, but let's keep this scenario simple.

  • $100 Ezoic display ads
  • $168 newsletter revenue

If you count that cash flow through those first 12 months, you would have brought in $15,540.

Even with just those two changes, this would be a great flip if you're able to execute.

But there are other changes I'd look into. The site has a very low DR and a pretty weak backlink profile, so I'd look at building way more backlinks ASAP for it.

emails.content:
Nano Thought

Earlier this week, I wrote a thread about how I started an ad network at 19 that was making up to $20k a week by the time I was 21. We then sold the business as my first exit.

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
When I was 19 I started an ad network By 21 It was hitting $20k+ weeks Here’s how I used authority to grow (and sell) a business...
July 14th 2022
25
Retweets
206
Likes

If you're interested, you can read the entire story here. But the tl:dr is this:

Arbitrage.

Most marketing opportunities are about arbitrage. Paying $28 for a lead and selling it for $48, for example. Those were the basic economics of the ad network I started and scaled.

If you're looking to build an online business, think in terms of arbitrage: What can you buy for $X and resell for a higher amount?

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

​
This week's flip is EarlyImpactLearning.com, a website listed for $201,700.

​​​

​Link to Listing​

This website makes a bit more money than the ones I usually cover in this newsletter. It's currently profiting $6,135 per month, which means it's selling for 32.8x monthly profit. Typically, I'd expect to see a 40x multiple, so in the regard you could say the site is "cheap".

Another note: This is a Dutch Auction, so the price will continue to drop until someone purchases the website.

With a site of this size and revenue, It's more interesting as part of a larger portfolio than just a flip.

The site is already being monetized in several ways, from Ezoic display ads to courses and books sold via WooCommerce. So unlike many other flips I cover, there's no easy "add ons" you can quickly use to boost revenue.

The site already has some strong SEO, including 173 articles and a 25 Domain Authority. And check out the traffic:

From the listing, here are some other assets the site comes with:

"Site comes with an email list of around 12,000 subscribers. Comes with a Youtube channel with 2,500 subscribers. Comes with a Facebook page with 6,500 likes. Comes with an Instagram account with 2,300 followers"

In many ways, this website is already an established brand with several marketing channels, unlike most of the websites I usually cover.

But, there are definitely areas that can be improved.

From the listing, here are three ideas the seller identifies for growth:

1) Affiliate – the site currently has zero affiliate marketing on it, and so this is very much an untapped area. Affiliate offers could be placed on high trafficked blogs, you could write reviews of relevant gear, or affiliate offers sent out to the email list (or all three)
​
2) Growing traffic through writing more content based on what has worked so far. I have one writer currently, but I believe many more could be found through recruiting from my email list.
​
3) Creating funnels that link the blog to the info products. Most info product sales currently come very simply through a weekly email. Some come from a few simple links in the blogs. But more active linking of the blog to info products or funnels to sell relevant info products has always been high on my to-do list but not happened yet.

I think the email list of 12,000 can be monetized much better. From the listing, they don't break out revenue from the email list.

In this niche, I think the email list should be monetized at a rate of $0.25 per email per month. My first goal after buying this website would be to make that happen. If you could get the email list to that level of revenue, it would be worth $3,000 per month.

I'd implement this by sending offers monthly to the email list and increasing the emails to 2x a week instead of 1. This could mean running a sale on one of the website's most popular books for email subscribers only - or even just selling sponsorship space to advertisers.

Let's also not forget that we should expect to keep adding subscribers! I'd add in a pop-up lead magnet offering a free resource for users that input their email, as well as implement some lead forms through the right articles.

If done well you could hope to convert traffic at 2%. At 50,000 unique users per month, we should expect about 1,000 new email subscribers per month. Let's assume some will unsubscribe, so we'll call it a net of 900 new subscribers per month.

Let's say you bought this website and held it for one year. Here's what you the financials would look like if all you did was focus on the email newsletter:

  • $6,135 in monthly revenue from the website, unchanged from Month 1 to Month 12
  • 22,800 email subscribers by Month 12 = $5,700 in monthly revenue
  • New Total = $11,835 in monthly revenue

Using a 40x multiple, the website would be worth about $473,300 - more than double what you paid for it. In fact, that would be a 135% return, not even factoring in the revenue you would have pocketed throughout the year.

This just goes to show how powerful email lists can be. Having an email list means you own the customer relationship. You can reach out at anytime instead of waiting for them to remember you and visit your website again.

There are also some really really interesting opportunities to build a community here around the website.

As always this is just one hypothetical scenario of what could happen. Make sure to do your own due diligence and only buy something you know works for you with your skillset!

​

Builders Build

This week on Builders Build, we talked with Nicholas Brown, Head of North American Acquisitions at Dragonflip. Nicholas is a Sweden-based business broker who’s been working on complex mergers and acquisitions worldwide at multiple companies.

On this episode we talk about:

– Best and worst spaces to build for acquisition

– How to prepare to sell your business

– Tips for evaluating your business

– How to calculate a ballpark figure for your business

– What information you should have on hand before starting the selling process

– What categories are hot right now and where ecommerce is headed

– And so much more.

emails.subject: 💸 $21K ➡️ $37K with a Graphics Card Site?
emails.content:
Nano Thought

I often think about business models and run scenarios in my head about which are the best and worst types of businesses to run.

In the hundreds of hours I've spent thinking about this, I still haven't come up with a better business model than owning content sites.

While I think "passive income" is way more rare than most gurus make it out to be, owning content sites is about as close as you can get to passive income without having millions of dollars to invest in stocks or real estate funds.

​

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
I love owning content sites because there is no customer to deal with Your ad space is sold automatically and you are paid automatically
July 25th 2022
2
Retweets
127
Likes

No customers to deal with, you probably don't need employees, and you don't have to worry about shipping out products yourself.

You can put out some content and change up the website, then sit back for a few weeks and let the site do its thing.

But there are also big opportunities in this space. If you want, you can dig in and build a huge, scalable business. You can accomplish just about anything you want with content sites!

People always ask how big of a business could this be? Answer is it can be small, like a semi passive $20/month side hustle, all the way up to huge, multi-million dollar ventures that get acquired by private equity firms.

Or here is an example of right in the middle:

Mike (Niche Twins) ✍🏼
@NicheDown
I just stumbled upon this branded portfolio of sites started by an 18 year old (now 25 running his business from Bali). He's easily making well over $100,000 every month, and probably has been for years... pic.twitter.com/qRJmU25FRG
July 26th 2022
14
Retweets
117
Likes

My favorite businesses will always be online ones like websites and newsletters. You can run them from anywhere, upfront costs can be low, they're infinitely scalable, and there are thousands of niches to build in.

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

​

Check out this website for sale on Flippa. It's a content site in the graphics card niche that did about $600 in revenue last month with over 12,000 monthly pageviews. Let's dive in:

​
Right off the bat, I like the backlink profile I'm seeing in Ahrefs:

​

​

One downside of this website is its age. Newer sites are obviously less proven, so it's harder to know if the traffic is a fluke or if it's repeatable over the long-term. However, that backlink profile looks great for such a young site.

I'd say this is a healthy site that's growing pretty well.

It's also in a great niche. The microchip industry is growing and becoming more important to everyday life, from connected 'smart' devices to the growing ubiquity of phones and computers. While the site is currently positioned within a subset of the microchip industry, it will clearly benefit from these macro trends.

We've also seen chips in the news lately, with the Senate working on a $280 billion subsidy. Computer components is obviously a great area to be in.

One thing that's important to note is you should understand this space if you're going to run this website. It can be a complicated niche, so probably best for someone who already has an interest in this stuff. I would say that goes for most niches, but especially this one since it's so complicated.

It would also be important to stay up-to-date on new technology if you're running this site.

Let's analyze this website for a potential flip. As you probably know by now, there are tons of ops to buy and hold... BUT you can get some real gains by improving and flipping.

So before buying a site, ask yourself, "what can I do to increase the traffic or revenue?"

You know your own skills best, so you'll have to answer that question for yourself with each deal you analyze. I typically use a 12 month time horizon for analyzing a deal.

If I wanted to flip this website, here are the changes I'd implement:

  • Add Ezoic display ads. This could add roughly $200/month in revenue or more
  • Sell 2 sponsored posts per month @ $100 each

For this example, let's say that both of these changes can be implemented and realized in the first month.

In addition to those two changes, I'd of course keep producing content, building backlinks etc.

Since this site is growing so fast, I think the multiple on the sale will be high. The revenue listed on Flippa is $304/month, but that's the average over the last 12 months. The site has been in the $600 to $800 range over the last few months.

When a site is growing this quickly, it might be easier to value it based on a multiple of trailing 6 months revenue, as opposed to just 1 month like I often do.

Over the last 6 months, this site did $3,218 in revenue (an average of $536.33 per month).

If we use a 40x multiple on that average monthly revenue, we get a selling price of $21,453. That seems about right considering how the bidding has gone so far on Flippa.

Let's break down the math:

  • Buy the site for $21,453
  • Increase revenue from $536/mo to $936/mo with the changes outlined above
  • Collect $11,232 in revenue during Year 1 of holding the website
  • Website is now worth $37,440 after Year 1

So after 1 year, without assuming any increase in traffic, we can add about 75% in value to the asset, plus collect all that cash flow.

Let's say that we sell after 1 year. Our net return on the sale would be $15,987 (Sale - Initial Purchase), plus we collected $11,232 in cash flow throughout year 1.

That's a $27,219 return on our initial $21,453 purchase plus our time. That's a 127% return!

emails.subject: 💸 Start Your Online Empire with a $1k Site
emails.content:
Nano Thought

If you're building businesses, you're better off building in niches that will continue to grow. You'll benefit from tailwinds and make more money. The future is definitely SaaS, newsletters, and websites. More and more of our lives are moving online, so internet businesses are a great place to be for the next decade (and beyond).

I also love running online businesses because you can have a completely remote team that works from anywhere. Margins can also be great with little or no overhead or crazy capital expenditures.

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Pieter Levels started 9 companies making $2,700,000 per year with 0 employees and 0 funding. Here’s his 7 step playbook to build a million dollar company from scratch: pic.twitter.com/Z58ZdGwRoO
July 29th 2022
121
Retweets
726
Likes

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

I'm going to cover a ​type of website I usually don't write about in this newsletter: A starter site.

A starter site is a website that's built out and ready to go, but has very little revenue ($14 in July). Basically, you're paying for the development/design work that's already been done.

When buying a site with such low revenue, you don't just value the site multiple of cash flow. Instead, I'd look at "replacement cost". How much would it cost you to hire someone to build a similar site from scratch? You could also add in some time value premium of buying the existing site, since creating a new website would obviously take more time than just buying the existing site.

​

​Link to Listing​

If you are looking to get your start in online businesses and don't mind getting your hands dirty, there are plenty of opportunities like this.

The first thing that I would do if I bought this site: Update the existing content and add a lot more.

Currently, the copy on the website doesn't make a whole lot of sense. You could quickly clean it up so that the value proposition is much clearer to visitors when they land on the site.

SEO-wise, the work has only just been starting. The current owner has 37 articles up but hasn't seen many results. The DA is 8 and there are 0 first-page rankings.

With a few hours of content creation, I think I could make huge leaps in the SEO of this site.

Another change I'd make: Fix the affiliate links.

Some of the affiliate links on the website are broken. Fixing those up would be a quick way to create some value and increase revenue.

Here is a summary of my hypothetical plan for buying and fixing this site:

  • Fix existing copy on the site so it makes sense
  • Create new blog articles and publish 2 per week
  • Build links with high DA sites in the same niche
  • Fix affiliate links
  • Check other affiliate programs to see if there are more lucrative options
  • Sell sponsored posts
  • Start collecting email addresses for a newsletter

This type of site can be a good opportunity to learn the ropes and experiment. Not high-risk since it's a low price and there's little revenue. In other words, the only way you can go is up with a site like this!

​

​

We cover everything from niche content websites to social media profiles to newsletters to SaaS’ to domains. (As well as a litany of other things we love in the digital asset space).

emails.subject: 💸 Anyone can make $3084 a month with an automative website
emails.content:
Nano Thought

Whats up gang! Last week was chaos so sadly. We missed a newsletter, but don't worry! We are back in action.

Everyone has heard of a roll up right? All the big private equity shops you know are doing it. Its an amazing way to make 1+1=3

Sometimes you can pull it off with small online businesses as well. It might be that you find several small sites, 301 redirect them to a bigger authority site, and consolidate the content in one space.

Or maybe you're buying 3 ecommerce brands that each pay media buyers $5k a month. Now you're saving $10k by having that media buyer work in house for you running ads for all the brands. Boom!

Point is! Roll ups and lowering expenses through acquisition doesn't just need to be for the big multi billion dollar PE firms. We can all do it as well. Check out a recent thread I did on the topic.

​

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
A roll-up can help you build an empire. But what exactly is a roll-up strategy? Let me explain:
August 12th 2022
23
Retweets
185
Likes

​

{{ snippet.cksn-morning-brew-8-17-22 }}

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

Not too many affordable easy flips on my radar this week guys. So why not take a shot a looking at a bigger site with some long term growth opportunities!

Dont forget, everything doesn't need to be a quick flip. Sometimes buying a cash flowing online business that isn't a full time job is just as big of a win as an easy flip. Anyone can buy an online business that brings them 30%+ cash on cash return. Beat that S&P 500!

This week we are looking at a site in the Automotive Space, for sale on Investors Club

​

​

​Link to Listing​

Right off the bat, the site is for sale for 35x~ its monthly net revenue. Sounds pretty fair with all things considered. Lets take a quick look at the site in Ahrefs..

The site is ranking for a TON of keywords! This is awesome. If you were to buy it I would look into adding some strong backlinks throughout it. The overall DR is pretty low considering the sites size. You would want to build more of a moat around your rankings by creating a stronger backlink profile. And DEF make more content that is focused on converting affiliate offers. Everything on the site is essentially focused on informational content, that is monetized with display ads...this is the opportunity.

Change You could Make #1: Work on increasing authority with backlinks

One of the great things about this site? Traffic is CRANKING! Its surviving all the google updates left and right. This is a great sign to me that google LOVEs the site. Work on getting some guest posts and niche edits for the site!

Change You could Make #2: Build content that is focused on affiliate revenue

The clear major win here would be to keep building out content, but make it relevant to affiliate offers!

Have no idea where to find the right affiliate offers? Well here is a good list of some :)

Here is a summary of a hypothetical plan for buying and improving this site:

  • Clean up site design to give it a more cohesive aesthetic
  • Find 52 keywords that are below a difficulty of 10 and above 100 in search volume with ahrefs​
  • Plan out 1 article a week for the next year
  • Insert affiliate links into the articles

This site would be a great buy, grow, and hold. And if you want to flip it? Go for it.

The broker thinks this sites earnings potential is $4k a month. I actually think its higher than that with some quick keyword research I did. But let's assume you get it up to $4k in 12 months. This is with you writing 1 article a week (or outsourcing it) and having a small backlinking strategy in place.

Ok so just for fun lets assume you don't get it to earn $4k a month until 12 months in, and you work 3-4 hours a week on content and link building...surely you could find 3-4 hours a week.

In the first 12 months you make $37,008

In the next 12 months you make $48,000

After 24 months you have earned $85,008 AND you have a site now worth $140,000

If you sold the site you would have $225,008 from a $115k investment - NOT BAD

Of course you could just keep it, and keep growing it :)

This is of course one of many hypothetical scenarios. You need to do your own due diligence and make sure this would be the right site for you and your portfolio.

​

emails.subject: 💸 Could you make $6-10k a month from this wedding site?
emails.content:
Nano Thought

Everyone has been freaking out about Google algorithm updates recently. I get it, it's scary. This is why as soon as you get a site to be big enough, you should be trying to get it less and less dependent on a single channel. Ive had many sites hurt by Google updates, but MANY do better because of them!

When someone loses rankings, someone else gains rankings. It's really that simple.

Try and make sure your sites are ranking for many keywords not just a few, and are getting traffic from many sources, not just Google. We want traffic from FB groups, forums, other sites, Bing, your email list, and social media profiles...IE find what channels work for your niche and site, and build.

For many of you, that might even be paid traffic!

Before you go freak out about upcoming updates, check out this thread my friend BowTiedWookie from twitter wrote below:

​

BowTiedWookie
@BowTiedWookie
Google’s Helpful Content Update rolls out today. A quick summary of what the update is, sites that will likely be impacted, and what you should do going forward 👇🧵
August 22nd 2022
3
Retweets
7
Likes

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

With some recent Google updates, Im being a little more careful about content sites that get all their traffic from Google. So instead of just finding any old flip opportunity. So let's take a second to look at a site that isn't just a content site, but has an opportunity to make money with a little work from a different angle.

This is a 9 year old, online LGBT Wedding directory, monetized by ad space, and selling listings.

​

​

Check the listing here​

This isn't the best site for passive income but if you are willing to put in the work of some cold outreach? It could be a total cash cow. AND NOT ALL GREAT ONLINE BUSINESSES ARE SITES THAT MAKE MONEY FROM AFFILIATE OFFERS AND DISPLAY ADS!

Listings on Pridezillas.com are $200 per year for featured listings and $100 per year for basic listings.

They also have monetized the blog and depending on the product each blog listing sells for $80-500 per blog post.

You could buy this site, get Linkedin Sales Navigator, and find business that want to list on the site. Just by setting up a simple search for "wedding planners" or any other vendor like wedding photographers, DJ's, wedding venues, officiants, florists and more and then picking the job titles of "manager" or "owner".

​

From there, set up a simple outreach plan.

50 DMs a day to these business owners and managers, and one would easily be able to sell $6k a month in directory listings and blog posts. Make nice little ad rate card that explains what the buyers get, and make your 10x easier. The current owner thinks you could get it up to $10k but let's be conservative.

Not passive...but you could probably outsource for $2k a month and pocket the other $4k!

This would make the site worth an easy $144,000 if we assume a 36x multiple on the monthly net revenue.

You could honestly just build this business from scratch yourself

Of course this is just one hypothetical scenario. Do your own due diligence! I just wanted to show you all a different business model!

​

Purchased for a little over $400 (lets round up and pretend $500) and was making $7-8 a month.

Some small improvements and it was up to $20-30 a month and I sold it for $1200.

In less than 1 minute after putting it for sale it sold!

To go along with that I am purchasing another off market deal, cant wait to get started:

​

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Just agreed to terms to purchase a new website! - sports niche - $10.5k purchase price - $300+ in monthly revenue - ready for improvements - bought from someone who bought my course! Can’t wait to get started. Thread to come on the plan!
September 1st 2022
7

​

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

This week we have a super interesting site that has a SUPER clear path to big revenue improvements in my mind. Very curious if others see this the same way I do! Its a content site about getting rid of pests (rats, roaches, etc)

​

Check the listing here​

Ok so right off the bat, the things we DONT like about this site.

  • traffic has been very up and down over last 12 months
  • referring pages dropped off a cliff last year

Even though the referring pages dropped, the referring domains didn't much. This makes me think maybe there was a forum that linked on every forum post/page to the site, and that it was removed. TBH this isn't the end of the world to me. Seems like things have really stabilized.

And overall other than that, it has a decently strong backlink profile in Ahrefs

​

Ok! So this site is a content website that generates revenue through display ads and affiliate income. Revenue is mostly coming from Mediavine and Amazon associates.

The seller has done a decent job monetizing it, but they are leaving serious dollars on the table.

They should be selling leads...

A quick google search for "sell pest control leads" will show you that pest control companies will pay between $35-105 for each phone call they get about pest control thats qualified.

Dont believe me? Check this out​

  • Create a phone number with Call Fire (this will allow you set up call tracking and forward live calls to lead buyers)

Ok! So this site is a content website that generates revenue through display ads and affiliate income. Currently we are seeing most the revenue come from Adthrive display ads and Amazon Associates affiliate revenue.

In general, the seller has done a great job monetizing. The listing even says they build sites and sell them all the time, so no surprise they did this one right as well.

BUT, there are opportunities to increase affiliate income by exploring more sub niches such as Koren beauty, nail, microcurrent and anti-aging etc.

The site is getting 1700 unique visitors a day...they could be getting 20+ sign ups a day. The truth is? Its because their lead magnet/optin is terrible.

​

Test different things to offer people for signing up. A 1% optin/sign up rate is 100000% doable. If you can make that happen, this sites value changes very quickly.

Try offering them discounts on products through a deal you cut with an affiliate program, or something...non foot related ha.

(This is based on it profiting $1500 a month for 12 months and selling for a standard 36x monthly net profit multiple)

Lets say you held onto the site 2 years, and you started monetizing the email list from months 12-24. Lets also assume it never grew past 5k subs...

The site would be worth $99,000 and over the 2 years you would hav made $51,000. Add those and then subtract the cost of the site...it one might hypothetically make $108,000. Not bad for a couple hours of work a week!

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

But this is still true if you're running paid ads, or email campaigns, or organic social. At the core of them all..is content.

At Nano Flips we rotate through in house writers, sometimes I write content for sites myself, and some great contractors we have worked with for years.

But it dawned on me.

Many of you out there have NO idea where to get great content. So Ive decided to put together a great list of contractors and agencies that Ive tested myself.

We will start with SEO friendly content for niche websites (the most common kind of online business we talk about here in the newsletter).

I posted on Twitter about ordering a 10k word test from a new content agency for one of my niche blogs about sports I just bought.

When i posted about it tons of agencies reached out, so looks like I'll have a few extra to vet for you all!

Nano Flips Special Offer

{{ snippet.sept-21-2022-oct-9-2022-cksn-vinovest-sponsorship }}

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

I know half of you want sites under $50k, and the other half looking to deploy $50k! So for today, I want to take a look at a great site from Empire Flippers. Its in the food and beverage niche. I cant share the URL, but just go ahead and check out the listing and see the URL for yourself here.​

Not every site is a quick flip, but this could be great buy, hold and grow.

​

Ok so right off the bat, the things we DONT like about this site.

  • Traffic is a little bit on the decline
  • revenue is a little on the decline

With that said....overall its trending very much up! And its in a super evergreen niche something I love.

Overall, it has a decently strong backlink profile in Ahrefs

​

The site makes its money from Amazon Associates (48.69%), display advertising (48.02%), and affiliate (3.29%).

Traffic comes primarily from organic search (94.91%), direct (4.41%), and referral (0.47%). The top three countries driving traffic are the US (77.22%), Canada (5.91%), and the UK (3.94%). The top three pages make up 38.15% of total site traffic, contributing to 22.02%, 11.67%, and 4.46% of traffic respectively.

THESE ARE GOOD THINGS!

The sad part is, its probably had its revenue maximized already. But we can def increase traffic! (Which will increase revenue ha)

If I were to buy this site here is what I would do:

  • Find competitors with weaker backlink profiles and lower DR than me. I would use Ahrefs to see whatever pages they were ranking for that were super low competition, and then I would make content for those keywords. Since this site has a much strong backlink profile, you would be likely to rank within a couple months for bunch of that new content if things went right.

​

  • Figure out what keywords have high traffic and are on page 2! With a few backlinks we could bring lots of those pages to page 1 and increase traffic drastically. The amount of traffic a site gets being on page 2 for a keyword is NOTHING in comparison to what it can get when it hits page one. Guess what...I did some digging for you. There are almost 400 keywords that are in this situation for this website.

Nano Flips Special Offer

{{ snippet.sept-21-2022-oct-9-2022-cksn-vinovest-sponsorship }}

This Week’s Nano Flip Opportunity

We found a site over on Motion Invest to highlight this week. Its a website about Off Roading! This could be a perfect site for someone who loves off roading, and could even work if you don't. Here is the listing.

​

​

Ok so right off the bat, the things we DONT like about this site.

  • UR rating of 2 and DR rating of 1 according to Ahrefs
  • Since it ranks so many keywords with no authority, it would be easy for a competitor to outrank the pages
  • Traffic and top 10 keywords (according to Ahrefs) dropped in September 2022
  • Site is pretty new

Ok now that we got that out of the way, let's look at some of the good things. First off traffic has been growing overall this whole year (small drop in sept to be aware of that will likely reflect in oct as well), and considering this year had some of the strongest Google algorithm updates Ive seen in a long time, that says a lot!

​

The site is also in a nice broad niche, that has a passionate group of hobbyists in it.

This means there is like TONS of content to create, an opportunity to build a community or newsletter, and it shouldn't be impossible to find someone to outsource great content to in the future if you don't want to write it yourself!

Some other highlights:

➔ There are 48 pages that have Amazon products being linked to and no have the proper Amazon Affiliate Disclaimers in place.

➔ There are 159 Amazon links being used and of those 12 links are missing an affiliate tag.

➔ The site links to 139 different Amazon products and of those 13 products are out of stock, meaning people who click on those links can’t actually purchase the product. Swapping those products with different products that are in stock can help to increase income.

The traffic is also nice and spread out among the articles. No page is getting more than 5% of the total traffic to the site.

THIS MEANS THERE IS AN OPPORTUNITY TO MAKE MORE MONEY FROM THE SITE! NEW OWNER COULD FIX THOSE LINKS!

If one were to buy this site here is what they would do:

​

  • BUILD SOME BACKLINKS! The site is doing great, but it has no authority. I would want to do a backlink gap analysis to see where my competitors had great links from, and start building some links to protect the sites rankings.

​

  • Build a community or newsletter! You could do both but let's assume you build a newsletter. The site is getting 50k+ uniques a month. Lets assume we could capture 1-2% of those people into a newsletter about Off Roading. Thats 1k new subscribers a month! We can monetize this don't forget :)

​

  • Figure out what keywords have high traffic and are on page 2! With a few backlinks we could bring lots of those pages to page 1 and increase traffic drastically. The amount of traffic a site gets being on page 2 for a keyword is NOTHING in comparison to what it can get when it hits page one.

​

  • Start finding niche communities where you can share great content from the site. Just from looking at FB Groups and Reddit, Ive managed to find 100k or so new potential readers. I would also use these communities to find people that want to write for the site. Many Im sure would love to write for free!

​

​

  • Last on my list would be to get the site redesigned and pulled together to feel more like a cohesive brand. This will help in selling sponsorships and in building a newsletter/community. (last my list and BE CAREFUL NOT TO MESS WITH SEO)

​

The website is making $2,004 per month and is selling for 33x its average monthly profit at $66k~

Without using leverage or making changes, if the site stays strong it will bring in roughly 30% cash on cash returns, not too bad for a business that can be a passion project.

But lets assume you make some changes! At 2% growth of the email list, thats 12k new subs a year. Let's say 10k to compensate for some churn from unsubscribes.

To be conservative, lets also assume we don't monetize the email list for 12 months AND that it doesn't grow after 12 months (obviously it would)

If each sub earns us .25 per month, that means year 2 the list makes us $30k in revenue, and on massive 95%+ margins.

Maybe we have to spend $500 a month on content and backlinks to maintain rankings and build a moat (this would also make the site grow...as well as revenue. But for the sake of being conservative we will pretend this just maintains traffic)

Year 1 the site could earn $24,048 and cost $6k to run leaving the new owner with $18K~ net profit

Year 2 the site could makes $54,048 ($2004 a month site revenue + $2500 month email list revenue) and cost $6k to run leaving the new owner with $48k~ in net profit

Its new revenue puts the sites valuation at roughly $144k~ based on 35x monthly net revenue if you sold it

Which all ads up to mean that if this worked out over the next 24 months the new owner could make $210k gross or $144k net profit for a couple hours of work a week (the biz cost $66k to buy don;t forget). OR they could of course keep it and make $4k a month semi passively.

Thats a 218.18% ROI on a $66k investment

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

emails.subject: max pain ahead
emails.content:
It’s James.

Months ago I wrote about the coming crash.

“CHILL JAMES IT’S GONNA BE FINE!!”

12 months ago Twitter said Bitcoin was a hedge against inflation.

Now even 6 figure earners shop at dollar stores.

“More young, middle-class Americans flock to dollar stores, seeking a refuge from record-high inflation“ — MarketWatch

Literally.

So here’s what’s gonna happen:

We’re on the verge of a real recession.

Rent, gas and food prices are through the roof.

Stocks and crypto are down 80%+.

The Real Estate bubble is bursting.

“With 7% Mortgage Rates, It's Game Over For The Housing Bubble“ — SeekingAlpha, Oct 7th, 2022

It’s not “just another bear market”.

Basically:

Living just got 50% more expensive.

And our stocks, crypto and real estate are at risk.

So naturally…

Most people are still in a state of disbelief.

They’re waiting for stuff to bounce back up.

For their rent prices to drop.

If this is you?

STOP

Do not waste your precious energy.

Much better to play offense.

My buddy Aaron reached out the other day and he was asking me how I’m dealing with the situation….

Now Aaron has a career and he was concerned about his mortgage rising and potential Tech layoffs.

Dave Ramsey would tell you to budget your way out of it.
​

“It’s TrAnSiToRy!!!!”

Screw that.

I’m not waiting for the markets to bounce.

I’m not waiting for anyone to save me.

I’m focused on controlling my income.

I mean why do we work anyway?

Your work should serve your lifestyle.

Now personally, I’m a fan of businesses that don’t require tons of active time.

I want to put in X hours and own an asset that pays me every single month.

(Unlike service businesses and careers which are full-time jobs)

So I showed Aaron how I’m managing my own digital real estate

Within a weeks he took over a digital asset and started cash-flowing ~450/mo

Not bad. But it gets better.

With a few tweaks … In 6-12 months he may be able to get that monthly income to 2K-5K/mo (or more).

A chunky consistent income stream for a couple hours of work a week. With no bosses or clients.

Point is?

Playing defense is putting you and your family at risk.

emails.subject: 💸 If I was starting over, I would do this instead
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}, James here

I got over 100 DMs asking me a variation of:

“How would you build a fulltime income online from scratch in 12 months?”

And honestly?

​

I wouldn’t.

​

Let me explain:

When most people think of stacking incomes… these are the usual strategies

​

By putting in more time and energy…

They either push harder on their career / service business (and now have 10 bosses to answer to)

By waiting…

They may even sit on cash waiting for the perfect time to buy real estate or dividend stocks.

By strictly gambling…

They may (god forbid) gamble on NFT projects hoping to get rich (and find out ETH prices have crashed 70%+)

Or, by building from scratch…

They spend months and months trying to build a business from scratch. Looking for product market fit.

​

Here’s the deal.

With inflation going crazy and the markets tanking?

We can’t afford to waste time.

​

In my mid 20’s I did run an agency.

That was my career.

So my partner and I worked hard around the clock for years.

And it’s only when we started growing an online newsletter asset…

… that we were able to sell the company for 8 figures in 3 years.

​

But then in 2021 I tried something different.

Bought a “digital property”. Grew it for 12 months. Sold it for $774K in cash.

​

I didn’t need to wait.

Or gamble on speculative investments.

Or refresh ETH prices 5 times a day.

Or spend years building something from scratch.

And certainly didn’t put in more energy managing bosses or clients.

All I needed was to find an EXISTING cash flowing business. And take over it.

​

So now…

When I want to grow another income stream here’s what I do:

#1 — Find an online asset that’s ALREADY CASH FLOWING that I can CONTROL

(I hate depending on markets or people for my income)

#2 — That’s SEPARATE FROM MY TIME AND ENERGY and can be run remotely

(I’m a lazy investor! haha)

#3 — Where I can BUY LOW with little upfront capital

(I’m not a risk taker! I like assets where I can screw up so badly and still win big)

#4 — Where there’s a CLEAR PATH to SCALING CASHFLOW in 6-12 months.

Full control.

Exit potential.

Instant cashflow.

Minimal investment.

Clear path to 2x cash flow in a few months.

My kinda asset!

​

Now look

Even though I could easily ask for $5,000 or even $10,000 to help a

small group of investors build their Digital Real Estate portfolios

Because there’s a chance of recouping the investment so quickly…

… i’m not gonna do that simply because my goal isn’t to get rich off of info products

I’m a full time digital real estate investor.

And my goal here is to help others acquire their
​
own digital real estate “freedom portfolio”.

Are you in?

​

To “monthly paychecks” with no bosses,

James

P.S. If you don’t wanna own a cash-flowing online business?

​Opt-out, and I won’t message you about it.

emails.subject: Why I’m not charging $8,000 for the Digital Real Estate Program
emails.content:
I have an ulterior motive…

It’s James.

Over the past few days I’ve received tons of emails and DMs from future digital real estate investors…

LOTS of good energy.

Because the way the world is changing and could accelerate DRAMATICALLY at any moment.

And right now?

Those who are killing it are focused on stacking cash flow.

And I’ve been quietly building out a playbook.

A playbook anyone can follow.

So this is where YOU come into play.

Because what I’m about to drop?

It gives you an unfair advantage… even if you’re new-ish to online biz.

If you’re one of a limited number of people on this list who secures a slot in my LIVE program…

And you’re prepared to spend a few hours quietly building?

I’m honestly pumped for you.

Lives are gonna change.

Seriously…

Now 12 months ago I first unlocked my Digital Real Estate Mentorship program.

And what happened next was amazing.

Case studies were created every single week.

Deals were closed LIVE on the calls.

Partnerships formed.

And in just one cohort we’ve had over $1.25M worth of deals!

Then I realized…

Intimate mentoring is a lot of work.

That’s why I’m moving away from it in the coming months so I can focus on my own digital real estate projects and podcast.

But before I do?

I’m opening up one (possibly final) intimate cohort.

Folks in just one of the cohorts I coached have closed over 25 cash-flowing acquisitions within 8 weeks.

So being ahead of the curve on this one is a superpower.

Now, when it comes to SPEED and HOW QUICKLY you can build recurring income…

I don’t see ANY other model that compares to digital real estate.

I know because I’ve been doing this a long time.

And honestly?

A couple of times I’ve had to check myself for being JEALOUS of the people I’m putting this in front of.

But SCREW THAT ENERGY!

Now listen...

My goal is to start working with you on the Nano Flips Digital Real Estate Mentorship Program very soon.

And given how ripe the market is and the obvious demand in my inbox…

I could easily peg an $8,000 or even $10,000 price tag on this and work with a much smaller group of people.

But the reason I started mentoring?

Was because I wanted to create an inner circle of asset owners.

And the more people I can help become Digital Real Estate Investors?

The more opportunities we’ll have together.

I’m talking

Cross selling between our assets to increase cash flow.

Merging assets to multiply valuation.

Securing bigger exits.

And so much more.

Now, obviously there are certain limitations…

BUT here’s one thing I want to make clear:

I absolutely DO NOT want you jumping on this if money is your only priority.

I’m dead serious.

This is an investment for diligent and ethical people.

And in my experience, the best students are motivated by:

  • Building a real business
  • Optimizing systems and processes
  • Curiosity and a willingness to learn new things

I only want to accept people who are capable of following instructions.

So even though the investment won’t be anything near $8,000...

If you have the desire, the discipline and the high standards necessary?

Then we're going to make lots of recurring income together.

Does that sound like a deal?
