emails.content:
Nano Thought

Back to our regularly scheduled program of tips, tricks, and online businesses for sale direct to your inbox weekly!

I wanted to take a second to remind everyone, that you don't just have to own 1 website, you can build a portfolio of them. Just START with one.

Here is a tweet from my friend Paul about a new portfolio of sites he is building.

Paul Lemley
@PALemley
Here's more evidence for niche site operators that a multi-site portfolio is better than a single site... pic.twitter.com/Hg9feP0DLM
October 31st 2022
13
Retweets
134
Likes

Worth noting something here. See how the majority of the sites aren't hitting? This is one of the reasons I like buying! When you buy a website/online business that already makes money, you're paying for the cashflow AND the product market fit. The PMF if you will.

You are basically guaranteeing you get a site thats on the right side of that chart, as opposed to one on the left side that isnt getting much traffic.

​

Nano Flips Special Offer

{{ snippet.sept-21-2022-oct-9-2022-cksn-vinovest-sponsorship }}

This Week’s Opportunity

This week we found a pretty nice little content site over on Flippa. Some of you will hate it. Others will see an opp. This newsletter is here to show you all kinds of deals. Im going to start spending more time highlighting sites with pros AND cons. And talk about sides of both.

(The site Im really excited about is in the next section)

​

Ok so right off the bat, the things we DONT like about this site.

  • It has almost no authority, tons of the keywords could be taken over by competitors if the site doesnt getter backlink profile
  • Very new website
  • Seller BIN is overpriced
  • Content is poorly written

Ok, so we have covered that! Now lets look at the site

​

Ok so first off, I would do a light rebrand here. Its too simple. We also would want to get some backlinks built to this site ASAP. The fact that it ranks for so many keywords without any authority, means a stronger competitor could take over its rankings.

BUT

This also makes me think this niche has TONS of opportunities like the ones it is ranking for already.

I went into Ahrefs, and did a quick analysis of its competitors. There are several that are just as weak in terms of authority, and ranking for WAY more keywords.

For some this could be a turn off. For others? I see an opp to beat the competitors, and start building great backlinks ASAP, to hold onto the rankings it already has.

Some notes to consider:

➔ The site is already monetized with ezoic AND amazon

➔ The content is poorly written, I would go in and clean it up ASAP.

➔ Would look into installing Lasso, and using different affiliate programs for monetization like home depot, lowes, etc.

​

If one were to buy this site here is what they would do:

​

  • BUILD SOME BACKLINKS! The site is doing great, but it has no authority. I would want to do a backlink gap analysis to see where my competitors had great links from, and start building some links to protect the sites rankings.

​

  • CLEAN UP THE CONTENT. It was clearly written by someone who isnt great at English. I would suggest the buyer be either an actual user of these tools, or know writers who are.

​

  • Figure out what keywords have high traffic and are on page 2! With a few backlinks we could bring lots of those pages to page 1 and increase traffic drastically. The amount of traffic a site gets being on page 2 for a keyword is NOTHING in comparison to what it can get when it hits page one.

​

Last on my list would be to get the site redesigned and pulled together to feel more like a cohesive brand. Would consider switching to Astra or Generate press for the sites theme.

The website is making $USD $133 /mo per month average over the last year and is currently bid at $1k or so currently, with a buy it now set at $11k.

The last couple months, the site has done amazingly though. Considering the recent google updates, and ranking changes the last 2 months Im both surprised and impressed its survived and continued to grow!

Last month it did a little over $300 in profit....which is why the seller thinks its worth $11k.

Its not in my opinion

I would think that more like $6-8k was the range this site should go for. Considering it has no moat and will need work quickly to keep it where it's at and grow.

I wanted to highlight this site to show you, that for the right person with the right plan, it could be a win.

But for the wrong person it could be a disaster. These are online businesses, you should have an idea of how to run them or fix them if you plan on buying them.

OR maybe you saw this listing and thought "that sites garbage...but I can beat it"

A lesson here either way.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​

Off Market Special

Ok guys, I want to take a moment to highlight a site for sale from a friend of mine...BowTiedWookie. He's a killer, was one of the first people to join our site flipping program, and now I always ask him to come and teach lessons to people in our program.

He is selling this site, dont want to miss out on this one:

4 year old website in health niche stated to be making $2,300/m in revenue L3M being sold by BowTiedWookie (a great Substack btw).

​

Seller says:

  • Revenue currently 38% affiliate, 24% direct ads partnership, 22% Amazon Associates, 13% digital product, 3% KDP.
  • Site was created in 2018, aged domain added in summer 2021, we bought it in October 2021 from private Twitter sale.
  • Went from 68 -> 228 published posts
  • The site has gotten a boost in the last 5 consecutive core algo updates but there is always risk when you rely on one traffic source
  • 15 posts currently ordered from writers (free with the purchase of site)
  • 3 HARO links currently ordered from the Agency (free with the purchase of site)
  • Mediavine launched in mid-October (site was ad-free before this)
  • Had almost 3K subs but recently cut the list to ~750 - our emails are not great, huge opportunity for someone who understands email
  • There are a lot of small DTC companies in this niche. We started renting our Facebook pixel out to one of them this month as a test. If we held onto the site we’d hire a VA to DM every single DTC company in the space and try to rent the pixel to them

I trust this guy, he has been through our program, and has built something great.

Hit him up if your interested on Twitter here​

​
​Builders Build

As always here is a little plug for my podcast.

Nano Thought

Back to our regularly scheduled program of tips, tricks, and online businesses for sale direct to your inbox weekly!

I wanted to take a second to remind everyone, that you don't just have to own 1 website, you can build a portfolio of them. Just START with one.

Here is a tweet from my friend Paul about a new portfolio of sites he is building.

Paul Lemley
@PALemley
Here's more evidence for niche site operators that a multi-site portfolio is better than a single site... pic.twitter.com/Hg9feP0DLM
October 31st 2022
13
Retweets
134
Likes

Worth noting something here. See how the majority of the sites aren't hitting? This is one of the reasons I like buying! When you buy a website/online business that already makes money, you're paying for the cashflow AND the product market fit. The PMF if you will.

You are basically guaranteeing you get a site thats on the right side of that chart, as opposed to one on the left side that isnt getting much traffic.

​

Nano Flips Special Offer

{{ snippet.sept-21-2022-oct-9-2022-cksn-vinovest-sponsorship }}

This Week’s Opportunity

This week we found a pretty nice little content site over on Flippa. Some of you will hate it. Others will see an opp. This newsletter is here to show you all kinds of deals. Im going to start spending more time highlighting sites with pros AND cons. And talk about sides of both.

(The site Im really excited about is in the next section)

​

Ok so right off the bat, the things we DONT like about this site.

  • It has almost no authority, tons of the keywords could be taken over by competitors if the site doesnt getter backlink profile
  • Very new website
  • Seller BIN is overpriced
  • Content is poorly written

Ok, so we have covered that! Now lets look at the site

​

Ok so first off, I would do a light rebrand here. Its too simple. We also would want to get some backlinks built to this site ASAP. The fact that it ranks for so many keywords without any authority, means a stronger competitor could take over its rankings.

BUT

This also makes me think this niche has TONS of opportunities like the ones it is ranking for already.

I went into Ahrefs, and did a quick analysis of its competitors. There are several that are just as weak in terms of authority, and ranking for WAY more keywords.

For some this could be a turn off. For others? I see an opp to beat the competitors, and start building great backlinks ASAP, to hold onto the rankings it already has.

Some notes to consider:

➔ The site is already monetized with ezoic AND amazon

➔ The content is poorly written, I would go in and clean it up ASAP.

➔ Would look into installing Lasso, and using different affiliate programs for monetization like home depot, lowes, etc.

​

If one were to buy this site here is what they would do:

​

  • BUILD SOME BACKLINKS! The site is doing great, but it has no authority. I would want to do a backlink gap analysis to see where my competitors had great links from, and start building some links to protect the sites rankings.

​

  • CLEAN UP THE CONTENT. It was clearly written by someone who isnt great at English. I would suggest the buyer be either an actual user of these tools, or know writers who are.

​

  • Figure out what keywords have high traffic and are on page 2! With a few backlinks we could bring lots of those pages to page 1 and increase traffic drastically. The amount of traffic a site gets being on page 2 for a keyword is NOTHING in comparison to what it can get when it hits page one.

​

Last on my list would be to get the site redesigned and pulled together to feel more like a cohesive brand. Would consider switching to Astra or Generate press for the sites theme.

The website is making $USD $133 /mo per month average over the last year and is currently bid at $1k or so currently, with a buy it now set at $11k.

The last couple months, the site has done amazingly though. Considering the recent google updates, and ranking changes the last 2 months Im both surprised and impressed its survived and continued to grow!

Last month it did a little over $300 in profit....which is why the seller thinks its worth $11k.

Its not in my opinion

I would think that more like $6-8k was the range this site should go for. Considering it has no moat and will need work quickly to keep it where it's at and grow.

I wanted to highlight this site to show you, that for the right person with the right plan, it could be a win.

But for the wrong person it could be a disaster. These are online businesses, you should have an idea of how to run them or fix them if you plan on buying them.

OR maybe you saw this listing and thought "that sites garbage...but I can beat it"

A lesson here either way.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​

Ok guys, I want to take a moment to highlight a site for sale from a friend of mine...BowTiedWookie. He's a killer, was one of the first people to join our site flipping program, and now I always ask him to come and teach lessons to people in our program.

He is selling this site, dont want to miss out on this one:

4 year old website in health niche stated to be making $2,300/m in revenue L3M being sold by BowTiedWookie (a great Substack btw).

​

Seller says:

  • Revenue currently 38% affiliate, 24% direct ads partnership, 22% Amazon Associates, 13% digital product, 3% KDP.
  • Site was created in 2018, aged domain added in summer 2021, we bought it in October 2021 from private Twitter sale.
  • Went from 68 -> 228 published posts
  • The site has gotten a boost in the last 5 consecutive core algo updates but there is always risk when you rely on one traffic source
  • 15 posts currently ordered from writers (free with the purchase of site)
  • 3 HARO links currently ordered from the Agency (free with the purchase of site)
  • Mediavine launched in mid-October (site was ad-free before this)
  • Had almost 3K subs but recently cut the list to ~750 - our emails are not great, huge opportunity for someone who understands email
  • There are a lot of small DTC companies in this niche. We started renting our Facebook pixel out to one of them this month as a test. If we held onto the site we’d hire a VA to DM every single DTC company in the space and try to rent the pixel to them

​

Ive been doing involved in the online marketing space for over 15 years, and the amount of big Google algorithm updates we have seen this year is unlike any other Ive ever experienced.

This is one of the many reasons that you want to start owning your audience. Moving website and social visitors to email lists so you can market to them again and again.

This is true whether you own a niche blog, ecom brand, or saas. No matter what you want to be in control.

Nano Flips Special Offer

{{ snippet.dec-22-2022-cksn-masterworks }}

This Week’s Opportunities

​

There are a couple interesting sites I found this week - lets look at one in the mental health space. The listing can be found here​

​

This is a 1.5 year site. It currently makes all its money from the Betterhelp affiliate program.

The Betterhelp affiliate program pays $225 USD per conversion and all conversions can be tracked through the Betterhelp dashboard.

Almost 20% of the content is written by a therapist professor at a Maltese university, which gives high quality and more authority to the content. This is something you might want to keep going as Google really puts weight into who is writing content in the mental health space when it comes to ranking pages.

First off the site hasn't sold - I would say its slightly overpriced and would value it at $100k or so if it passed a full due diligence.

There are 2 obvious levers here in my mind to pull to increase revenue and the value of the site:

  1. A pop up lead form that captures emails and presents the visitors with a quiz. At the end of the quiz they would be suggested to sign up for Betterhelp - those that didnt sign up exactly then would be in a weekly newsletter about mental health "sponsored" by Betterhelp with more links in it.
  2. A local therapy directory - you could easily build a directory page, and do some simple cold emails and DMs to therapists offering them $20 a month to be in the directory. It would come with a backlink and description and contact info. Maybe ask them to link back to your site as well! Get paid to get backlinks!

I dont think it would at all be difficult to increase revenue on this site by $1500 a month or so between these 2 changes. This would increase the value of the site by roughly $50k+.

If you made these changes month 1 and really worked hard the first month - you could make make $46,980 in the first 12 months of owning the site.

When you sold it you might be able to get $160,000+ from the sale -

If you paid $100k that would leave you with a total profit of....$106,980.00

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

Nano Thought

The year is coming to a close and that means this is the last issue of Nano Flips in 2023! To give you guys a quick some up of 2023 for the me (James) personally:

  • Sold 1 High Six Figure ecommerce brand
  • Sold 1 micro niche site from our portfolio
  • Purchased 1 new micro niche site to add to our portfolio
  • Advised on over 100+ online business purchases and sales

This doesn't even include some of the amazing wins from our other team members!

As iOS updates started eating us alive, we started a real serious push back into SEO and organic search. Its paid off well, but one of my sites has been bouncing in and out of google because of updates non stop! No worries, the plan doesn't change, we push forward knowing that we will ranking higher in the future.

Just to put this out there - next years goals include

  • Buying or building a software business
  • Growing this newsletter from 15,000 readers to 50,000
  • Flipping another site from my our portfolio
  • Launch our 12 month online business buying program

I still think that if you have a basic understanding of the business you're buying, and a plan to grow it, that buying an online business is the best way to really dive headfirst into profitable entrepreneur ship. But if money is super tight for you, it may not be the answer for you yet.

As always here is a little plug for my podcast, here is an episode I never wrote about before in the newsletter.

It is obscenely difficult to create a podcast and get traction on it. You have this massive effort to get it produced – never mind the topics! – but it only results in marginal return on investment (ROI). That’s the dark side of podcasting, right there.

When you’re hyper-focused on getting results from your efforts, the rest of it becomes… time-consuming, a chore. And when your ROI starts slipping, you have to wonder whether it’s all worth it or not.

As goal-oriented men, where are we going with this pod? The troth of despair that hangs in the air needs to change, which means the pod needs to change if the numbers are going to continue to motivate us. emails.content:
Nano Thought

When I first started Nano Flips, the idea was to just show how there were fantastic opportunities for anyone to buy, improve, and sell an online business with less than $500k.

As the newsletter has grown, it's become clear to me that many are unaware of the scale of internet businesses. With that said I wanted to highlight one of the greatest internet exits of all time:

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
YouTube was once a dating website. Then its founders took it from $0 ⏩ $1,650,000,000 exit in 18 months. This is the AMAZING story of how they achieved the “impossible” 👇 pic.twitter.com/bZvRAL6zfZ
January 31st 2023
16

A flip doesn't have to be a small content site changing its ad network and being sold for more 12 months later, or an email marketing agency that is a great bolt on acquisition for a larger agency.

Sometimes, you create magic and fully pivot from a dating site to creating YouTube and exiting for $1.6 billion 18 months later like in the thread above.

If you cant afford to buy a business? You should be building one.

​

This Week’s Opportunities

Found some interesting deals this week, but lets start with a dating site on Flippa, you can see the listing here​

​

Before we dive into this one, I want to say that it would require a serious amount of due diligence for a potential buyer. But if it passed your due diligence, it looks like it could be a major win.

The listing is for a 22 year old Online Dating Site with trademark, Forums, Blogs, eCards, Videos, Quizzes, Poems, Articles, 8 million+ views per month, 95,000+ unique visits per month

First off a quick check in Ahrefs, lets me know this site is an SEO machine

But the major win is that its just monetized with Adsense...

It doesn't have the amount of members listed and emails, but there are several ways I would try and monetize this better.

Alone switching from Adsense, to something like Ezoic, MediaVine, or Adthrive could add 50%+ in revenue

But there is also a major opportunity to cut a deal with many different dating site affiliate programs or even dating coaching offers. If you went the "adult" route you could make a TON of money from promoting cam sites and the like, but if you wanted to keep it "vanilla" one could just promote a normal dating site like eharmony and easily get $10 a sign up.

If you converted 1% of the visitors - that would be 950 people a month OR $9500 in additional revenue

Now there are 10,000 rabbit holes we could go down in terms of other growth opportunities, but these are the obvious ones to me and its worth looking at the numbers if the above scenario played out (and it passed all the due dillegence checks required)

Purchase Price - $249,000

First 12 months revenue with tweaks to monetization - $208,446

New Valuation of Business at 40x monthly net valuation: $694,820

Total Value gained minus purchase price in 12 months: $445,820

I think everything here is relatively conservative, and you might be able to find an exit to one of the many larger dating companies, even one of these public ones in which an exit for stock would still be acceptable.

emails.subject: 💸  Will AI Be The Death Of Google Search? Bard vs ChatGPT
emails.content:
Nano Thought

The hot topic of the moment, clearly is AI. Every day people ask me my thoughts on what it means for websites, and online businesses.

Well lets first take a look at the big news of the week, Google announces Bard AI in response to ChatGPT. Bard is a conversational service aimed at countering the popularity of the ChatGPT tool backed by Microsoft. Here is the mock up Google released of it in use (this looks like just a mock up to me).

You can read more about it here.

Now lets talk about what I think this means and some other people I respect the opinion of

Dom Wells of OnFolio sees this as a shift, and not the end:

Dom Wells
@DomWellsOnfolio
Very early take but I think Google launching Bard is actually good for SEO. There was a real threat that people would switch to searching via ChatGPT whereas now, they will probably stick to Google. Yes, some of your keywords will get less traffic, but you'll still get traffic.
February 6th 2023
0
Retweets
23
Likes

Sonny Lowry thinks, no way google lets their cash cow die:

Sonny Lowry
@sonny8s
@JamesonCamp @DomWellsOnfolio also means their GDN business disappears. it means no new content/adsense incentive for AI to actually get the data from. And 85% of their revenue is adwords their golden goose, they will never want to fck that up. one guy said looks like featured snippets on steroids
James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
@DomWellsOnfolio Yea I don’t think search disappears ha. Google would have some serious anti trust issues if it stopped millions of small businesss from being able to operate
February 7th 2023
0
Retweets
3
Likes

My take? Some content sites are going to see a hit on certain keywords - very similar to featured snippets.

Over the next 3 years we will see large changes in search, luckily if you have been reading this newsletter for a while, you know I dont think search is going to die, and this should re-enforce what I always say

"You want your business to have a diverse set of traffic sources, and be bringing in traffic from many keywords if its reliant on search"

Ive been doing this for 15+ years, if you're new to the online world, you should know...things are always evolving and changing. It's on us as entrepreneurs to change with the times. For everyone that is negatively affected by the rise of AI - there will be another who uses it to build massive wealth.

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Yep AI is gonna destroy a lot of peoples jobs and income It’s also going to make a bunch of people obscenely wealthy …I guess it’s up to you to decide which group you’re going to be in
February 3rd 2023
5
Retweets
88
Likes

This Week’s Opportunities

Im still a full believer that content sites will continue to have their place for the next decade, but wanted to show interesting deal flow I've seen in the digital product space recently. Check this listing out here​

Its not that I think this is an amazing deal, in fact If it passed my due diligence, Id say it was overpriced by a decent amount. If it was a fit for you, I would negotiate down. BUT if youre amazing at pinterest, or have a course/online education business, this could be a perfect fit for you.

The sale of this site comes with six (6) domain names, each of which, has its' own course material for sale.

Currently, the website has four (4) course bundles that are recently updated, evergreen, and ready to sell. These courses include (listed in customer-ascension order):

  • Pin Practical Masterclass - Course on long-term organic strategies and on-site conversions.
  • Pin Practical Influence - Course on leveraging affiliate marketing on Pinterest platform.
  • Pinterest Advertising 101 - Includes content that was repurposed from Pin Practical Promotions. (Pinterest Advertising can be followed by Ads That Scale as an upsell offer)
  • Ads That Scale - Includes content that was repurposed from Pin Practical Promotions.

The current owner has fully let it die, but when was active it did about $150K a year, passively it is doing $1500 a month or so. Knowing that? I might say it was worth $75k or so depending on what you think you can do with it.

​

Lets look at another interesting opportunity from Empire Flippers here​

​

This site isn interesting if you owned a DTC cookware brand! Might be an opp to build a simple one off the backend of it as well.

"This listing is for a display advertising business created in October 2016 in the culinary niche. The WordPress site features informational content related to baking. The business has experienced year-over-year growth and is in an evergreen niche. The business has a solid domain rating and backlink profile and drives traffic through multiple sources. The business requires minimal time to maintain.

Traffic comes primarily from organic (58.91%), social (20.18%), and direct (19.57%). The top three countries driving traffic are the US (54.79%), the UK (10.45%), and Canada (8.67%). The top three pages make up 21.69% of total site traffic, generating 7.43%, 7.32%, and 6.06% of traffic respectively."

The site is getting 100k visitors a month!

That should easily be 1k new email subscribers, and easily .25 in revenue from each subscriber per month if you sold products to the list OR even sponsorship from meal kit delivery programs.

Here is a list of affiliate programs for them: https://shivanshbhanwariyadigital.com/meal-kit-affiliate-programs/​

At an average of $20 per sign up, if we could get .5% to sign up from banner ads and emails, one could add $1k a month easily to the business.

That would add $40k or so in enterprise value to the business in the first month or two.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

James built up a successful strategy consulting firm and was lucky enough to sell to the right buyer at the right time. Stepping off the rollercoaster that is being an entrepreneur from time to time, James always gets back on.

It’s all about knowing when to sell…and when not to sell."

emails.subject: 💸  $27,000 From an Exercise Website
emails.content:
Nano Thought

I recently was going through some of my old tweets. It's nice to have an archive of all your thoughts, whether they are cringe or not ha. We are the first people in history with this ability to do so. Despite finding TONS of things ranging from my thoughts in the US gov handing out free money during the pandemic, or me asking for thoughts on bringing $100,000k+ a month in ad spend to adroll...

I found something super intersting. A reminder to bet on yourself, and that risk and reward are inherently tied together.

Check this out:

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
About 2 years ago, I held a term sheet in my hands. It was to buy a company we started a year earlier for $2M. One of the hardest things I’ve ever done, was rip that term sheet up. They saw the same thing I did, it could be worth a lot more.
December 20th 2019
0
Retweets
15
Likes

​

Now whats REALLY fun to see...is that on July 2nd of 2022, we ended up selling that business I was tweeting about, for $31,000,000.

Before you all ask...it was a holdings company.

Mostly a portfolio of websites and equity in some brands and other companies we had taken instead of cash for consulting and advertising packages on our websites and email lists

Long story short...take risks when you can, and bet on yourself. The upside potential is massive and we are truly on here once.

​

This Week’s Opportunities

This week let's look at 2 listings. The first is a small content site from Motion Invest, the listing can be seen here​

​

Lets get some of the things we don't like out of the way:

Things we don't like:

  • This is fully reliant on search and with all the AI changes coming, I believe some content sites will have drops in traffic for certain keywords in the next couple months
  • The site is built on an expired domain (web.archive.org/web/20180511195634/cardiocapital.com)
  • The top 10 keywords have been on a downwards trend over the past few months (according to AHREFS).
  • UR rating of 13 and DR rating of 9 (low stats)

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • 62% of the current ranking keywords have informational intent (according SEMRUSH). The buyer can focus on editing and updating the content that is already on the site.
  • Traffic is up from the same time as last year. The traffic is nice and spread out among the articles.
  • There are 15 missing affiliate tags (according to Site Buddy) that could be fixed for a small win.
  • Opportunity to build newsletter
  • Major opportunities with affiliate programs for cardio equipment

A new owner could:

  • Set up an email pop up and banners on the site to capture 1-2% of visitors into email subscribers. That would mean 200+ new subs a month. At .25 per a sub in revenue per month that would give the new owner $600+ a month in new revenue at the end of 12 months. Increasing the value of the site by $24,000 or so.
  • Search for weaker competitors in ahrefs and create content around keywords they are targeting, so that the new owner could over take them
  • Use a tool like Lasso to look for and plugin new affiliate programs other than amazon for cardio equipment.

With all these changes (if it all went right) one might be able to 3x their investment on this site in 12 months.

​

On to the next opportunity, this one is a gaming site listed on Empire Flippers, you can see the listing here​

Alright lets get some of the things we DON'T like about the site out of the way

Things we don't like:

  • Since the site is all about one game, there's a chance it could lose popularity down the line
  • The current content team won't stick around after the sale (but this could be great for a hobbyist!)
  • This is fully reliant on search and with all the AI changes coming, I believe some content sites will have drops in traffic for certain keywords in the next couple months

Ok...things we do like:

  • Over 750 well written pieces of content (this creates a TON of authority in Googles eyes)
  • The site's traffic and revenue have skyrocketed over the last year (its surviving updates and thriving(
  • It has some strong backlinks from Nexusmods, Thenerdstash, and Wingg

Opportunities to Keep Growing:

  • Start a podcast about the game and get it listed on Spotify and Apple Podcasts (this can bring in traffic and backlinks)
  • Build a forum or discord or newsletter to gather a community that you can push content to whenever you like
  • Search for weaker competitors in Ahrefs and create content around keywords they are targeting, so that the new owner could over take them

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what I see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

We talk about how he lost $100,000 trying to acquire a firm, the downside of financial touts, and stock buying schemes he's encountered."

emails.content:
Nano Thought

There are so many great great stories of people leaving their uninspiring 9-5 to build an exciting online business.

One of my favorites, is of Brian Kelly, and him building The Points Guy.

Check it out below:

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
In 2010, Brian Kelly was a recruiter with no passion for his job. In 2019, his travel blog made about $20,000,000 in revenue. Here’s how he turned his hobby into an 8-figure business: Let's start with a summary of the story, and then we'll get into some actionable lessons.… twitter.com/i/web/status/1… pic.twitter.com/1KFp0eUus8
March 30th 2023
4
Retweets
40
Likes

This is a reminder to all - that its more about the drive and the willingness to figure things out, than it is about the experience on has. Most of the experience that entrepreneurs have...often comes from well...figuring it out as they go!

Maybe you want to build something from scratch, or maybe you have no idea what you would build, so you find it easier to buy something. Either way, the internet is vast and the opportunities are endless.

​

This Week’s Opportunities

Content Sites

Here is a breakdown of a site from Empire Flippers. The listing can be seen here​

​

Site Summary:

The site is a content site that makes most of its money from Display Ads and Amazon Associates that was created in November 2017 in the technology niche. More specifically, this site is focused on creating informational & affiliate content about Home Audio & Video, TV & Streaming, Gaming, and miscellaneous Tech topics. Let’s dive into the details of this deal!

First here is a look at what seems like a nice history of growth on ahrefs a clear drop thats not great, but def a recovery in traffic.

​
​Things we don't like:

  • The site was massively impacted by May 2022 core update. It has recovered tremendously but only reached about 70% of 2022 traffic highs.
  • Products in this niche are constantly changing. Technology products are constantly changing and require website owners to frequently update their content to keep up.
  • Lack of internal linking & unique imagery on the website.
  • Lack of basic E-A-T signals. (authority in googles eyes)
  • Minimal social media presence & currently not collecting any emails.

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Lots of well written & informative content creating solid topical authority in the technology niche
  • Traffic from Tier 1 countries & is diversified across many different pages. Top page only gets ~8% of the website's traffic. This mitigates the risk of one page losing its ranking & losing a significant portion of overall traffic.
  • Current team of writers willing to stay onboard - Makes ownership transition much smoother.
  • Some high-quality backlinks including Kodak, GadgetReview, and more.

A new owner could:

  • Re-design the homepage to feel more like a real brand/business. The current homepage is simply a reel of the latest blog posts. Adding content to the homepage helps Google understand what your site is about. It also increases the chances that people will view your business as legitimate and link to your site.
  • Implement basic CRO (conversion rate optimization)techniques to boost affiliate revenue. Adding product comparison tables and large buy buttons should increase clicks and revenue.
  • Optimize top pages with unique images and internal linking to pass link equity. There are many pages on this site that attract backlinks and a ton of traffic. Adding internal links from these pages to other related pages can build topical authority & boost site wide traffic.
  • Create a YouTube channel reviewing products. A new owner could create a YouTube channel and perform in-depth reviews of their top-earning products. YouTube reviews can produce a significant amount of affiliate commissions.
  • A new owner could also invest in creating more affiliate content - Best of X, product comparison, product reviews, etc. Utilizing a more uniform template for your best-of lists can make it much easier to scale your content production without sacrificing quality.
  • Collect emails to create a technology-based newsletter & promote affiliate products. This allows you to continuously retarget your audience!

Final Thoughts:

Overall, the site is a high-traffic content site in the Technology niche. In the last year, they have been hit significantly by Google updates that heavily impacted traffic. As a buyer, this introduces major risk.

The current site is making 94% of all income from AdThrive. This means that the biggest growth lever is to improve the amount & quality of affiliate content to boost earnings.

The owner is selling this site for ~$126k (34x multiple of trailing 12 months average profit). This is a fair offer that leaves room for a new owner to make improvements and see a large return. However, due to risks from Google updates, we would think making an offer in the range of ~$111K (30x-32x monthly multiple).

By adding new affiliate content and implementing the CRO techniques we just discussed, a new owner could conservatively boost the earnings 15%. This would bring in an extra ~$555/mo or ~$20k in value!

Assuming the site owner reinvested all revenue in growth for the first 4 months & half of their revenue for the trailing 8 months, they could potentially earn ~$17k in revenue! The site would then be valued at ~$153k.

**Potential return = Revenue + sale profit = $17k + ($153k - $126k) = $44k*

​

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​

Nano Flips Special Offer

​

{{ snippet.april-6-19-13-16-20-27-wander }}

​

This Week’s Opportunities

​Empire Flippers FBA Listing​

Here is a breakdown of a site from Empire Flippers. The listing can be seen here​

Site Summary:

An Amazon FBA business created in July 2018 in the occasions & gifts, office supply, and equipment niches. The business has 2-brands and is protected with trademarks and Amazon Brand Registry. It sells 10 SKUs that are gifts for various occasions throughout the year and a product used in laboratories and by hobbyists.

The earnings history shows a nice linear growth trend. The business has grown 98% year over year. Revenue has grown considerably and the profits have also grown gradually as well.

​

​
​Things we don't like:

  • High multiple for these market times and compared to other FBAs.
  • Niche for the main brand is low barrier to entry. Competition will always be a risk.
  • Not suited to flippers. This is a well-optimized business.
  • All traffic is organic Amazon. Business is heavily reliant on one audience. Also, no follow-up marketing is done so risk of this being a one-stop shop.
  • PPC isn’t established. A competitor with strong PPC could be taking the paid market share on Amazon.
  • Around 50% of the products have less than 100 reviews. There’ll be high PPC costs and low conversions for these products. Although they have high reviews, and some of the products even have Amazon’s Choice badge, there is still room for growth here.
  • Products get double quality checks. While this is what’s kept the products high quality and the reviews high, it’s costly to do this.
  • To take this business to the next level and go from $2M in revenue to say $20M, you’ll need to build out a team.

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Funding approved through Boopos which offers up to 80% flexible financing with no personal guarantee
  • The products have average rating of 4.7 stars. Both brands have Amazon’s Choice products.
  • It’s in a high profit margin niche with high-margin products. Profit margins were still over 25% in 2021 when freight rates peaked
  • Star supplier is a partner. They communicate with other suppliers to bundle products and they handle the freight forwarding. Makes sourcing and logistics hands off for owners.
  • Products aren’t tied to holidays or events so there’s no seasonality.
  • Shopify store to diversify risk with multi-channel selling.
  • The business has experienced 98% year-over-year growth.
  • Strong profit margins.
  • A defensible company protected with 7 trademarks.
  • Super efficient and cost-effective operations. The two owners spend just 6 hours per week running it

A new owner could:

  • There are no established paid channels for the business, PPC is a major opp
  • Build an email list for remarketing to increase repeat purchases.
  • Both brands are well poised to expand the number of products offered. For the single-product brand, the product line is incredibly easy to expand due to the low cost of entry and ease of ordering from the current single supplier
  • The second brand sells the gift boxes, you could repeat the product launch strategy for new products. The Sellers have agreed to include 5 new potential boxes to launch and they’ll share their launch strategy.
  • Offering subscription for these types of products is a good opportunity to increase repeat sales and earn recurring revenue. Most of the products last for a few weeks to a month, which is an ideal timeline for a monthly subscription.
  • Remove the second quality check. It might be time to remove the second quality check to reduce costs and increase efficiency.

Final Thoughts:

Overall, this is a well established and optimized business. It’s best suited to a buyer who wants a hands off, long-term, and secure investment. Or an aggregator with a team to scale the business to the next level.

Having said that, there are some quick wins like launching the product ideas and new products provided by the sellers that any buyer could implement to increase profits.

The Sellers have listed for ~$1.4M. (37X multiple of trailing 12 months average profit).

This is a high multiple, so we expect the sellers to be open to negotiation to closer to 35X.

The biggest growth lever is to establish the Amazon PPC.

As of last year, Amazon now allows you to send marketing emails to your list. So building out an email list and running some retargeting campaigns is a free and effective way to increase repeat purchases.

Plus, if you remove the second product inspection you could probably keep an extra ~$10K a year in profit.

Plenty of quick-win opportunities for this large, established company that would make an ideal long-term, secure addition to your portfolio. If it’s your first time dabbling in FBA or ecommerce, there’s plenty of room for error since the business has a long earnings history, strong product reviews and Amazon presence, and formidable supply chain.

If you could negotiate to a 35x and used Boopos for financing $264k in cash would get you $169k a month in revenue of $38k in profits. Thats assuming you didnt split that with a partner or raise any money from investors.

With those numbers thats a potential 172% cash on cash return year one before any improvements.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​

Listen to it here on spotify

This Week’s Opportunities

Flippa Content Site Listing

Here is a breakdown of a site from Flippa. The listing can be seen here​

Site Summary:

PC Building Lab is an affiliate content site in the technology niche. More specifically, this site focuses on PC building & PC parts. Affiliate commissions and display advertisements monetize this site. Let’s dive into the details of this deal!

First off I want to highlight how sketchy and weak this sites backlinks are, Ahrefs gives us a good look.

Ok now that we got that out of the way, for the right person, this site could be a win for their portfolio. I would be weary of its weak link profile though.

​
​Things we don't like:

  • Suspicious backlink profile. Almost zero backlinks are pointing toward the homepage. This is normally a sign of spammy link-building tactics!
  • EEAT could be improved
  • Top 2 pages take up ~40% of the sites overall traffic
  • Nothing special about content, could be disrupted with the rise of AI

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • The site has continued to increase traffic over last ~11 months
  • Ranking on page 1 for decent keywords with revenue-generating potential
  • In-depth and well-written content that fully explains the topics that is written by subject matter expert
  • Niche has many high-ticket products that can produce large commissions.

A new owner could:

  • Re-design the homepage

I would shrink the hero image so that it does not take up 90% of the above-the-fold space. The text should also be added to the homepage to send clear signals to Google that define the website's purpose.

  • Research better affiliate programs

Amazon is great but is often the lowest-paying affiliate program. Experiment with other affiliate networks & private affiliate deals to get a high commission per sale.

  • Improve Money Pages CRO

Add comparison tables under the introduction of best-of lists should improve revenue by ~20%. Many people do not read the full post and just want to be told what the best product is!

  • Improve Topical Authority

A new owner should build relevant backlinks to the homepage; write informational content & internal link-related articles; create social media profiles for authors.

  • Create a Youtube Channel

Creating a YouTube channel to review specific PC components can drive considerable traffic & revenue. Embedding YouTube videos on your blogs can also improve their organic rankings!

Final Thoughts:

Overall, this site is in a great niche with lots of long-tail keywords to target. The content seems to be great & is written by subject matter experts. Although the PC niche is competitive, focusing on a specific type of PC component (i.e. “best motherboard cpu combination”) can be lucrative!

A new owner should immediately insert affiliate comparison tables on all “Best-of X” style posts to boost affiliate revenue ~20%. Creating more money pages targeting low-competition keywords can bring an extra ~$200/mo. At current traffic levels, Implementing display ads on informational posts can also bring another ~$80/mo.

However, the backlink profile introduces considerable risk to this website. The overall lack of links pointing to the homepage is not natural and introduces a significant risk of being impacted by a future Google update. A new owner should focus on immediately building links to the homepage to create a more well-rounded & natural backlink profile.

Its currently bid at $10k as I write this. This is quite high and very much based on its recent months revenue. We wouldnt recommend going higher than this.

If rev stayed at $375 (lowest in last 3 months) and you could add another $250 a month with new content and ads, this site would be making $625 a month and be worth $22,500. That would be a 225% cash on cash return if those numbers held up and you paid $10k for the site.

Id say you should budget to use all the profits over the next few months to improve the site. It needs stronger links and more content ASAP.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. This Week’s Opportunities

​Empire Flippers FBA Listing​

Here is a breakdown of a site from Empire Flippers. The listing can be seen here​

Site Summary:

An Amazon FBA business created in July 2018 in the occasions & gifts, office supply, and equipment niches. The business has 2-brands and is protected with trademarks and Amazon Brand Registry. It sells 10 SKUs that are gifts for various occasions throughout the year and a product used in laboratories and by hobbyists.

The earnings history shows a nice linear growth trend. The business has grown 98% year over year. Revenue has grown considerably and the profits have also grown gradually as well.

​

​
​Things we don't like:

  • High multiple for these market times and compared to other FBAs.
  • Niche for the main brand is low barrier to entry. Competition will always be a risk.
  • Not suited to flippers. This is a well-optimized business.
  • All traffic is organic Amazon. Business is heavily reliant on one audience. Also, no follow-up marketing is done so risk of this being a one-stop shop.
  • PPC isn’t established. A competitor with strong PPC could be taking the paid market share on Amazon.
  • Around 50% of the products have less than 100 reviews. There’ll be high PPC costs and low conversions for these products. Although they have high reviews, and some of the products even have Amazon’s Choice badge, there is still room for growth here.
  • Products get double quality checks. While this is what’s kept the products high quality and the reviews high, it’s costly to do this.
  • To take this business to the next level and go from $2M in revenue to say $20M, you’ll need to build out a team.

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Funding approved through Boopos which offers up to 80% flexible financing with no personal guarantee
  • The products have average rating of 4.7 stars. Both brands have Amazon’s Choice products.
  • It’s in a high profit margin niche with high-margin products. Profit margins were still over 25% in 2021 when freight rates peaked
  • Star supplier is a partner. They communicate with other suppliers to bundle products and they handle the freight forwarding. Makes sourcing and logistics hands off for owners.
  • Products aren’t tied to holidays or events so there’s no seasonality.
  • Shopify store to diversify risk with multi-channel selling.
  • The business has experienced 98% year-over-year growth.
  • Strong profit margins.
  • A defensible company protected with 7 trademarks.
  • Super efficient and cost-effective operations. The two owners spend just 6 hours per week running it

A new owner could:

  • There are no established paid channels for the business, PPC is a major opp
  • Build an email list for remarketing to increase repeat purchases.
  • Both brands are well poised to expand the number of products offered. For the single-product brand, the product line is incredibly easy to expand due to the low cost of entry and ease of ordering from the current single supplier
  • The second brand sells the gift boxes, you could repeat the product launch strategy for new products. The Sellers have agreed to include 5 new potential boxes to launch and they’ll share their launch strategy.
  • Offering subscription for these types of products is a good opportunity to increase repeat sales and earn recurring revenue. Most of the products last for a few weeks to a month, which is an ideal timeline for a monthly subscription.
  • Remove the second quality check. It might be time to remove the second quality check to reduce costs and increase efficiency.

Final Thoughts:

Overall, this is a well established and optimized business. It’s best suited to a buyer who wants a hands off, long-term, and secure investment. Or an aggregator with a team to scale the business to the next level.

Having said that, there are some quick wins like launching the product ideas and new products provided by the sellers that any buyer could implement to increase profits.

The Sellers have listed for ~$1.4M. (37X multiple of trailing 12 months average profit).

This is a high multiple, so we expect the sellers to be open to negotiation to closer to 35X.

The biggest growth lever is to establish the Amazon PPC.

As of last year, Amazon now allows you to send marketing emails to your list. So building out an email list and running some retargeting campaigns is a free and effective way to increase repeat purchases.

Plus, if you remove the second product inspection you could probably keep an extra ~$10K a year in profit.

Plenty of quick-win opportunities for this large, established company that would make an ideal long-term, secure addition to your portfolio. If it’s your first time dabbling in FBA or ecommerce, there’s plenty of room for error since the business has a long earnings history, strong product reviews and Amazon presence, and formidable supply chain.

If you could negotiate to a 35x and used Boopos for financing $264k in cash would get you $169k a month in revenue of $38k in profits. Thats assuming you didnt split that with a partner or raise any money from investors.

With those numbers thats a potential 172% cash on cash return year one before any improvements.

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

This Week’s Opportunities

​Empire Flippers​ Content Sites​

Here is a breakdown of a site from Empire Flippers. The listing can be seen here​

Site Summary:

This deal consists of 2 independent websites in the Culinary niche that are monetized via display ads (93%) & Amazon affiliate (7%).

Their content consists primarily of informational posts about various cooking recipes & common questions related to cooking. This business was originally created back in 2019 and has grown to produce a significant monthly revenue.

Let’s dive into the details & see what this deal is all about!

​

​
​Things we don't like:

  • 1 of 2 domains is currently declining in traffic since Nov 2022
  • Both sites are currently below Mediavine traffic threshold standards. A new owner would experience a decrease in rev if not approved by Mediavine.
  • Content focuses on low ticket items (Oats, Pyrex dishes, etc.)
  • Revenue has declined since 2021

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Well diversified traffic. No single page on either website is getting more than 8% of total traffic. This means the business is not 100% relying on just a single page!
  • Decent EEAT signals. Author bios with relevant history as a chef displayed on all blog posts.
  • Email capture boxes are well designed and embedded on blog posts.
  • Both sites generate >90% of total traffic from organic search. Leaves opportunity to drive social traffic.
  • Sites have several high quality backlinks (i.e. Wikipedia, TheDailyMeal, TastingTable, etc.)

A new owner could:

  • Improve CRO On Current Affiliate Links

Placing a few contextual links throughout articles is not going to drive significant revenue. Adding large red “Buy Now” buttons and affiliate tables comparing products could improve affiliate revenue by ~20%

  • Focus on Higher Ticket Affiliate Offers

A new owner could create new content hubs around expensive cooking/baking equipment (i.e. Mixers). Adding new affiliate content focused on high ticket offers could boost monthly rev

  • Focus on Pinterest & Youtube

The cooking niche is perfect for Pinterest! People love looking up creative/unique recipes. A new owner could invest in growing a large Pinterest following to boost traffic & rev. Creating Youtube videos reviewing cooking/baking equipment could also boost traffic & improve revenue

  • Digital Products

A new owner could invest in creating digital products to promote to their audience. Maybe an online cooking class

  • Email List

A new owner could keep growing the ~2k person email list. Use this list to promote affiliate products, digital products, and share blog posts. Using a free recipe ebook as a lead magnet could significantly improve email signups. Optimizing email campaigns could earn an additional ~$100/mo or more. This list could also grow much faster with the amount of traffic the site gets a lead magnet.

Final Thoughts:

Overall, these websites in the culinary niche make for an interesting investment opportunity for a new or experienced operator. In my experience, cooking is an excellent niche for a content/affiliate website for several reasons.

  • Cooking has a broad appeal…everybody eats!
  • Its an evergreen topic, meaning that it is always in demand and does not go out of style
  • There are many affiliate marketing opportunities (cooking equipment, cooking classes, etc.)
  • Social media can be a powerful tool for driving traffic to a cooking affiliate website (especially Pinterest + YouTube)
  • Could build a newsletter or community which will be important as search engines may change with Ai in the future
  • If you are buying or building content sites in 2023 YOU MUST be thinking about how you can build retention models like newsletters and communities and find traffic sources other than search engines

The website is currently listed for a 28x monthly multiple of the current revenue of $4,344. The low valuation likely accounts for the fact a new owner would not be approved onto Mediavine (would have to use Ezoic).

Might even be worth offering a slightly lower multiple (26x) based on the declining revenue and traffic.

While you're here!

One of our team members has a site they started and don't have time to work on - it just started making a little money. Its being sold as a starter site on Motion Invest - check it out here​
​

​

Overview of the Website

This starter website has been around for over 1 year and 6 months.

✔ The top 10 keywords are down over the past year (according to Ahrefs).

✔ 41% of the current ranking keywords have informational intent (according to SEMRUSH). The buyer can focus on editing the content that is already on the site.

✔ The highest percentage of organic traffic currently comes from Bing.

✔ There are 61 out-of-stock items (according to Site Buddy) that could be fixed.

✔ Site is currently monetized via Amazon with the opportunity to expand into other monetization methods.

✔ The site was built on an expired domain from 2013 (web.archive.org/web/20190301000000*/bowlingview.com)

​

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. emails.subject: 💸  Recession Proof Online Businesses are For Sale
emails.content:
Nano Thought

There are 1000s of businesses for sale every single day. The trick is to know which levers to pull to improve them. This could include a myriad of things like:

  • changing pricing
  • cleaning up product pages to convert higher
  • improving the speed of a site
  • going after low hanging fruit of keywords to rank for in Google search
  • creating a social channel for the business
  • setting up retargeting ads
  • adding a newsletter or community to a business to keep customers/readers returning
  • or you can do something like this ⬇️
James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Bought a site doing about $300 a month for $10k Will start selling 1 sponsored post/advertorial per month for $300-500 Will quickly allow us to double the value of the site for a flip in 6 months pic.twitter.com/N1Pq2r9AVb
May 3rd 2023
3
Retweets
94
Likes

Now I want to be clear....

Not every site you buy, will be able to sell sponsored posts on it for $500 each

And I wouldn't reccomend selling more than 1-2 of those a month in 99% of cases. And its super important to make sure they are a fit and good quality!

But if you get the right niche, and buy a business/website that has tons of authority, and traffic, in the right niche...its one of the easiest revenue streams to unlock.

This was an inbound request and we get 3-4 of these a month. They will write the post, we will approve and edit it, and post it. Maybe a 20 minute process on our end in total to add $500 in revenue and possibly more than double the value of the site for when we sell it.

Site Summary:

Site Summary:

An Amazon FBA, display advertising, and affiliate business created in June 2017 in the pet care niche. The business comes with two WordPress sites and an Amazon account registered through Amazon Brand Registry.

It sells 3 SKUs related to game-type products for a household pet. The business has experienced solid year-over-year growth in revenue and the top-selling SKUs have a 4.2-star rating or greater across thousands of reviews. This business requires minimal time to maintain.

​
​Things we don't like:

  • Sells in the UK, so a buyer will need to get registered with VAT, which can take up to 3 months or more. Or they’d have to close that channel off.
  • Comes with display ads and affiliate sites so a buyer will need to have some knowledge of SEO or have an editor to edit content—the owners currently do this themselves.
  • Logistics is reliant on only one supplier located in China.
  • Affiliate sites use expert writers on the About Us page. Some of the SEO traffic is reliant on their names, so a buyer would probably need to keep paying them to contribute writing to maintain site traffic.
  • According to the seller, the listing pages had a high bounce rate because the packs were too large and expensive. Though they’ve just launched smaller packs and expect those to sell well.
  • Inventory management hasn’t been the best in the business’ history. The seller notes they’ve been out of stock a few times. The seller buys as and when needed instead of ordering in bulk.

​

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Solid metrics: profit margins, TACoS, COGS, year-over-year growth.
  • Affiliate sites are well-built: diverse traffic sources, nice spread across the sites, and ranks highly for some relevant keywords.
  • Comes with an on-the-ground inventory manager contact in China.
  • Multiple revenue streams. Not 100% reliant on Amazon.
  • Has an audience off Amazon that can be used for product launches, upsells, and remarketing.
  • Comes with products ready to be launched. The seller has had great feedback for these products. And they’re hard to make, so difficult for competitors to replicate. Plus, the seller has a trademark pending for them.
  • The brand and products are protected by trademarks.

A new owner could:

  • Build a Shopify store on the affiliate sites to sell products off Amazon. This would diversify the ecommerce side of the business.
  • Build an email list from the affiliate site traffic. Can use this list for product launches and sales, or build an email newsletter to nurture the customer base.
  • Sell the products that are ready for launch and optimize inventory management to prevent stock outs and reduce COGS.

​

Final Thoughts:

​

This is a solid Amazon FBA business on its own, but it also comes with established and profitable affiliate and display ads sites that support the brand and diversify the business.

It comes with plenty of growth assets. Especially the products ready for launch are quick-win ROI opportunities.

In the long term, optimizing inventory management and experimenting with product pack sizes and pricing to get sales more consistent will help stabilize the business and set it up for the next level of growth.

It’s a business with potential whether you understand content sites or not. You can outsource content production and editing and focus more on the Amazon side of the biz and even use the affiliate sites to expand the ecommerce arm. If you have knowledge of SEO and affiliate, then you can grow that side of the business to diversify the business’ earning power and make the asset more secure.

​

In 1790, 90% of Americans worked on farms.

If you’re a copywriter, a media buyer, a graphic designer, or an SEO specialist… you’re screwed.

You’ve got 3, maybe 5, years until AI does to you what the tractor did to field hands.

Farm hands are gone.

Farmland is one of the best, physical, investments you can make. It returns a steady 11% a year.

And farmers are rich.

The average farmer has a net worth of $2 million according to

That’s twice what the average 45 year old physician is worth.

Almost 4 times that of the average American.

Because there is a difference between working the field and owning the farm.

All from the people who are buying and building digital real estate right now.

I mean think about the travel industry for a second.

It’s just not a thing anymore.

But Priceline.com was founded in 1997.

It went public 2 years later.

That catapulted Jay Walker, the founder, into the ranks of the ultra rich.

​
Less than two years after he started the site he flipped it onto the public market and made over $1 billion.

And it’s still a $96 billion company.

That’s why you need to own digital assets.

They are the best investment class on the planet.

If you’re still reading this email you know it’s true.

You can not stay a field hand.

You can not keep trading time for money.

It’s time to buy the farm.

It’s time to grow your wealth through digital real estate,

And build a portfolio of many digital properties.

That’s why I’ve created my Digital Real Estate Mentorship program.

To give you step by step instructions on how to do it.

It is everything you need to get started investing in digital real estate.

So don’t wait.

We both know that jobs are going away.

If you’re a lawyer… If you're an architect… If you’re a programmer… we’re looking at end games.

Computers are going to replace most of those jobs in the next 5 years.

If you’re still relying on them to pay the bills when that happens… you’ve got nowhere to go.

But if you own the farm. If you start building a portfolio of high profit digital real estate then you could be set for life.

You’ve just got to act now.

emails.subject: The secret to fast website flips
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }},

We’ve gotten a ton of questions over the last couple of days about the Digital Real Estate Mentorship Program.

So I thought it would be worth it to answer a few of the most common ones.

Is there a payment plan?

Yes.

We’ve got a 3 pay plan you can choose at check out.

What’s the secret to a successful flip?

Growth.

Digital Real Estate sells for 20-40X monthly revenue.

That means a site that makes $500 a month would sell for anywhere between $10,000 and $20,000.

And every sale is a little different, but revenue is generally measured on a trailing 5-6 month window.

So the sales price is mostly going to be based on the average revenue of from the 6 months.

Obviously that means that once you buy a site you need to grow revenue in order for it to be successful.

But here’s the thing most people don’t understand.

You don’t need to double the revenue to double the sales price.

Because the 10-20X monthly revenue range for sales price isn’t random.

Sites with flat revenue (not growing month over month) are much harder to sell.

It can take weeks to find a buyer. And they sell at the bottom of the price range.

A site that makes $500 a month and has been flat for the last year is unlikely to get more than $10,000-$12,000.

BUT a site that’s making $500 and showing 5-10% month over month growth… that sells FAST. And it can command a premium price. It’s far more likely to sell for $18,000-$20,000.

Which is why I hand you my step by step plan to quickly and consistently grow revenue the second you join the program.

Because, if you buy the right piece of digital real estate, it’s possible to more than double the value of the asset by increasing revenue by 50%

Let me give you an example.

Say you buy a dog food blog that’s been making $500 a month for the last year. Your purchase price is $10,000.

Over the first 6 months you own the site you grow revenue 10% a month.

That breaks down like this:

  • Month 1 revenue: $550
  • Month 2 revenue: $605
  • Month 3 revenue: $665.50
  • Month 4 revenue: $732.05
  • Month 5 revenue: $805.25
  • Month 6 revenue: $885.78

That puts your average revenue for those 6 months at $707.26

So if you sold at the same multiple you bought at the asset would go for $14,145.

That’s a 40% return. Just by itself. No stock or bond on earth comes close to touching that.

But then remember that a growing site can sell for A LOT more than an asset that isn’t growing.

If you got a 25X multiple that asset would be worth $17,681.50.

If you got a 30X it would be $21,217.80

35X would be $24,754.1

That’s what I love about digital real estate.

Stocks, bonds, cryptocurrency any other asset you can name… it’s out of your hands.

You have zero control over the return you make.

Digital Real Estate puts the power back in your hands. It’s still mostly passive - it only takes a couple hours a week to manage your portfolio.

But if you know what you’re doing the returns can crush anything you’ll see on the public market.

With no worries about what’s happening on Wall Street. You’re in control. Not the fed. Not the market.

And I can show you how to get started right now.

What’s included in the program?

There’s more than I can fit in an email.

Members get:

  • All my SOPs, due diligence checklists, and tools. Everything you need to find the highest growth potential sites
  • My complete system for growing revenue.
  • Live access to me and my team over zoom.
  • A community of investors to help you find and vet deals
  • The best resources for funding deals.

And so much more.

If you want to see everything we’ve got in store for you, you can click here to see a complete breakdown.

PLUS we’ve added an easy payment plan option to make getting started as simple as possible.

​Click here to join the Digital Real Estate Mentorship Program now.​

To your success.

James

emails.subject: 💸  $73k a month from a children's brand?
emails.content:
Nano Thought

To those of you who have been around here for a while....Welcome back to our regular programming.

Weekly sites for sale, and tips on how to grow them

"Why would someone sell an online business that's making money?"

This is one of THE MOST common questions that I get. I recently brought up the topic and got some great replies on Twitter:

​

Shlomo Freund
@FreundShlomo
@JamesonCamp haha. I hear this all the time: Why would someone sell such a business? 1. They are tired of it (and that's ok) 2. The grew it to the maximum they can. 3. They have a bigger opportunity. 4. They need the money 5. I probably missed more reasons....
James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
Im always blown away when people say "No way you can buy an online business that's profitable! Nobody would sell that!" You couldn't be more wrong, the opportunities are endless
11:46 AM • Jun 19, 2023
0
Retweets
1
Likes
Read 1 replies
​

​

To sum it up...there are infinite reasons! Don't forget that when you buy a stock, it's being sold to you by another person that has decided they don't want it. Even when you buy Amazon and Apple! The largest most profitable companies in the world.

It's not your job as a business buyer, to decide if the seller's personal reasons are good or not. It's your job to decide if the business is a good one.

And is the right one for you to run and grow. Here are a few deeper explanations:

  1. Cashing in: Selling a business allows the owner to receive a lump sum payment, which can be used for personal or professional purposes, such as taking a well-deserved vacation, remodeling their home, or buying a new car.
  2. Lifestyle Change: Running an online business can be demanding, and some entrepreneurs may decide to sell their business to pursue a different lifestyle or work-life balance.
  3. Creative Block: Entrepreneurs may experience a creative block or burnout, leading them to sell their business and seek new challenges or projects.
  4. Health Concerns: Unfortunately, health issues can be a significant factor in the decision to sell an online business. Entrepreneurs facing health challenges may choose to sell their business to focus on their well-being
  5. Scaling and Operational Challenges: While online businesses offer incredible scalability, not all businesses can maintain exponential growth. Entrepreneurs may decide to sell their business if they feel they've reached the peak of its potential or if they're struggling to manage the operational challenges that come with growth

​

Nano Flips Special Offer

​

Ok Gang!

This is a pretty sweet little deal right here. Im often looking for insights from other operators and markets that I respect. Olly Richards is one of them.

​

​Olly Richards put together a giant, 117-page case study about how he’s scaled his business to $10M.

When he sent it to me I have to admit I was pretty impressed at the depth.

Seems relevant not just for creators and coaches but anyone looking for creative solutions to scale with a super lean team. If your buying, building, or operating sites, its def worth a download.

​

​Download here​

​

This Week’s Opportunities

​Empire Flippers FBA Listings​

Here is a breakdown of a site. The listing can be seen here​

Site Summary:

An FBA listing for ya all this week!

This listing is for an Amazon FBA and eCommerce business created in January 1998 in the children niche. The business has been selling online since 1998 and on Amazon since 2008! The included Amazon Seller Central account is registered with Amazon Brand Registry and features 50 SKUs (plus 10 product bundles) for children's toys.

The business has been earning 7 figures in revenue since 2002. All of the products have 4+ star ratings, with the top-selling SKUs having thousands of reviews and one has an Amazon's Choice badge. Nice long history without a ton of time needed to maintain.

​
​Things we don't like:

  • A relatively significant portion of the business comes from bulk orders instead of being strictly FBA or DTC.
  • Logistics is reliant on only one supplier located in China.
  • The business is experiencing a bit of YoY revenue decline.
  • Because some of the products can be seasonal, inventory management can be difficult and it’s important to approach high sales seasons with care.

​

Ok Y'all! things we do like:

  • Nice net profit margins at 31%, evergreen niche and strong reviews.
  • The business has 2 decades of clearing 7-figures in revenue so it’s a VERY well established brand.
  • With just 60 SKUs there’s a good amount of diversification without having an overwhelming number of products. One of the products even has an Amazon’s Choice Badge.
  • Limited amount of work required each week, mostly to do with inventory management.

A new owner could:

  • Focus more on building out additional streams of revenue such as Shopify and Walmart. Walmart would be an easier quick win than Shopify.
  • Optimize and scale PPC campaigns to get revenue figures back on the upward trend - consdider bringing new media buyer in house
  • Develop additional products within the children’s niche that complement the existing line.

​

Final Thoughts:

There’s no doubt that a business that’s been this successful for more than 20 years can continue to be successful well into the future. (Its called the Lindy effect yall)

The most obvious thing that needs to be addressed as soon as the new owner takes it on is the declining revenue. With optimization of PPC campaigns and expanding into other verticals, it’s def doable for the right operator.

If you’re looking for an established business and have the knowledge and desire to grow it to the next level, this could be a great fit. None of the pain of finding products and gathering reviews but all of the opportunity for creating success in new channels.

Worth looking into some lenders for this one if youre interested in it. Seems as if it might qualify!

​

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​
​Podcast Corner

Ok team, this week I want to share a podcast that truly spoke to me. Hopefully it will speak to you guys as well.

Often we measure success in the wrong ways, and chase wins only to find that they are unfifilling.

This is one of the reasons that I urge people to build or buy an online business. So that they too, can start to explore what truly makes them feel fulfilled. Working for yourself is the easiest way to explore that for many.

Rick shares his insights on why curiosity is a powerful tool when it comes to achieving dreams and finding success, the influence our attitude has towards the things that we do and the people we surround ourselves with, and how to stay focused on your goals and not get distracted by negativity and lack of support. Thanks yall, see ya next week!

(James)
