emails.subject: 💸  How Jared made $25k with a couple hours of work
emails.content:
Nano Thought

Alright! Let's break it down with a fun analogy 🚀🏡

Think of the online business world like a housing market in the bustling Digital City. You've got two options:

  1. The SkyRocket Tower: It's a brand new, shiny skyscraper, rising right at the center of the buzz. It has laser light shows at night and virtual reality balconies. Everyone's raving about it, but it was built in a hurry, and there are rumors about shaky foundations. You might enjoy the high life for a bit, but what if the next big storm hits?
  2. The SteadyHaven Cottage: Nestled in a consistent neighborhood, this charming cottage has been around for years. It's well-built, has a blooming garden, and a tight-knit community around it. Sure, it doesn't have the VR balconies, but it's weathered many storms, and people who live there tend to stay for generations.

Now, let's translate this into online business:

  • The SkyRocket Tower is that exciting new online business. It might be a cutting-edge AI-powered fashion site that predicts trends. While it looks glamorous now, its technology might be unproven, and customer loyalty is untested. What happens when the novelty wears off or a competitor arrives?
  • The SteadyHaven Cottage represents a stable content website. For instance, a cooking blog with timeless recipes, community engagement, and a loyal following. It may not have the AI flashiness, but it has dependable revenue from various sources like ads, affiliate marketing, and a subscription model.

So, which would you choose?

  • SkyRocket Tower is like a thrilling roller coaster ride. Exciting, but potentially unstable. Its attraction may be temporary, and investing in it might lead to a bumpy ride.
  • SteadyHaven Cottage is like a trusted family car. It may not be the fanciest, but it's reliable, safe, and gets you where you want to go.

Buying an online business that's stable and has been around a while is like investing in a solid, well-maintained home. It might not make your heart race, but it'll provide warmth, shelter, and steady appreciation over time. And with some improvements...it will be worth LOTS more.

In the flashy digital landscape, it's the steady cottages that often turn out to be the wisest investments. 🚀🏡💼

Now that we understand that - we DO want businesses that we can make quick improvements to!

Sometimes we can find a simple change and GREATLY improve the cashflow and value of an asset.

Here as a great example of how one small change, can add $25k in value with a few hours of work:

We switched all of our affiliate product boxes from AAWP to Lasso for one of our websites. June: AAWP July: Lasso Results? Let's get into the details! 🧵👇

By switching to Lasso to display products, he added $700 a month in profit to this site. Which at a normal multiple adds $25k+ to the value of the site if he sells it.

If you want to try Lasso check it out here.

​Olly Richards put together a giant, 117-page case study about how he’s scaled his business to $10M.

When he sent it to me I have to admit I was pretty impressed at the depth.

Seems relevant not just for creators and coaches but anyone looking for creative solutions to scale with a super lean team. If your buying, building, or operating sites, its def worth a download.

​

​Download here​

This Week’s Opportunities

Lots of deal flow this week. Let's look at some newsletters, content sites, and more!

​

Newsletter Business

For those interested in running a newsletter, here is an interesting one!

It's a French newsletter in the crypto space. Obviously quite a niche, but there are riches in the niches! I believe we will have another bull run in crypto again one day. This could be a great bolt-on for someone already in the space.

​

Content Site Business

Looking for a content site to start with or add to your portfolio?

​This is an interesting one from Motion Invest​

This water website has been around for over 1 year and 10 months.

✔ ~58% of the current ranking keywords have informational intent (according to SEMRUSH). The buyer can focus on editing and improving the content that is already on the site.

✔ Site is currently monetized via Amazon with the opportunity to expand into other monetization methods. The seller also earns some money via Shopify Collabs. Only Amazon was included in the income average.

✔ The top 10 keywords are down over 12 months (according to Ahrefs).

✔ The site doesn’t have a logo and the theme is plain. So that could be something for the buyer to improve upon after taking over.

This is a truly ugly website you guys.

Digital Product Business

Looking to get into the Auto Transportation Broker Business? Well, Niche Investor has an interesting site for sale here. Launched in November 2013, this 9-year-old business has helped hundreds of people get started with their auto transportation broker business seamlessly.

The website includes a suite of digital goods that help guide industry newcomers and experienced business owners. It has 175 articles published, established social media profiles, and 1,197 email subscribers.

It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

Nano Thought

Alright! Let's break it down with a fun analogy 🚀🏡

Think of the online business world like a housing market in the bustling Digital City. You've got two options:

  1. The SkyRocket Tower: It's a brand new, shiny skyscraper, rising right at the center of the buzz. It has laser light shows at night and virtual reality balconies. Everyone's raving about it, but it was built in a hurry, and there are rumors about shaky foundations. You might enjoy the high life for a bit, but what if the next big storm hits?
  2. The SteadyHaven Cottage: Nestled in a consistent neighborhood, this charming cottage has been around for years. It's well-built, has a blooming garden, and a tight-knit community around it. Sure, it doesn't have the VR balconies, but it's weathered many storms, and people who live there tend to stay for generations.

Now, let's translate this into online business:

  • The SkyRocket Tower is that exciting new online business. It might be a cutting-edge AI-powered fashion site that predicts trends. While it looks glamorous now, its technology might be unproven, and customer loyalty is untested. What happens when the novelty wears off or a competitor arrives?
  • The SteadyHaven Cottage represents a stable content website. For instance, a cooking blog with timeless recipes, community engagement, and a loyal following. It may not have the AI flashiness, but it has dependable revenue from various sources like ads, affiliate marketing, and a subscription model.

So, which would you choose?

  • SkyRocket Tower is like a thrilling roller coaster ride. Exciting, but potentially unstable. Its attraction may be temporary, and investing in it might lead to a bumpy ride.
  • SteadyHaven Cottage is like a trusted family car. It may not be the fanciest, but it's reliable, safe, and gets you where you want to go.

Buying an online business that's stable and has been around a while is like investing in a solid, well-maintained home. It might not make your heart race, but it'll provide warmth, shelter, and steady appreciation over time. And with some improvements...it will be worth LOTS more.

In the flashy digital landscape, it's the steady cottages that often turn out to be the wisest investments. 🚀🏡💼

Nano Thought

We had some good news for Macro markets this week...which means good news for us as well as the micro or "nano" markets ;)

My takeaway is a couple of different things

  1. Inflation is finally coming down, and the Fed thinks they may have it under control
  2. Debt is not going to get any more expensive
  3. Some assets will still be undervalued until next year when the Fed starts cutting rates again, and everyone starts borrowing and buying

One thing that has become VERY clear to me is that the macro environment very much has an effect on the micro.

The higher the interest rates, the less the spending and investing, the fewer buyers, the less competition.

This means there is an opportunity as a buyer today that will disappear when the Fed cuts rates next year.

The next 6 months may give us all a window to purchase cash flow positive businesses at a discount to what they will be worth next year.

Baron Rothschild, a British banker and politician from the wealthy international Rothschild family, once said that the best time to buy is “when there is blood in the streets.” In simple words, when there are fewer buyers, it's a great time to purchase.

Google Updates Y'all

If you are in the SEO world, you probably have heard about Google's most recent Core update. The HCU or "Helpful Content Update"

Latest Core Update Highlights - April 2023

  • The update lasted for 13 days and 2 hours.
  • We're in the early stages, so the full impact is still unfolding.

What We Know So Far:

  • 🌎 It's a global update affecting all regions and languages.
  • 🌟 The aim is to recognize and reward top-notch web pages.
  • 📅 Though Google shared the news on August 22nd, some experts spotted changes nearly a week earlier. (One of our sites is up 40% in traffic)

For SEO Experts:

  • 📉 Reports indicate some websites saw traffic dips 5-7 days before the official announcement.
  • 🧐 Stay vigilant with your SERP rankings and analytics as the update unfolds.

A Note from Google:

  • 📉 A dip in your site's performance? Don't panic! It might be the update adjusting things, not your site's content or structure.
  • 🚀 If rankings fall, prioritize improving your site's overall quality before diving into technical fixes.
  • 🔍 Stay updated by checking the Google Search Status Dashboard.

Remember, updates mean growth. If one site loses traffic, it means another site has replaced it in the search engine results!

It is also a reminder that GOOGLE SEARCH TRAFFIC SHOULDN'T BE YOUR ONLY SOURCE OF TRAFFIC

emails.subject: 💸 Get paid Thousands to Drive an RV and Write about it!
emails.content:
Nano Thought

Im very bullish on Internet based businesses these days. And no I don't just mean content sites (although there is some AMAZING opportunity there).

Lets take a look at some Newsletter/media exits recently:

Thomas Shields
@readmynewslettr
8 Newsletter/Media Acquisitions: (2020) Charlotte Agenda acquired by Axios - Local news - Value: $4.5m - 55k subs, $2m rev (2021) The Water Coolest acquired by Barstool Sports - Sports news - 100k subs
6:15 AM • Nov 1, 2023
1
Retweets
22
Likes
Read 5 replies
​

As always the opportunity is there.

If you can lean into some clever seller financing, or have cash, the opps are better than ever. With higher rates...we see less people using debt, which means less buyers, today, which means....less competition.

Rates will drop again eventually, and things will go back to being risk on, and valuations will go up. Learning to time and recognize cycles is a super power, and something I only really started paying attention to in the past few years.

More excited than ever for the next time rates come down!

We Need 17 Seconds Of Your Time!

We have been putting a lot of stuff together behind the scenes here recently. And it clicked to the team on Friday...why dont we just ask the readers what they want!

So, if you want to do us all a favor and fill this out: https://forms.gle/mFiS3Nf9LU6HW2DcA​

Its like 3 multiple choice questions, and it will help us put together more content that you want!

If you dont want to? No stress :) We will keep at it anyway!

​

This Week’s Opportunities

Some deal flow this week.

Ecom Business

"Women's jewelry brand that is both eco-friendly and supports charitable causes"

🎉 Here's a site for sale you might be interested in from Acquire,

This is a VERY interesting one. I happen to know the seller personally.

The reason I find it interesting is the email list it comes with is 391,000+ people

I won't pitch this to all of you, but for those who understand how valuable a list like this is, you know its worth the cost of the entire business.

I would look at trying to structure some creative deal structure with the seller, possibly even offer some seller financing. If I bought it I would JUST really care about the customer data/list.

​

Content Site

​Nice looking RV site for sale!​

Just some quick details about this site!

➔ Rankings for 3.9k keywords.

➔ Ranking for 302 keywords on the first page.

➔ Authority score of 9.

➔ Majority of the traffic is coming from the US.

Ways to improve it for a flip

➔ There are 690 Amazon links being used and of those 12 links is missing an affiliate tag.

➔ The site links to 351 different Amazon products and of those 18 products are out of stock, meaning people who click on those links can’t actually purchase the product. Swapping those products with different products that are in stock can help to increase income.

I would say this is a perfect buy for someone that actually LOVES RVs! Take real photos and genuinely blog about being an RV owner.

Take a page out of Mikes Book: https://twitter.com/NicheDown​

He has a site called https://www.staynewengland.com/ that is truly crushing it these days, and its because he IS GENUINELY WRITING ABOUT EXPLORING NEW ENGLAND!
​

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​
​Podcast Corner

Back when I was on the Ecommerce Building Blocks podcast, check it out below!

​

​

What’s on the pod?

If you’re looking to get into entrepreneurship and making money online we dive deep into that topics today. On this week’s episode, Jason sits down with Web property flipper, James Camp from Nanoflips.

Jason and James dive into the rabbit hole on how to acquire niche content sites, how to improve them and what size of business is great to get your feet wet in the flipping space. They discuss how to analyze a web property, how to fix it up and how to think about exit. And if niche content sites aren’t your thing Jason and James also talk about flipping houses, watches, NFTs, and eCommerce sites.

Is it better to look at major fixer-uppers or sites that just need a fresh coat of paint? -

Best channels for monetization -

The craziest flip James Camp has ever seen -

How to drive and maintain traffic to a site once you’ve flipped it -

Tips for choosing the kinds of sites to invest in in the next year.

emails.subject: 🔥 Don’t Get Burned on Your First Flip
emails.content:
The world is on fire.

I genuinely feel that way.

Sometimes when the world is this chaotic and the news is blasting negative headlines I forget that there are tons of opportunities available…

Whenever there’s turmoil on the global stage, some things get a lot worse.

Like real estate getting hit by the highest interest rates we’ve seen in 23 years…

…But some things get a lot better.

In digital real estate, we don't play by the same rules...So we have a LOT more flexibility.

And from what I’m seeing in my feed, I’m convinced there has never been a better time to buy a website.

Here’s my take:

In the global economy, the USD is the most widely circulated currency.

And the U.S. is currently fighting 2 proxy wars, adding to trillions of dollars of national debt that’s been growing for many years (and there’s no telling when - or if - that will ever go back down).

If you’ve got trillions of dollars of debt that you need to pay off, you can either make money or… ”make money” - as in just print more.

More dollars in circulation obviously means less value per dollar, leaving us in the inflation-ridden hellscape we currently find ourselves in.

And that cycle is going to continue for the rest of our lifetimes:

Creating debt → raising rates → dropping rates → printing money → creating debt, and so on.

What does this mean for you?

It means your money is literally burning a hole in your pocket.

Compensation has not risen at the rate of inflation, so even if you received a 2-3% increase in your salary every year, you’ve already lost obscene buying power.

If you’re an employee…

  • Your salary can’t keep up with inflation
  • Your wages don’t keep up with the cost of living
  • You have no guarantee that your job will still be there tomorrow.

Remember the tech layoffs in January? That won’t be the last round.

And worst of all, you have no power to do anything about your employer.

If you choose to do nothing, you might as well pull a 20 out of your wallet and light it on fire.

The cycle of raising rates, dropping rates, and printing money is guaranteed to continue for at least the next decade.

If you learn to recognize the pattern, you can essentially predict the future. Look at this:

As of November 1st, Japan approved a 110 billion dollar stimulus package to fight inflation.

We can see the global impact of this cycle playing out in real-time, and it’s not going anywhere any time soon…

But you know who’s not going to get hit as hard by an economic downturn if World War III breaks out?

North Korea.

Just kidding…

It’s business owners.

People still spend during inflation cycles - the world just gets more expensive.

But when you own a business, you now have the control to increase prices.

The same goes for owning assets.

Assets go up in relation to currency, so as prices increase, assets become more valuable.

Bottom line: you don’t want cash in your pocket as this cycle continues.

You want to own assets that give you the power to pull some levers and keep earning as people continue to spend.

Whether that looks like full-time entrepreneurship or a supplemental investment plan, the strategy is the same.

By the way, I didn’t invent any of this.

Every billionaire since the dawn of time has preached the value of assets, assets, assets.

I’m just taking that time-tested theory and applying it to a digital age.

You have more opportunity to own a business right now than any group of humans have had since the start of civilization.

I know people in Bangalore who are running $20K/month internet businesses.

It does not matter who you are, if you have access to the internet, you can do this.

And you can do it a hell of a lot sooner than you think.

In the next X days, I’m going to show you exactly how to take advantage of the perfect storm created by global market trends so you can buy digital assets that will allow you to print money without causing additional inflation.

So mark this email as important to keep this at the top of your inbox, because the next 5 days are going to feel like Christmas on steroids.

Talk soon,

-James

​
​
​

emails.subject: 💰 Who wants to make 2-4X ROI?
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name | strip | default: "there" }},

I know we talked last time about the USD losing value.

Just to give you an update, the dollar lost 7% of its value from 2021 to 2022

If you had 5,000 in your bank account, it’s now worth 4,650.

Let’s say you had 10,000…

Now it’s worth 9,300.

At 50K…that’s a loss of 3.5K in a single year.

If that doesn’t inspire you to make a change to your strategy, you may have a gambling addiction…

Jokes aside, I used to be a lot more comfortable taking risks. Back when I was 14 and determined to become an entrepreneur, I was willing to try anything…

I even bought an ebook on melting down scrap gold. Imagine me sitting in my mom’s apartment melting down scrap jewelry to sell gold - a modern-day Andrew Carnegie 😆

These days, I keep my deadbolt locked in the middle of the day. You never know in Beverly Hills.

Just yesterday I saw a poodle off its leash…

Truth is, at this point in my life I’m not looking for some high-risk, 1,000X return opportunity.

I’m looking for something with a low-risk threshold - something I know is going to work.

If you’ve been following me for a while, you already know there’s a segment of online investment properties too small for private equity and the “1,000Xers” to look at.

These properties - what I like to call “Nano Flips”,” range from 600 dollars to 250K. but these strategies will work for any online business.

I used some of the same SEO tactics I’m going to teach you on sites of multibillion-dollar companies, like McKinsey & Company, as well as when mentoring VC-backed startups at Google Launchpad and Techstars.

So it really comes down to finding the right site for you.

Myself and the Nano Flips community have built millions of dollars in value just using these small content sites.

These "Nano Flips" aren’t going to excite anyone looking to acquire a billion-dollar tech company…

But if you’re looking to acquire a profitable business that you can manage with just a few hours a week…

This is a perfect opportunity for you.

Especially if you have a full-time job and you’re trying to increase your earnings at a predictable rate without dedicating an additional 20 hours a week.

Let me show you what I mean:

Tech has come to a reckoning in the past couple of years with companies massively over-valued at 10, 20, even 100X.

The actual online business world is sub 10 million dollars, but they’re still trading at 2.5-4X their yearly profits.

That’s a huge opportunity for you as an investor.

Because you don’t want to invest in a big bloated tech startup or bet on the stock market.

You want to invest in something with good odds, low risk, and great returns.

Let’s look at the numbers (I literally just Googled this)

Right now, Meta has a price-to-earnings ratio of 26.3

The peer average is 30.2

Meaning if you put a dollar into Meta right now, it will take 25.5 years for the profits to reach the current value of the company.

Compare that to the smaller sites we’re buying…

At 2.5-4X, that’s an average of about 3 years to earn your money back.

Smaller online assets are beating massive tech companies like Meta hand over fist.

You can buy one of these websites at 3X ROI and make 33% back this year.

Meaning…If you can find a cash-flowing business and make small improvements, every $1 you change in monthly profits adds $36 in value to the business.

That’s why I always recommend you start small:

  • Buy one site to cover gas and utilities
  • Then buy another one to pay for your mortgage
  • Then another one to save for vacation

This is the path to early retirement.

When you start small on something low-risk, you get to enjoy these exponential gains.

Every mile is traveled the same way, regardless of who you are: one step at a time.
​
And if you’ve never bought a business before…don’t spend all your savings on the 1st.

Tomorrow I’m going to dive deep on acquiring small nano flips that won’t make you rich, but will build your confidence and monthly cash flow.

See you then.

-James

​
P.S. We’re opening up the Nano Flips Accelerator program again soon. I’ll let you know when we’re accepting applications.

emails.subject: How to analyze deals in a nanosecond
emails.content:
Okay, so it might take a little bit longer than 1 billionth of a second, but I know I can help you get to 99% certainty in 1/10th of the time.

I looked back at the last decade of research and experience I had available and put together a buyer’s checklist to simplify things for you.

Your checklist is linked at the bottom of this email.

As you’re going through it, here are 3 questions to help you recognize unrealized potential:

  • Are there any opportunities to add monetization channels?
  • Can we improve on existing monetization channels?
  • Can we find ways to increase traffic?

That should give you a head start on finding your next opportunity.

Shane used these strategies on a site he bought for $9.5K and made a massive impact with just a few hours of work.

His site started at $400/month in profit. Pretty solid, but not the kind of number that makes anyone salivate.

He updated the metadata descriptions and added a website speed tool for $15/month.

Six months later, the site was pulling in $900/month.

These simple changes made his website worth $32,400, or an $18k increase in the valuation.

Just like that.

That’s the power of buying a business that’s already successful - you don’t have to sink time into the road from 0-1.

Trust me, going from 1-2 is a lot more fun.

If you do this right, you can buy cash flow with a site that’s already profitable.

It’s the difference between a new coat of paint and adding an addition to the house.

There are over 5,000 new websites listed every day on marketplaces like Acquire and Flippa. You can probably find 1 worth investing in, right?

Keep at it with the research. Click here for your Buyer's Guide.

You’ll be surprised how good you get at spotting potential (and avoiding the trash sites)

Hope this helps you go out there and get after it. Next time we’ll talk in-depth about how to optimize these websites and maximize your ROI.

-James

emails.subject: 🚨 How to avoid buying a scam
emails.content:
Question of the day: How do I know it’s a good business?

We’re just 2 days out from the live workshop where I’ll be sending deals your way…

Like the pet site I mentioned yesterday that’s done $1,065 in the last 30 days, and is PRIMED to make 25% more with a couple quick changes. Just one of a few things I can’t wait to show ya.

Want a 50%+ ROI year on? a 2x? Well the first step is to avoid 99% of the listings you see for sale.

A lot of you have been asking about red flags this week, and the truth is there’s a lot of garbage to sift through on Flippa, Acquire, and all the marketplaces. So here are a few things to keep an eye out for - straight from our internal due diligence checklists:

  1. Fake traffic reporting. Sounds obvious, but don't fall for a scam with a giant spike in traffic, and a super low bounce rate. If they won't let you into analytics or search console...walk away (Ill show yall what that should look like).
  2. New or sketchy sellers: If they don't have reviews or aren't VERY willing to go out of their way to show you who they are? Run
  3. Sketchy backlink profile. If there are hundreds of thousands of shitty links to the site from Chinese or Russian sites...get ready for it to get crushed by a Google update eventually.
  4. Dying industries. All ships rise on high tide baby! Easier to win when a niche is growing than dying.
  5. Looks too good to be true. If it makes $1k a month and "takes no work" and is selling for $5k...you’re getting hustled, run for the hills.

Want to avoid getting ripped off? Join the call on Friday and I’ll show you the good stuff.

And the bad stuff.

And some free stuff - like 1:1 calls with me 🙂

Here’s the link again: https://www.go.nanoflips.com/webinar-registration​

You coming?

-James

Nano Thought

Welcome to the holidays season y'all.

Im here seeing my family in my tiny home town of NYC.

Saas valuations are looking normal on the "nano" side, same with agencies. Ive watched DTC come down to earth, and I think we are about to see a real buying opportunity with content sites.

OK!

Googles most recent update, HCU, (helpful content update), hit many small sites hard. Those sites might not be dead, in fact they might be able to see another day of glory with search traffic, AND crush it on social. Maybe they can drive tons of traffic from Facebook and Pinterest for example.

But since valuations are predicated on trailing profits, many of these sites have had their profits crushed, and my bet is these sellers, realize come January, they they need to drop their valuations, since the last the months their profits have been so down.

This is our opportunity :)

Sites selling for $40k will go for $20k

Sites selling for $200k, will go for $120k

The opportunity on sites that got hit will exist!

This Week’s Opportunities

Favorite Deal this week

​Partially SBA Pre-Qualified: Upwork-Like Platform for Tutoring​

"A 15 year old content site devoted to custom motorcycles, specifically the cafe racer. Huge social following, big and active e-mail subscriber list."

🎉 Here's a site for sale you might be interested in from Flippa.

This is a VERY interesting one. One of the more interesting content sites Ive seen for sale in recent weeks.

  • A 15 year old content site devoted to custom motorcycles, specifically the cafe racer. Huge social following, big and active e-mail subscriber list.
  • Huge social following.
  • Large e-mail subscriber list of highly engaged readers.
  • Content is submit by builders and posted by VA. Very low operational overhead.
  • Site is monetized via adsense, adthrive, amazon and impact

The reason I find it interesting is it is has been around forever. It has survived all the big Google updates this year, it is based on a niche and excited group, it can be turned into a real little media company, and its UNDERMONETIZED!

The magic here is going directly to brands and selling full on ad packages with a media kit.

Lets look at an example, of a package that could be put together and then sold directly to advertisers, not through an ad network:

One month Ad Campaign

  • 4 Sponsored posts (editorial style coverage or product reviews of their products, on the website) - $2000 value
  • 1 Month of Banner ad across all pages of site, 150k impressions - $1500 Value
  • 1 Full Email Blast - $2000 Value
  • 4x Sponsorship of weekly newsletter - $2000 Value
  • 4 Shout out on socials - $500 value

Total Value of Package: $8000

Total Cost to buy: $5000

This would be reasonable guys, a little work of growing the newsletter etc, and then reaching out directly to advertisers would make this totally doable.

How would you find advertisers?

  • Google Cafe Racers and see who is advertising on Google Ads for keywords
  • Check websites to see who is advertising on display ads on sites
  • Find a meet up or conference and buy the list of sponsors from it
  • this is just 3 ideas off the top of my head

Put together a list of 20+ brands in the space to get the ball rolling, and put together a little ad rate kit with Canva FOR FREE, and start reaching out!

How to reach out and sell?

  • Make your CRM of people to reach out to in excel/sheets/or notion
  • Use tools like Apollo.io and LinkedIn Sales Navigator to find the contact info of people at the brands you want to sell to
  • Start reaching out asking if they would like to advertise

ITS THAT SIMPLE. I KNOW BECAUSE IVE DONE OVER $1M OF REVENUE THIS WAY

Now this would mean this site was making $6500+ a month if you sold 1 ad package a month. And btw you could discount it more, or sell multi month packages. Once you run through the 20 advertisers start all over again :)

Let's look at what it does to valuation though, currently the site is at about $35k. Maybe the site goes up to $40-50k over the month its listed.

If you could make these changes at a 36x monthly profit multiple, the site would be worth...

$200k+ on a flip

But this doesn't feel like a flip to me. If everything checked out about the site, and it was as good as it seems at first glance, you could probably drastically increase traffic.

And turn it into a small little media brand, making $1M a year. With a multi million dollar exit one day.

Other Businesses This Week

Here is a little breakdown of some of the listings we see on the marketplaces and brokers in the media space. This includes newsletters, content sites, and more.

Some require a little love and TLC from the right buyer to run them, and some are just cranking away out of the box :)

Agencies

​B2B Growth Marketing Agency - 7- Year- Old B2B focused marketing and copywriting business. High margin, turn-key business with a full team in place.

Content Sites

​Image Tools - Profitable passive income internet business with high-profit margins and strong online presence. Ready for a new owner to take it to the next level

​

As always...do your own due diligence, the above is based off of what we see as an opportunity from the info provided in the listing and some light due diligence, not a deep dive. It just one of many scenarios that could play out and its up to you to do your own due diligence and see if this makes sense for you!

​
​Thought Leader Theater

Every week we take a look at a video or podcast from myself or a thought leader in the space

This week let's take a look How Pieter Levels Makes $2.7M/Year With 0 Employees...

​

​

What’s on the episode?

  1. Get ready for an engaging listen as Pieter Levels joins My First Million
  2. He compares it to being the center of attention in a club and emphasizes the value of genuine connections over shallow interactions. He also talks about the importance of balancing a hectic work life with personal time, health, and meaningful relationships.
  3. Pieter delves into his diverse range of projects, including innovative tools like a QR menu creator and an inflation tracker, and Rebase for CI development. Listen for his candid take on work ethic and authenticity, possibly influenced by his European roots. HE DOES IT ALL
  4. The conversation takes a turn to discuss Pieter's financial journey, particularly during the pandemic. He shares how his earnings soared from under a million to $2.7 million annually, thanks to the rising trend in nomadic lifestyles. His experience offers valuable insights into seizing opportunities during changing times.
  5. Finally, Pieter touches on his minimalist lifestyle choices and investment strategies, including his involvement in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum. He talks about the importance of living simply, focusing on quality living, and being mindful about revealing personal wealth, offering a unique perspective on success and security.

Thanks yall; see ya soon!

emails.subject: 🌊 How To Turn 20 hours of work into $16k buying a Saas
emails.content:
Ok it's 2024 y'all, time to buy a business!

I did a little piece on X (Twitter on this the other day) that you can see here But really thought that it was an important breakdown to share with you all in an email.

Its VERY important to understand that once you have the right tool

You can look at any business and know how to improve it, and if it's worth your time.

Lets look at one of the frame works for this :

Ok so you decided to finally do it & you're going to buy an online business!

But your biggest fear...is how to grow it Well, all methods of traffic generation work...

  • Cold email
  • Organic Social
  • Paid Social
  • SEO
  • Paid Search
  • Display

All of it...but what your job as an entrepreneur if you build a buy a business, to do, is to figure out which one of those channels is worth pushing on

Lets look at an example Ok so maybe you buy a small saas - lets say its a CRM for agency owners, that you found on Acquire.com

It costs $197 a month for customers and you can see the average life time value of a customer is $3940 since on average a customer uses it for 20 months before cancelling

For now, lets ignore the COGS of the software, and say that means you can spend $4000 to acquire a customer and still make money!

Thats exciting

A quick search in Ahrefs lets you find some keywords that you think your new business you bought can rank for. It already has authority and a decent DR since someone else already launched it and it, so you decide SEO could be a good route here.

Thats one growth lever pulled, but you realize that it could take a couple months to rank, and the search volume isn't great for the keywords youre finding You DEF want to create the content and go after those keywords, but you also want to ramp this up and start getting more results and growth for this business you have bought

So you start thinking about what the other channels are

You dont have the budget to spend $20k a month on paying an agency to run ads for you as is. Maybe the retainer is $3500 a month + % of your ad spend and you really need to spend $10k+ a month they tell you to see what works and test campaigns

You decide you can learn some media buying, and save that testing for when you have more budget, or you have your organic SEO traffic built up and you can retarget them.

So you keep going down the list, thinking

"what is another type of traffic I can try?"

You get to cold emailing...

"Hmm ok for a couple hundred bucks a month, I can get something like listkit or apollo going and start emailing agency owners and DMing them on Twitter and LinkedIn"

For a few hundred dollars a month in cost, you realize that you can get 20 calls booked, and can close 4 of them on a trial.

Up front this is only $800 you bring in month one, but knowing your old CLTV (customer lifetime value) of $4000, we now realize that effort is worth $16k to you...

As a part time effort this starts to look very worth it

Worth it enough that you could hire an SDR (sales person) in the future, and justify paying them $3k a month + commission

I think you are starting to see how this can work.

But its not always that cold emailing is the answer.

SEO is the only answer that works for ALL online businesses

emails.subject: 🌊 Revolutionize Your Businesses Workflow: How to Crush it after you buy a biz
emails.content:
So you bought a business...but how do you manage your time?

So over the years, I've done everything from juggling handfuls of clients at once, to working 80 hours a week for years straight on one business before we finally sold it for just over $30M.

Through nothing but pure trial and error, I discovered several simple life-changing things that helped me stay productive, and I wanted to cover a few of them for you today.

So whether you're a full-time entrepreneur, someone working on a side hustle, or you just bought your first biz. Take 2 mins to check out what worked for me through all the ups and downs. Instead of making a 5000-word email about all the complex things, let's just look 2 today.

Let's Dive in

Time Blocking...and the Pomodoro technique - and combining them

The Art of Time Blocking

What is Time Blocking? Time blocking is when you divide your day into blocks of time, each dedicated to accomplishing a specific task or group of tasks. If you have a job and are buying an online business as a side hustle THIS WILL BE KEY!

How to actually make Time Blocking work?

Start by listing your tasks for the week. Then, allocate specific time blocks for these tasks in your calendar. Remember, the key is to be realistic about how much time each task will take and to include breaks and buffer times.

Here is a normal calendar

Now here is a time-blocked one

This may seem crazy for many of you, but for those who NEED structure (like me) to get tedious work done, it's a game changer.

So this is great, right? You start with a todo list (my favorite app for that is https://todoist.com/)

Then you can place your tasks in your calendar with time blocking, but how do we stay productive DURING that time?

This is where the Pomodoro Technique comes in...

Developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s, the Pomodoro Technique uses a timer to break work into intervals, traditionally 25 minutes in length (you can make it longer or shorter), separated by short breaks.

Each interval is known as a Pomodoro, named after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer Cirillo used.

Choose a task, set a timer for 25 minutes, and work until the timer rings. Then take a 5-minute break. After four Pomodoros, take a longer break of 15-30 minutes.

I know this sounds silly...but it works.

If you have articles to write for SEO...this changes the game, same with creating ad copy, or emails. Anything that you need to just PLUG in and get work done, this is super helpful for.

If you need a simple rec? Here ya go https://pomodor.app/​

Or on my phone I have one called "Focus Tomato"

But tbh...you can just crush it with an alarm from your phone.

Now to tie it all together? The most basic way to be super productive as a small online business owner?

1. Make a To-Do List

  • First things first, jot down everything you need to tackle. This list is your roadmap for the day or week ahead. (I can't function without a todo list)

2. Outline Your Day with Time Blocks

  • Take that to-do list and start carving out your day into time blocks. Assign each task or group of tasks to specific blocks of time.

3. Implement the Pomodoro Technique Within Each Block

  • Within these time blocks, use the Pomodoro Technique. Set a timer for focused work (like 25 minutes), followed by a short break. This works yall...trust me.

4. Adjust Pomodoro Duration for Intense Tasks

  • Got a task that needs deep focus? Flex the rules a bit. Extend your Pomodoro to 50 minutes for those big, brainy tasks.

Simple. Done.

A bit of a different email but I think will be useful for many.

The truth is, I can tell you all the ways to improve sites, and we can find great businesses for sale. But half the battle truly is mindset and mental frameworks.

Good luck out there yall!

emails.subject: 🚀 Anything is possible - $100k Months and $1M Ones
emails.content:
The Opportunity of Internet Businesses - We are still early

Ok Gang!

All the emails I’ve sent recently have been very structured and really just looked at internet businesses for sale and how to improve them and run them.

But belief and mindset is just as important as the tools we have.

So I wanted to rant for a second about how anything is possible.

I genuinely do believe that Internet businesses are an opportunity for anyone in this world who wants to take advantage of them.

Anyone with internet access can own one. It’s truly an opportunity that never existed before. Entrepreneurship was guarded throughout all of capitalism until the rise of the Internet - and we’re still incredibly early on.

You once needed to physically be in one location, and to risk everything to build or buy a business. This is simply no longer true.

The Mindset of Possibility

I know it's cheesy y'all....but I want to take a moment and talk about how really anything is possible - that we are really the only ones stopping ourselves from moving forward.

If you can make $1 online (and I promise you every single one of you can), you can make a million dollars online.

Will a cheesy screenshot from one of mine help you believe it? Here ya go:

I realized recently that I hang on in the corner of the internet where people talk about $100k months, $200k months, or even million-dollar months.

This is a bubble. Not because it’s not possible, but it’s a bubble because people don’t see how it’s possible.

For context, I got kicked out of school so much that I went to 5 highschools...and I dropped out of college. With 8 credits left to this day.

Im not special, all of you can do the same.

A Grounding Interaction

Recently, while buying some groceries after a long week, I had an interaction with the gentleman bagging for me:

  • A kind, nice guy in his early 20s
  • He asked me what I would be doing on Saturday night
  • I said, “It’s been a long week, my man. I’m probably just gonna go play some PS5 and cook and relax.”
  • He said, “So sick. I’ve been saving up for a PS5.”

It was a reminder that I live in this bubble and that I should have gratitude for the amazing life that internet businesses have granted me - where the concept of saving up for a PS5 seems crazy.

I wrote about it on Twitter:

James Camp 🛠,🛠
@JamesonCamp
This corner of the internet is a bubble We don’t see the real world. $100k+ months sound normal to us Yesterday buying groceries, the guy bagging them asked me my plans I said “it’s been a long week just going to go home and cook and play some PS5” His reply: “that sounds… https://twitter.com/i/web/status/1769420687226400932
10:49 AM • Mar 17, 2024
4
Retweets
380
Likes
Read 29 replies
​

The Key: Gratitude and Risk

If youre still in the camp of thinking $10k, $100k, or even $1M months from your laptop are impossible. This is for you.

Recognize that many many things are possible - that anything is possible actually. People much dumber than me, make much much more than I do.

I am still my own worst enemy and still work on my mindset every day. It's a never-ending process.

So I want to take this moment to recognize it’s important to have obscene gratitude for what we all already have.

Clearly, things could be worse, no matter what. In my experience... gratitude seems to be one of the keys to happiness.

Anything is possible. Be grateful for what you already have. But there is always more you can get. Balancing these 2 beliefs is key.

Whether you own a blog doing $100 a month, a software business doing a million a month, or you’re sending rockets into space like Elon.

We’re here on this planet one time and one time and one time only from my perspective at least.

So while you’re here, take advantage of that.

Take the risk, take the swing.

The only way to escape mediocrity is to take a risk. And if that’s not for you, that’s okay.

But if you want more, if you don’t want to just be saving up for a PS5, then you have to take swings. I promise you anything within the laws of physics is possible for all of you.

emails.content:
The Optimist's Edge: How to Find and Grow Your Ideal Business

Ok Gang!

I recently came across a quote that really REALLY hit home:

"Pessimists sound smart, optimists get rich."

This simple yet profound statement truly truly hits on the mindset needed to succeed in buying or building a business.

As someone who is "money and traffic agnostic," I believe that there's a perfect business opportunity out there for everyone. And that no one business type is better than another.

Whether you're interested in content sites, e-commerce brands, software businesses, or agencies, the key is to find the right fit for your unique skills, interests, and resources.

Nano Flips Special Offer

This is a sweet little deal right here. Im often looking for insights from other operators in the market that I respect. Olly Richards is one of them..

​Olly Richards put together a giant, 117-page case study about how he’s scaled his business to $10M.

When he sent it to me I have to admit I was pretty impressed at the depth.

Seems relevant not just for creators and coaches but anyone looking for creative solutions to scale with a super lean team. If you're buying, building, or operating sites, it's def worth a download.

This is a bubble. Not because it’s not possible, but it’s a bubble

​Download Here​

Content Sites: Still Thriving

Despite the ups and downs of Google updates, content sites can still be incredibly profitable.

And Google isnt dead y'all, we do SEO for several clients, and every single one of them is currently doing well. (trending up - knock on wood it stays that way)

Take, for example, my friends Colin and Oren have a website in the art space that's performing exceptionally for example:

Colin Landforce 🛠
@landforce
This is a content site in the fine art niche, it's rarely touched and mostly longtail keywords. I keep seeing tweets about SEO being dead but this thing is just plugging away and growing every month. 🤷‍♂️ lol @orenmeetsworld

​

But many are afraid of Google these days. Id be lying to you to say the last 12 months wasn't some of the largest google updates Ive seen in a decade. Doesn't mean its dead though!

Diversifying Traffic Sources

While we still get a lot of traffic from Google, it's essential to diversify into other channels as well. Nothing works exactly the same forever, so the trick is to be nimble and keep your finger on the pulse of what's working and what's not.

Anyone who has been seen my case study on my biggest site ever, MJObserver.com (sold in 2020, then the acquirer gutted it for parts, sold off again and now dead)

Knows that a MASSIVE amount of our traffic came from Facebook and Email. (and was doing $2M a year or so)

The game has always been about diversification in the media space, just now more than ever!

Opportunity in Struggling Websites

There's also a massive opportunity in buying websites that have been hit by Google updates. You can acquire a struggling website and leverage its existing content to drive traffic through other channels. Hasib Alic touched on it here:

Hasib Alic
@HasibStrevio
There's a huge opportunity right now: 1. Buy a site with solid content that has been affected by the recent Google updates for almost nothing 2. Create a Facebook page, buy followers through Facebook like campaigns, and post content there 3. Make your money back in 3-6 months… https://twitter.com/i/web/status/1774549645177360422

​
  • Pinterest: Many people are crushing it with Pinterest-based content today - a site with tons of content means you just need to make pins for it (working on a training for you all dont worry)
  • and then of course, you should be gathering up that traffic from all those channels, getting them on an email list, and OWNING the traffic so you can get to your readers again and again

Embracing Optimism

Remember the quote from earlier? "Pessimists sound smart, optimists get rich."

This is incredibly true.

You can either be the person who always finds fault in everything or the person with a positive outlook who takes calculated risks.

Risk is inherently tied to reward, and with strategic thinking, you can increase your chances of success.

Finding Your Perfect Business

Take a sec to step back and think about the type of business you'd like to run:

  • One that fits your skill sets (this can be learned)
  • One that fits within your budget (you can get creative)
  • One that interests you (this one isnt as easy to fix as the others)

We've helped people buy e-commerce brands, agencies, content sites, theme pages, and software businesses. There's no one-size-fits-all solution, but I promise you, the right business is out there for you.

Success in business is about finding the right fit for you while maintaining an optimistic outlook - not always easy...but key.

Be open to opportunities, stay positive, and don't be afraid to take calculated risks.

As the saying goes, "Pessimists sound smart, optimists get rich."

With the right mindset and strategy, you can find and build the perfect business that aligns with your goals and passions.

Just gotta be willing to take a risk and dive in

Thanks y'all!

emails.subject: 💸 The Surprising Truth About Scaling A Business
emails.content:
The Secret to Scaling An Acquisition: Finding Your Sweet Spot

Ok Gang!

I was working with an entrepreneur that I've done some coaching with who runs small agency doing $25k a month, and we had a deep dive about scale. I think he can take his business to about $2M a year, but not much higher without ripping his hair out and changing his margins.

It made me think, I really need to share this with the Nano Flips crew.

I've spent years banging my head against the wall, trying to force businesses to grow into the mid-seven or low eight-figure range.

But here's the surprising truth I've learned: not every business is meant to scale, and that's okay.

The Sweet Spot

Many small internet businesses find their groove at a few thousand, tens of thousands, or even hundreds of thousands of dollars per month. While some may have the potential to become nine-figure giants, many won't – and that's perfectly fine.

I've found that the sweet spot of maxed out on part time for many, or not truly going through growing pains is $100k-500k a year.

This realization has shaped my approach to entrepreneurship. It's why I in the past have built portfolios of businesses rather than putting all my efforts into scaling a single company often.

The Hidden Costs of Forced Scaling

Trying to force a business to grow often leads to increased expenses, higher operational costs, and added complexity. The secret is to understand the unique qualities of each business and find its optimal size.

DONT MAKE YOUR LIFE HARDER THAN IT NEEDS TO BE

Sometimes the answer is to delgate to an operator, make a little less on that business, and move on to build or buy another.

Celebrating My Birthday with an Exciting Announcement

Last week, I turned 36! I know...Im getting old.

It was a simple but meaningful birthday, filled with small joys and a reminder of my long-term vision for Nano Flips.

I want to make Nano Flips a key component of a larger business that will allow me to raise hundreds of millions of dollars to acquire even bigger companies in the future.

And in honor of my birthday, I'm taking a big step towards that goal.

Introducing the Next Nano Flips Cohort

We will be helping 20 individuals find the perfect business, navigate the acquisition process, and develop a tailored growth strategy – whether that's running the business for cash flow or flipping it for an exit.

We will start the next one cohort soon....

We have had over 100 people make their first acquisitions in past ones. Ranging from content sites, to small agencies, ecom brands, and micro saas.

Later this week, I'll send out another email with listings of businesses for sale that caught my eye.

Hey [Name],

​

Have you ever found yourself stuck at a crossroads, paralyzed by the fear of making the wrong move? I know I have. Just last week, I was agonizing over which direction to take my business in. I felt like I needed to have it all figured out before I could take a single step.

But then I remembered a piece of advice that changed everything: Action produces information. We don't have to have all the answers up front. In fact, the only way to get those answers is by taking imperfect action and learning as we go.

​

Think about it - when was the last time you made a decision that didn't require some course-correction along the way? Every choice we make is based on the best information we have at that moment. And the only way to get more clarity is by moving forward, gathering data, and adjusting our path as needed.

​

As the saying goes, "A good plan violently executed now is better than a perfect plan executed next week." So don't let the fear of imperfection keep you stuck. Embrace the power of imperfect action. Take that tiny step forward, even if you're not 100% sure it's the "right" one. Trust that the insights you gain will light the way to your next best move.

​

I've started putting this into practice in my own life, and the results have been game-changing. Instead of overanalyzing every decision, I'm focusing on taking consistent, imperfect action. And you know what? I'm learning faster, growing quicker, and feeling more energized than ever before.

So the next time you find yourself at a crossroads, remember: Action is the antidote to anxiety. Forward motion, even if it's clumsy at first, will create the clarity you crave. You've got this.

emails.subject: 💸 The $100k mistake too many first-time business buyers make
emails.content:
The Money Mirage

Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

Just got back from two weeks on the East Coast – wining and dining with Mom at Per Se (3 Michelin Stars) in NYC.

Then escaping to the Catskills for some mountain air with friends.

All while my businesses kept humming along, managed from my trusty laptop.

It got me thinking about why we're really in this game of entrepreneurship.

Here's the truth bomb: It's not about the money.

Shocking, right?

But stick with me, because this realization could save you from a $100k mistake I see too many first-time business buyers make.

Money's just a tool. A means to an end. But too often, I watch folks get starry-eyed over revenue numbers and profit margins, forgetting to ask the most crucial question:

What's the life you're actually trying to create?

Nano Flips Special Offer

I've been around the block, and 90% of the info you see online is total garbage...but thats FAR from true when it comes to my friend Olly.

​Olly Richards put together a giant, 117-page case study about how he’s scaled his business to $10M.

It's sort of a no brainer for anyone wanting to buy a business and scale it, or honestly? Scale one from scratch.

Its a no brainer for anyone trying to build a lean team, especially creators and coaches. If you're buying, building, or operating sites, it's def worth a download.

​Download Here​

The Real ROI: Return on Life

Because here's the kicker – a business that makes you a million bucks but chains you to a desk 24/7 isn't a win.

It's a gilded cage.

I've seen it happen. An entrepreneur buys a "successful" business, only to realize it's sucking the life out of them. They're working longer hours, missing family dinners, canceling vacations. All for a bigger bank balance they never have time to enjoy.

Don't fall into that trap.

Aligning Acquisitions with Aspirations

The real victory? A business that aligns with the life you want to lead.

Maybe it's:

  • A content site you can manage in 10 hours a week
  • A SaaS tool that solves a problem you're passionate about
  • A newsletter that writes about your favorite hobby
  • An ecom brand that Does $10M a year top line

The numbers matter, sure. But they're not the whole story.

Do you want to have a side hustle that pays for your apartment? Pays for your kids school? Or do you want to build an empire.

We all want different things, what do you want?

Lifestyle by Design

So before you dive into your next deal, get crystal clear on your endgame. What does "success" look like for you, beyond the bank balance?

Ask yourself:

  1. How many hours a week do I actually want to work?
  2. Where do I want to be able to work from?
  3. What kind of problems do I want to solve?
  4. How much time do I want for family, hobbies, or travel?

Because when you're clear on that, you'll know exactly what kind of business to look for – and what to pass on.

The Decision That Shapes Your Future

Buying a business isn't just a financial transaction. It's a life decision.

Choose wisely.

Here's a quick exercise to drive this home:

Imagine it's five years from now, and you're living your ideal life. What does your day look like? Where are you? What are you doing? How does your business fit into that picture?

Get specific. Write it down.

Now, as you evaluate potential businesses to buy, ask yourself: Does this business bring me closer to that vision, or push me further away?

Growth Strategy

  • Instagram Outreach:
    • Target Poshmark influencers and power sellers
    • Daily task: Engage with 20 profiles, personalizing each interaction and offering a free trial

    • Potential to rapidly scale the user base
  • Content Marketing:

    • Drive organic traffic to a landing page
    • Capitalize on the visual nature of Poshmark on Pinterest
  • Direct Outreach:
    • Use hashtags like #PoshmarkReseller to find potential customers

Email Marketing:

  • Build an email list with a lead magnet (e.g., "10 Tips for Poshmark Success")

The Numbers

Assuming we add 15 new customers per month, with an average 3-month retention:

  • Month 1: $400 + (15 * $20) = $700
  • Month 3: $2,260
  • Month 6: $3,100
  • Month 12: $3,400 (accounting for churn)

  3. Create a simple content calendar for social media posts
  4. Reach out to 5-10 Poshmark influencers for potential partnerships
  5. Optimize the Chrome extension store listing for better organic discovery

Potential Exit

At a 3x annual profit multiple:

  • Current value: ~$12,000
  • Potential value after 12 months: ~$122,400

Total return including profits: ~$150,000

Bottom Line

For someone familiar with Poshmark or interested in e-commerce tools, this could be an excellent opportunity. With a modest time investment of 30 minutes per day, you could potentially turn a $12,000 investment into a $100,000+ asset within a year.

This isnt even including trying to increase organic search traffic or running and paid ads.

Remember, the key to success with these smaller acquisitions is consistent, focused effort. It's not about making huge changes, but about steady, incremental improvements that compound over time.

emails.description: no promo - cohort presale call out
emails.content:
The Power of Strategic Investment: Fueling Your Entrepreneurial Journey

Hey{{ subscriber.first_name }},

Ever heard the phrase "It takes money to make money"?

It's more than just a catchy saying. It's a fundamental principle of business growth and personal development.

But here's the crucial part many miss: It's not about spending recklessly. It's about investing strategically - in your business, in your skills, in your future.

A Lesson in Strategic Investment

Let me share a recent experience that illustrates this principle.

I recently acquired a SaaS business. The product was solid, the potential enormous.

But there was a glaring issue: the website and landing page were severely underperforming.

I faced a choice:

  1. Keep the site as is and hope for the best
  2. Invest in a complete overhaul

I chose option 2.

The investment? $2,500.

This might seem frustrating since I already just handed over a good chunk of money for the business itself. But I recognized it for what it was: an investment in future growth.

This $2,500 wasn't just about a new design. It was about:

  • Boosting conversion rates
  • Enhancing user experience
  • Increasing customer trust
  • Ultimately, driving more revenue

In the world of entrepreneurship, sometimes you need to take calculated risks to unlock real potential.

In fact, I'll probably spend another $5k getting it to a place I want it before relaunch.

But the plan is for it then to be netting $10-20k a month.

Clearly...the investment

The Wisdom of Warren Buffett

Consider this insight from Warren Buffett:

"The most important investment you can make is in yourself."

This applies whether you're a seasoned business owner or just starting your entrepreneurial journey. Your skills, your knowledge, your business - these are all extensions of you and your vision.

Are you treating them as your most crucial investments?

Investing in Yourself: The Foundation of Success

Maybe you don't own a business yet. That's okay. The principle of strategic investment still applies.

Consider these possibilities:

  • That mentorship you've been thinking of buying
  • The public speaking course that could elevate your career
  • The industry conference that could expand your network

Each of these is an investment in your future entrepreneurial success.

Remember: Every successful business owner started somewhere. Usually, that somewhere was investing in themselves.

The 48-Hour Challenge

Here's a challenge to push you toward growth:

  1. Identify ONE area of your business or personal skill set that needs significant improvement.
  2. Research what it would cost (in time or money) to elevate it to excellence.
  3. If the investment makes you pause, you're on the right track. Growth often feels uncomfortable.
  4. Make a decision within 48 hours.

Why 48 hours? Because analysis paralysis is the enemy of progress. Trust your instincts, do your research, and take action.

Real-World Examples of Strategic Investment

Let's look at some inspiring examples:

  1. Sara Blakely invested her life savings of $5,000 to start Spanx. Today, it's a billion-dollar company.
  2. Jeff Bezos left a high-paying job to start Amazon in his garage. His initial investment? About $10,000.
  3. Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia bought air mattresses to rent out their apartment, leading to the birth of Airbnb.

These entrepreneurs didn't just spend money. They invested strategically in their visions.

The Bottom Line

Remember, in the journey of entrepreneurship, playing it too safe is often the riskiest move of all. Strategic investments - in your business, your skills, your future - are what separate the dreamers from the doers.

You're here because you're not content with the ordinary. You're here because you see the potential for something greater.

So take that step. Make that investment. Your future self will thank you.

Ready to Take the Leap? Join Our Next Cohort

Speaking of investments in your future, I've got some exciting news:

We're opening up our next Internet Equities cohort in October!

This is your chance to get hands-on guidance in buying and improving your first side hustle or internet business. We've helped countless entrepreneurs just like you take that crucial first step into business ownership.

Want to be at the front of the line?

Reply to this email with "Add me to the waitlist" and you'll get early access when spots open up.

Trust me, these spots go fast.

Remember, every successful entrepreneur started somewhere. This could be your somewhere.

Here's to your success and bold moves,

James

Growth Strategy

Just got back from a crazy productive strategy session with one of our portfolio companies. Hadn't visited them since we bought them 3 months ago, and let me tell you - the energy in that room was ELECTRIC.

Why? Because we're about to roll out some changes that could double their revenue in the next 30 days.

Look, I see a TON of SaaS businesses for sale right now. Most are solid companies doing $5k-20k MRR, but their owners are just collecting checks without pushing growth.

That's exactly why we bought this one - great product, loyal customers, but missing some obvious growth levers that we're about to pull.

Most founders are out there chasing new customers like it's their job (ok, it kind of is), but they're missing the goldmine sitting right in front of them.

Strategy #1: The "Magic Upgrade" Formula

Y'all, this is literally free money sitting on the table.

Quick story: I was consulting on a saas acquisition last year, the first thing we noticed was they had ZERO premium features. Just one plan, one price, everybody gets everything.

Here's what we are planning :

  1. Added white glove service offering
  2. Created a "Pro" tier with some features customers had been begging for
  3. Hit existing customers with an irresistible offer: "Upgrade in the next 48 hours, get 30% off forever"

Result? 20% revenue boost in two weeks. Not even kidding.

Pro tip: When we're looking at SaaS businesses to buy now, this is the first thing we check - are there obvious premium features missing? That's instant profit waiting to happen.

Strategy #2: The "We Want You Back" Campaign

This one's wild, y'all. Most SaaS businesses (including ones we buy) treat churned customers like ex-girlfriends - never to be spoken to again. Big mistake. HUGE.

Here's what we do day 1 after any acquisition:

  1. Pull everyone who cancelled in the last 6 months
  2. Send them: "New ownership, new features, special 'welcome back' offer"
  3. Hit them with an offer they can't refuse: "Come back now, get 3 months at 50% off"

True story: One client B2B SaaS companies got 15% of their churned users back with this exact playbook. That's like printing money.

BTW - when we're doing due diligence on a potential purchase, we ALWAYS ask for the churned customer list. Most sellers think we're just checking churn rates. Nope. We're counting our future customers.

Strategy #3: The "Price Right" Revolution

This one's gonna hurt a little, but trust me - most SaaS businesses are undercharging. Including that project management tool we just strategized with.

Quick gut check:

  • When's the last time they raised prices? (In this case...never had)
  • Are the best customers saying "this is too cheap"? (We had dozens of support tickets saying exactly this)
  • Are they charging based on actual value or just what competitors charge?

Here's what we're rolling out for our recent acquisition:

  1. 10% price increase for new signups
  2. White glove offering like we have implemented for clients
  3. New premium tier with those features everyone keeps requesting

Looking at another SaaS to buy right now - there seems to be some good opportunity. It's like finding money in the couch cushions.

BONUS MOVE: The Partnership Play

This one's magic: Find a complementary SaaS and bundle up.

We're actually in talks right now to buy a CRM tool specifically because it would pair perfectly with Off Market deal finding saas. Bundle them together? That's instant value creation.

The Bottom Line

Y'all, these strategies work whether you're buying a SaaS or growing one you already own. I've seen it firsthand. But here's the thing - you gotta move FAST. The market isn't getting any easier, and your competition isn't sleeping.

emails.subject: 🎯 Stop Planning Your Goals Like An Amateur
emails.content:
🎯 The Ultimate Guide to Goal Setting (And Why You Need to Start Now)

Hey Gang!

Sitting in my apartment in NYC, coffee in hand, watching the city lights flicker across the skyline. It's got me thinking...

You know what most people do? They wait until January 1st, hungover and groggy, to start thinking about their goals for the year.

That's like showing up to a race just as the gun goes off - no warm-up, no game plan, shoes barely tied.

We're gonna be smarter than that.

The Art of Strategic Goal Setting

Real talk? When I first started, I was winging it hard. My "goals" were about as solid as a pizza box in the rain.

"Make more money." "Grow the business." "Work harder."

Sound familiar?

Then I learned something that changed everything: The power of cascading goals.

Breaking it Down: The Goal Pyramid

Here's how I think about it now (and trust me, this works):

Yearly Goals: This is your North Star. The big, scary dream that makes your stomach do a little flip when you think about it. Not some weak "I want to make more money" stuff. I'm talking "I'm going to 10x my business and help 100,000 people" level goals.

Quarterly Goals: Think of these as your checkpoints. Each one gets you roughly 25% closer to that yearly goal. They keep you honest.

Monthly Goals: Now we're getting real. These are your stepping stones. Clear targets that stack up to those quarterly wins.

Weekly Goals: Your battle plan. What specific moves are you making this week?

Daily Goals: This is where the magic happens. The small wins that compound into something massive.

The Holiday Paradox (And Why I Changed My Mind)

Let me get vulnerable for a second.

I used to be that guy. Laptop out during Christmas dinner, firing off emails between bites of turkey, treating December 25th like any other Monday.

Want to know what that got me?

Burnout. Soul-crushing, creativity-killing burnout.

And a whole lot of moments with family that I can't get back.

These days? I'm a lot smarter about it. December is sacred time for:

  • Light strategic planning
  • Real family time
  • Actually recharging (not just saying I'm recharging while scrolling Twitter)
  • Getting my head right for what's going to be an absolute monster 2025
  • Building up that energy for a January launch

Your 2025 Blueprint: The Smart Way

Here's what I want you to do (yeah, this is homework):

  1. Block out 30 minutes this week. Non-negotiable. Make it happen.
  2. Write down your massive 2025 goal. Make it so big it scares you. If you're not slightly uncomfortable, double it.
  3. Break that beast into 4 quarterly missions. Be specific. Be measurable.
  4. Map out January's key moves. Just January. We'll deal with February when it comes.
  5. Then? Close the laptop. Seriously.

Just yesterday, I was working with one of my 1:1 clients on this exact process. He came in thinking he'd grow maybe 25% next year. After our planning session? We found a couple major opportunities in his business he was completely overlooking. Now he's on track to potentially 2x by Q3. Sometimes you just need another set of eyes to spot what you're too close to see.

Because here's the truth: The time between now and New Year's? It's not for grinding.

It's for being present. For recharging. For remembering why we're building these empires in the first place.

The Winning Formula

I've tested both approaches (so you don't have to):

Grinding through the holidays = Short-term gains, long-term burnout Strategic planning + intentional rest = Sustainable success

Merry Christmas & Happy Holidays!

Whether you're celebrating Christmas, Hanukkah, or just enjoying the winter vibes - I want you to know I'm grateful for this community we're building.

Hug your people. Eat the cookies. Watch the cheesy movies. The hustle will be there in January, and you'll be ready to crush it with fresh energy and clear vision.

Your 2025 is going to be absolutely insane. I can feel it.

But first? Enjoy these moments. They're what it's all about.

Hit reply and let me know: What's that big, scary 2025 goal looking like? I read every email, for real.

Thanks y'all!

James

emails.content:
Ok Gang!

Ever wonder how some businesses seem to get thousands of users without spending a dime on ads?

I just saw this great tweet that broke down exactly how one founder did it - and it reminded me of all the old-school growth tactics we used to use.

Michael Davidson
@mike_revenue
Bro if you’re starting a SaaS You can literally get 100s If not 1000s of users FOR FREE I did this for my first few SaaS startups and got 1000s of waitlist users Here’s the secret: FB groups Once you know who your ICP is You can literally finds dozens of groups Of your… https://x.com/i/web/status/1892065499258790368
8:15 PM • Feb 18, 2025
50
Retweets
1123
Likes
Read 42 replies
​

Listen, this isn't just some random growth hack.

This is the real deal.

We've used variations of this strategy to grow everything from media businesses to software companies.

I remember doing this exact thing with one of our investment news websites - we'd join Facebook groups focused on different public cannabis companies and investing opportunities. Not to spam links, but to actually share market insights and analysis. Within weeks, our traffic was exploding.

Did the same thing with a sports media business too. We'd dive into NFL team fan groups and college football communities, sharing real analysis and starting genuine conversations. Before we knew it, people were sharing our content organically.

Here's the exact blueprint:

Step 1: Find Your Watering Holes Find 20+ Facebook groups where your ideal customers hang out. Look for groups with at least 10k members. That's your goldmine.

Step 2: The Two-Week Warm-Up Spend two weeks just being helpful. Comment on posts. Share insights. Build a presence. No selling. Not yet.

Step 3: The DM Strategy Now here's where it gets interesting. Start reaching out to people individually. Play the beginner card. Ask questions. Let them teach you.

Then casually drop: "Hey, have you heard of [your tool]? My friend showed it to me and I just got on the waitlist..."

The psychology here is brilliant. When someone teaches you something, they become invested in your success.

Want to scale this fast?

Grab 5 VAs from Upwork at $20/day each. Train them on the exact script. Have them sending hundreds of DMs daily.

But here's the thing - most people do it wrong.

They jump in, start spamming their link, and wonder why nobody bites.

The real magic happens when you play the long game.

Every single niche has its own little corner of the internet. Its watering holes. The places where your perfect customers are already hanging out.

Facebook groups. Reddit. Discord. Forums. Slack channels.

I remember when we first started doing this with Craigslist posts years ago. We'd post hundreds of times a day. Each post carefully crafted to seem like a genuine user sharing their experience.

The same principle works everywhere.

Join the communities. Actually help people. Share what you know. Build real connections.

Then - and only then - start mentioning your tool or product.

"Hey, I found this thing that helped me with that problem you mentioned..."

"I got an extra trial slot if you want to check it out..."

"My friend showed me this tool that does exactly what you're looking for..."

The Numbers Game: Let's break this down realistically:

  • 500 DMs per day (with 5 VAs)
  • Converting 1 in 200 conversations to a free trial
  • That's 2-3 new customers daily
  • At $97/month? That's $200-300 in new MRR every single day

Is it a grind? Yeah.

Will it scale to $100M? Nah.

But I've watched businesses add $5-10k in monthly recurring revenue just from this approach.

And think about this - that extra $10k in MRR? That could mean $300-400k in enterprise value when you go to sell the business or add it to one you've already bought.

The best part? It costs nothing but time.

And if you're smart about it (maybe grab a few VAs to help), you can scale it pretty quickly.

Just remember - value first. Always.

Don't be the person spamming links.

Be the person actually helping.

The sales will follow.

Thanks y'all!

James
