emails.subject: 💸 The Side Hustle Trap: Why Smart Entrepreneurs Buy Businesses Instead
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

Last week, I was in Austin for Bitcoin Startup Day, sipping an overpriced cold brew at a trendy coffee shop near the convention center.

That's where I met Mark - a young developer with dark circles under his eyes who recognized me from Twitter.

"I've tried everything," he confessed after we got talking. "Dropshipping, Amazon FBA, day trading crypto... none of it sticks."

I smiled, because I'd heard this story a hundred times before.

The problem wasn't the business models. It was how he approached them.

The Fatal Flaw in Most Side Hustles

The world keeps getting more expensive.

Housing prices? Insane. Inflation? Still biting. Job security? What's that?

So people frantically jump from one "get rich quick" scheme to the next.

But here's what separates the people who build real wealth from those who don't:

They don't chase side hustles. They acquire assets with proven cash flow.

The Graveyard of Abandoned Side Hustles

"Dropshipping is dead!"

I literally had to stop myself from laughing when a 23-year-old "guru" told me this at a conference.

I actually know someone doing over $300,000/month dropshipping specialized equipment.

I know of another entrepreneur pulling in around $40,000/month with a content site in a "boring" niche that hasn't changed in 20 years.

The difference? They didn't invent something new. They bought something that was already working.

The Math That Changes Your Life

Let's break down what happens when you buy a small, established business making $1,000/month and grow it to $3,000/month:

  • That's not just $2,000 more in your pocket each month.
  • That's not just mortgage-payment money.
  • That's $50,000-$100,000 of enterprise value you've created.

Read that again.

When you sell, businesses typically go for 24-50X monthly profit.

So that $2,000/month increase? That's potentially a $100,000 payday when you exit.

All from a business you didn't even have to build from scratch.

The Reality Nobody Talks About

I recently heard about someone whose story really stuck with me:

Three years ago, a woman I'll call Sarah lost her corporate job of 15 years. At 47, she was terrified of starting over.

Instead of panicking, she bought a small Etsy shop making around $1,200/month selling digital planners.

She didn't reinvent the wheel. The business was already working. It had product-market fit. Customers loved it.

From what I understand, she simply improved the marketing, added complementary products, and optimized the operation.

Today, that "side hustle" reportedly generates five figures monthly, and she apparently turned down a substantial acquisition offer.

"I never thought of myself as an entrepreneur," she reportedly said. "I just wanted something stable that I controlled."

The Blueprint for Real Wealth

This isn't about dropshipping vs. SaaS vs. content sites.

It's about the approach:

  1. Find businesses with proven demand (2+ years of sales history)
  2. Look for opportunities others overlook (boring niches win)
  3. Buy the business (often for surprisingly reasonable prices)
  4. Optimize what's already working
  5. Scale methodically
  6. Enjoy the cash flow or flip for a life-changing exit

Whether it's a micro-SaaS tool, an e-commerce brand, or a media site – the formula works if you work it.

Your Next Move

Look around you. The most successful people I know aren't chasing the latest fad on TikTok.

They're quietly buying cash-flowing assets that others have already proven work.

And unlike real estate or stocks, these online businesses are still massively undervalued.

So here's my question for you:

What's stopping you from making your next side hustle your last side hustle?

Hit reply and tell me your biggest obstacle. I read every response.

Thanks y'all!

James

We're opening up 3 slots for one-on-one help finding a business within your budget and putting together a plan to potentially double your revenue in the next 12 months.

Reply with "LAST SIDE HUSTLE" if you're interested.

This Weeks Opportunities

Deals this week

​He Built a $1.6M App Empire Inside Shopify—Without Ads or a Team​

This Shopify-native SaaS does ~$47K/month in profit. The founder spends 2–3 hours a week on it. He's ready to sell.

You could turn this into a $3M+ business with a little pricing strategy, a second product, or even just emailing the customers (yep, that's not happening right now).

Let's get into it:

The Business

It's a bundle of 5 Shopify-native apps for eCom stores: Things like popups, timers, urgency tools, and email capture.

Sold inside the Shopify App Store. Customers discover it while looking for ways to boost sales—built-in demand.

  • 1,900+ active paying users
  • 6 years of history
  • Sticky, utility-based features
  • Recurring subscriptions
  • No paid acquisition

Current Performance

  • MRR: $52,500
  • Profit: $47,000/month
  • Annual Profit: ~$564,000
  • Asking Price: $1.6M
  • Valuation Multiple: ~2.83x profit
  • Team: None

This is what we call a distribution-first SaaS: it wins not by hype or virality, but by being in the right place (Shopify App Store) at the right time (when store owners are looking to grow).

What's the Real Value Here?

Let's get conservative for a second.

  • Assume 5% churn/month
  • That's a 46% annual churn rate
  • You'll need 80-90 new customers a month just to maintain MRR
  • Currently, those come inbound through Shopify—no ad spend, but also no owned growth

That's the hidden weakness: You're at the mercy of Shopify's marketplace unless you layer on your own growth engine.

But here's the opportunity in that:

Upside Plays (With Churn Adjusted)

1. Price Optimization With 1,900 customers and 5% monthly churn, you'd retain roughly 1,025 customers by year-end. If you increase ARPU by $5/month → That's $5,125/mo = $61,500/year = $180,000 in new value at 3x

2. Customer Reactivation + Email Flows With 5% monthly churn, you're losing about 875 customers per year. If you can bring back just 15% of those through reactivation campaigns, that's 131 customers at $30/mo = $3,930/mo MRR → ~$47,160/year → $108,000 in valuation at 3x

3. Cross-Sell or Launch a Second App With your 1,025 retained customers, a 10% uptake on a new $20/mo app = 102 x $20 = $2,040/mo = $24,480/year = $137K in value at 3x

4. Add 80 new customers/month outside of Shopify If your CAC is $50 and they stick for 10 months at $30/mo:

  • Value per customer = $300
  • 80/month = $24K/mo → $288K/year
  • You just created $324K in enterprise value from a proper acquisition strategy

Who Should Buy This?

  • A solo operator with SaaS chops who wants high-margin, no-team profit
  • A small dev agency or micro fund that can build new apps and sell into this base
  • A content creator in the DTC/eCom space who can promote it passively
  • A buyer with an email list of founders or eCom brands who can bolt this on

Valuation Before vs. After

Today's value: $564K profit x ~2.83x = $1.6M

After implementing just 2–3 of the growth plays above:

  • Profit could grow to $750K/year
  • Using the same 2.83x multiple:
  • New valuation = $2.12M

Hey team!

I've lost millions to overthinking...

Not kidding. Maybe 10's of millions.

Last night: 2am, calculator in hand, building pro forma's for something I can't stop thinking about...

And it hit me.

Possibly the largest destroyer of wealth in human history is just overthinking.

The richest people I know aren't smarter than you. They're not more talented.

Many are much more stupid than you tbh.

They just make decisions FAST and act immediately.

The Secret to 8-Figure Success

Asked one of my best friends who runs multiple 8-figure businesses how tf he does it:

"I don't overthink. I decide quickly and adjust as I go."

That's it. Nothing complicated.

No MBA required. No secret mastermind.

Just speed of execution.

While you're perfecting your business plan, someone else launched the same idea and is making money.

While you're optimizing your funnel, they're closing deals with an imperfect pitch.

My $30M "Accident"

DMO Holdings - my most successful business - sold for $30M but launched with a WIX WEBSITE....as basic as could be.

The businesses I spent MONTHS meticulously planning? Most never even got off the ground.

The pattern is painfully obvious:

My success has been INVERSELY proportional to my planning time.

What Actually Makes Money

Know what makes you money?

The sloppy, unfinished ideas that you just launch.

Not the perfect business model. Not the flawless marketing plan. Not the immaculate financial projection.

Just the stuff you actually put out into the world, however imperfect.

We get ONE life. And it moves fast.

Your first version will suck anyway.

So launch at 70% ready.

That's my new rule. When something's 70% there, I ship it.

Learn from real results, not theories. Build momentum. Momentum beats perfection.

Stop planning. Start building.

emails.subject: 💸 The Side Hustle Trap: Why Smart Entrepreneurs Buy Businesses Instead
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

Last week, I was in Austin for Bitcoin Startup Day, sipping an overpriced cold brew at a trendy coffee shop near the convention center.

That's where I met Mark - a young developer with dark circles under his eyes who recognized me from Twitter.

"I've tried everything," he confessed after we got talking. "Dropshipping, Amazon FBA, day trading crypto... none of it sticks."

I smiled, because I'd heard this story a hundred times before.

The problem wasn't the business models. It was how he approached them.

The Fatal Flaw in Most Side Hustles

The world keeps getting more expensive.

Housing prices? Insane. Inflation? Still biting. Job security? What's that?

So people frantically jump from one "get rich quick" scheme to the next.

But here's what separates the people who build real wealth from those who don't:

They don't chase side hustles. They acquire assets with proven cash flow.

The Graveyard of Abandoned Side Hustles

"Dropshipping is dead!"

I literally had to stop myself from laughing when a 23-year-old "guru" told me this at a conference.

I actually know someone doing over $300,000/month dropshipping specialized equipment.

I know of another entrepreneur pulling in around $40,000/month with a content site in a "boring" niche that hasn't changed in 20 years.

The difference? They didn't invent something new. They bought something that was already working.

The Math That Changes Your Life

Let's break down what happens when you buy a small, established business making $1,000/month and grow it to $3,000/month:

  • That's not just $2,000 more in your pocket each month.
  • That's not just mortgage-payment money.
  • That's $50,000-$100,000 of enterprise value you've created.

Read that again.

When you sell, businesses typically go for 24-50X monthly profit.

So that $2,000/month increase? That's potentially a $100,000 payday when you exit.

All from a business you didn't even have to build from scratch.

The Reality Nobody Talks About

I recently heard about someone whose story really stuck with me:

Three years ago, a woman I'll call Sarah lost her corporate job of 15 years. At 47, she was terrified of starting over.

Instead of panicking, she bought a small Etsy shop making around $1,200/month selling digital planners.

She didn't reinvent the wheel. The business was already working. It had product-market fit. Customers loved it.

From what I understand, she simply improved the marketing, added complementary products, and optimized the operation.

Today, that "side hustle" reportedly generates five figures monthly, and she apparently turned down a substantial acquisition offer.

"I never thought of myself as an entrepreneur," she reportedly said. "I just wanted something stable that I controlled."

The Blueprint for Real Wealth

This isn't about dropshipping vs. SaaS vs. content sites.

It's about the approach:

  1. Find businesses with proven demand (2+ years of sales history)
  2. Look for opportunities others overlook (boring niches win)
  3. Buy the business (often for surprisingly reasonable prices)
  4. Optimize what's already working
  5. Scale methodically
  6. Enjoy the cash flow or flip for a life-changing exit

Whether it's a micro-SaaS tool, an e-commerce brand, or a media site – the formula works if you work it.

Your Next Move

Look around you. The most successful people I know aren't chasing the latest fad on TikTok.

They're quietly buying cash-flowing assets that others have already proven work.

And unlike real estate or stocks, these online businesses are still massively undervalued.

So here's my question for you:

What's stopping you from making your next side hustle your last side hustle?

Hit reply and tell me your biggest obstacle. I read every response.

Thanks y'all!

James

P.S.

We're opening up 3 slots for one-on-one help finding a business within your budget and putting together a plan to potentially double your revenue in the next 12 months.

Reply with "LAST SIDE HUSTLE" if you're interested.

"I've tried everything," he confessed after we got talking. "Dropshipping, Amazon FBA, day trading crypto... none of it sticks."

I smiled, because I'd heard this story a hundred times before.

The problem wasn't the business models. It was how he approached them.

The Fatal Flaw in Most Side Hustles

The world keeps getting more expensive.

Housing prices? Insane. Inflation? Still biting. Job security? What's that?

So people frantically jump from one "get rich quick" scheme to the next.

But here's what separates the people who build real wealth from those who don't:

They don't chase side hustles. They acquire assets with proven cash flow.

The Graveyard of Abandoned Side Hustles

"Dropshipping is dead!"

I literally had to stop myself from laughing when a 23-year-old "guru" told me this at a conference.

I actually know someone doing over $300,000/month dropshipping specialized equipment.

I know of another entrepreneur pulling in around $40,000/month with a content site in a "boring" niche that hasn't changed in 20 years.

The difference? They didn't invent something new. They bought something that was already working.

The Math That Changes Your Life

Let's break down what happens when you buy a small, established business making $1,000/month and grow it to $3,000/month:

  • That's not just $2,000 more in your pocket each month.
  • That's not just mortgage-payment money.
  • That's $50,000-$100,000 of enterprise value you've created.

Read that again.

When you sell, businesses typically go for 24-50X monthly profit.

So that $2,000/month increase? That's potentially a $100,000 payday when you exit.

All from a business you didn't even have to build from scratch.

The Reality Nobody Talks About

I recently heard about someone whose story really stuck with me:

Three years ago, a woman I'll call Sarah lost her corporate job of 15 years. At 47, she was terrified of starting over.

Instead of panicking, she bought a small Etsy shop making around $1,200/month selling digital planners.

She didn't reinvent the wheel. The business was already working. It had product-market fit. Customers loved it.

From what I understand, she simply improved the marketing, added complementary products, and optimized the operation.

Today, that "side hustle" reportedly generates five figures monthly, and she apparently turned down a substantial acquisition offer.

"I never thought of myself as an entrepreneur," she reportedly said. "I just wanted something stable that I controlled."

The Blueprint for Real Wealth

This isn't about dropshipping vs. SaaS vs. content sites.

It's about the approach:

  1. Find businesses with proven demand (2+ years of sales history)
  2. Look for opportunities others overlook (boring niches win)
  3. Buy the business (often for surprisingly reasonable prices)
  4. Optimize what's already working
  5. Scale methodically
  6. Enjoy the cash flow or flip for a life-changing exit

Whether it's a micro-SaaS tool, an e-commerce brand, or a media site – the formula works if you work it.

Your Next Move

Look around you. The most successful people I know aren't chasing the latest fad on TikTok.

They're quietly buying cash-flowing assets that others have already proven work.

And unlike real estate or stocks, these online businesses are still massively undervalued.

So here's my question for you:

What's stopping you from making your next side hustle your last side hustle?

Possibly the Largest Destroyer of Wealth in Human History

Hey team!

I've lost millions to overthinking...

Not kidding. Maybe 10's of millions.

Last night: 2am, calculator in hand, building pro forma's for something I can't stop thinking about...

And it hit me.

Possibly the largest destroyer of wealth in human history is just overthinking.

The richest people I know aren't smarter than you. They're not more talented.

Many are much more stupid than you tbh.

They just make decisions FAST and act immediately.

The Secret to 8-Figure Success

Asked one of my best friends who runs multiple 8-figure businesses how tf he does it:

"I don't overthink. I decide quickly and adjust as I go."

That's it. Nothing complicated.

No MBA required. No secret mastermind.

Just speed of execution.

The Reality Check

While you're perfecting your business plan, someone else launched the same idea and is making money.

While you're optimizing your funnel, they're closing deals with an imperfect pitch.

While you're tweaking your website for the 50th time, they've already collected customer feedback and improved their offering twice.

My $30M "Accident"

Want to know something embarrassing?

DMO Holdings - my most successful business - sold for $30M but launched with a WIX WEBSITE....as basic as could be.

The businesses I spent MONTHS meticulously planning? Most never even got off the ground.

The pattern is painfully obvious:

My success has been INVERSELY proportional to my planning time.

What Actually Makes Money

Know what makes you money?

The sloppy, unfinished ideas that you just launch.

Not the perfect business model. Not the flawless marketing plan. Not the immaculate financial projection.

Just the stuff you actually put out into the world, however imperfect.

The 70% Rule That Changed Everything

We get ONE life. And it moves fast.

Your first version will suck anyway.

So launch at 70% ready.

That's my new rule. When something's 70% there, I ship it.

Learn from real results, not theories. Build momentum. Momentum beats perfection.

My "Anti-Overthinking" System

After my 2AM revelation, I created four simple rules:

  1. (almost) All business decisions must be made within 24 hours
  2. Everything launches at 70% ready, not 100%
  3. Any idea without traction in 60 days gets killed (to make room for the next one)

Will I make mistakes? Absolutely. Will I make more money? Without question.

Your Overthinking is Costing You Millions

The gap between where you are and where you want to be isn't knowledge.

It's applied knowledge.

Your overthinking is costing you millions too.

Stop planning. Start building.

Your Next Move (Like, Right Now)

Close this email.

Take that business idea you've been overthinking.

Cut your planning time in half.

Set a launch date for next week.

Then hit reply and tell me what you're launching so I can hold you accountable. I read every email personally.

Thanks y'all!

James

The Secret Weapon Every Deal Hunter Needs

Hey team!

You know what separates the pros from the amateurs in business buying?

Pattern recognition.

And here's the thing - it's going to be your absolute best friend.

But there's only one way to develop it...

The Grind That Pays Off

You've got to try again and again and again and again.

Eventually, you'll spot a $200k business selling for $20k.

Okay, maybe that's a slight exaggeration... but my point stands.

You'll see opportunities others miss because you recognize the patterns.

(Side note: AI will get scary good at this too and probably replace humans eventually. But for now? This is our edge.)

The 5-Second Rule

I can look at any listing and know within 5 seconds if it's worth another hour of my time.

You need to be able to do that too.

Sure, you could hire a consultant. You could get help. That might save you tons of time.

But I recommend learning to do it yourself first.

Think Like You're House Hunting

Here's the comparison I always make...

If you were buying a house, you wouldn't just look at the first Zillow listing and wire the money, right?

You'd walk through neighborhoods.

You'd open doors, flush toilets, flip light switches.

You'd bring a broker. Check comps. Calculate price per square foot.

You'd actually KNOW what a good deal looks like.

Same Game, Different Playing Field

This is identical when buying internet businesses.

Doesn't matter if it's:

  • A newsletter
  • A SaaS
  • An e-com brand
  • An Amazon KDP business

You NEED to understand what healthy businesses look like.

Your Pattern Recognition Bootcamp

Here's your homework:

Step 1: Go study the good, healthy businesses selling for premium prices.

Reverse engineer them. See how they work.

Step 2: Start looking at listings and having actual conversations with sellers.

What are the red flags? Do they respond quickly? Are financials organized?

Step 3: Compare and contrast.

What do the expensive, healthy businesses have that's consistent?

What are the cheaper, broken ones missing?

We're All Just Meat Computers

The truth is, we're pattern-matching machines.

And eventually, computer computers will replace us meat computers. (They already have for a lot of jobs.)

But if you're scared to buy something and feeling totally lost...

It's because you don't recognize the pattern yet.

The Solution Is Simple

Go gather the data.

Study the businesses that are crushing it.

Learn their marketing strategies. Their operations. Their financials.

Then when you see undervalued businesses, you'll instantly spot what's missing.

That's when you pounce.

Think of it as your personal deal scout.

While you're building your pattern recognition skills, we'll be out there identifying opportunities that match your criteria.

Reply with "Deal Flow" and I'll send you the details when we launch.

Remember: The patterns are there. You just need to train your eye to see them.

Thanks y'all!

James

The $800k Lesson Hiding in Plain Sight

Hey yall!

So I saw this tweet about ListKit hitting $800,000 in monthly recurring revenue and it got me thinking.

Nick Abraham
@NickAbraham12
ListKit hit $800,000 MRR using a genius hybrid offer - Run ads to cold email infra set-up offer - Break even on $1500 price point - Set client up with ListKit subscription ($500-$1000/mo) Basically takes the SaaS co's acquisition cost to $0 and boosts profit
10:56 AM • Jun 13, 2025
6
Retweets
72
Likes
Read 5 replies
​

They run ads to get people to buy their cold email setup service for $1,500. Break even on that. Then they get those same customers into their SaaS subscription for $500-1k per month.

Customer acquisition cost basically becomes zero. Everything after that first sale is pure profit.

Its the playbook more entrepreneurs should be running.

I've Seen This Before

This reminds me of what we did with Cannuka, our CBD skin cream business.

We were first order profitable. We'd break even (or make a little money) on that very first purchase. Then anything else customers bought from our email or SMS was gravy.

It worked.

Compare that to Blue Angels Hearing, a business I bought and flipped. We improved revenue by fixing their pricing and making the funnel better. But even after those improvements, it was still brutal because once someone buys hearing aids, their problem is solved. They're done. No repeat purchases. You're constantly spending money to find new customers because the old ones don't need you anymore.

That's a tough business model.

ListKit figured out how to avoid that trap entirely.

This Should Be Normal

Most companies pay money to acquire customers and don't see that cash back for months.

They're burning money and hoping the lifetime value math works out eventually.

But if you can break even upfront? Everything else is bonus money.

This shouldn't be some genius strategy. This should be how every business operates.

How to Find These Opportunities

When you're looking at buying a business, ask different questions:

What's missing? Is there no way to break even upfront? Are they missing recurring revenue? What about other products they could sell?

Look at their competitors. What are others doing that this business isn't?

Here's something you can try - ask ChatGPT o3 to analyze the business and competitors, then suggest products that could work as break-even offers or recurring revenue streams.

This works for services, ecommerce, software. All of it.

Here is a prompt for ya:

Analyze [business/product name] and all major competitors in this space. What complementary products or services could create a front-end break-even offer that funds customer acquisition? What recurring revenue streams are they missing? Give me 10 specific product ideas that could work as either lead magnets or profit-generating front-end offers that transition customers into higher-value recurring purchases.

Stop Selling Yourself Short

The biggest mistake I see is everyone underpricing their stuff.

I do it. You probably do it too.

If you're competing on price, you're screwed. You end up in a race to the bottom with no margins.

You want to compete on value. Price can be part of it, but it shouldn't be everything.

ListKit charges $1,500 for setup. That's not cheap. But it works because it funds their customer acquisition while positioning them as premium.

What Are You Going to Do?

Take a business you own or one you're thinking about buying.

What's missing? What could you add to break even upfront? What recurring revenue are you leaving on the table?

The math is simple: Break even on acquisition plus recurring revenue equals a business that actually works.

ListKit is doing $800k/month with this.

Stop making excuses and figure out how to make it work for you.

Thanks y'all!

The first deal will feel awkward. Your LOI will feel small. Your diligence questions will feel basic. That is fine. Owners learn in public. Week one you fix something obvious. Week two you ship one change that touches revenue. Week three you do it again. That rhythm is how you change your life. While you read this, someone else is writing the offer you wanted to make.

Quick Update

We’re building a one-week intensive on buying your first business. No fluff. No theory. You will learn how to find deals within your budget, run fast diligence that actually protects you, price your offer responsibly, and set up the first 30 days so you don’t burn cash.

The goal is simple: save you from a $100,000 mistake and shorten the path to your first win. Details next week.

This Week’s Opportunity

A Food Blog With ~171K Pageviews And 300+ Recipes

Here is the listing: profitable food blog with ~171K monthly pageviews and Mediavine/AdThrive approval.

The page shows an asking price of $150,000, monthly profit of $3,288, about 167K pageviews, and a claimed 97% margin.

If you’re new, run it like this

Before the LOI

  1. Ask for read-only GA4 and Search Console. Verify pageviews, country mix, device split, top pages, top queries.
  2. Ask for screenshots from the ad network dashboard and a few months of bank deposits.
  3. Open 30 URLs and read them. Are they original, useful, and consistent.
  4. Skim backlinks for junk. Confirm transfer of theme, plugins, photo and video rights, and social accounts.
  5. Price for risk. You are buying what it earns today, not the seller’s best month.

Days 1–7 after close

  1. Freeze big changes. Turn on daily backups with UpdraftPlus or your host’s backup.
  2. Create a staging site.
  3. Fix Core Web Vitals basics. Compress images with ShortPixel, lazy-load media, defer heavy scripts. Keep ad density inside network policy.
  4. Set uptime monitoring with UptimeRobot.

Days 8–30

  1. Add one clean email form to the top 30 posts. Use ConvertKit or Beehiiv. Offer a 7-day dinner plan. Send a welcome email that links your three best posts.
  2. Refresh the top 40 posts by clicks. Add step photos, a short FAQ, and two internal links to related recipes.
  3. Re-pin those refreshed posts. Schedule in Tailwind.
  4. Shoot short verticals for your top 20 recipes. Edit quickly in CapCut or Canva. Embed the video on the post. Publish to Shorts and TikTok.

Month 2

  1. Ship one tiny product. A $9–$15 PDF like a 4-week dinner plan or “30 weeknight dinners.” Sell with Gumroad or Shopify Starter.
  2. Add a light affiliate layer for tools you actually use. Keep it honest and sparse.
  3. Publish at a sustainable pace. One new or one refreshed post per week is enough if quality is real.

Months 3–4

  1. If traffic is stable for 30 days, run one ad layout test within network policy.

How you keep growing after month 4

• Create an editorial SOP: required photos, nutrition info, substitution notes, storage, and a 5-question FAQ per post. Use WP Recipe Maker or your recipe card plugin to ensure proper schema.
• Refresh cycle: every 120 days update ingredients, photos, and FAQs on your top 30 posts. Mark changes in a simple Airtable.

Internal linking and structure​
• Add a “related recipes” box that links to two within the same cluster and one to the pillar.
• Use a simple table of contents and a jump-to-recipe button so time on page is high without annoying readers.

Search and on-page​
• For each new post: one primary query and two support queries. Answer them in the FAQ.
• Keep titles human. Front-load cuisine, method, or key ingredient.
• Add structured data for Recipe and HowTo through the recipe card.

Media and distribution​
• Weekly video cadence: 2 quick verticals from existing posts, 1 B-roll montage.
• Pinterest: 3 fresh pins per new or refreshed post, 1 story pin.
• Web stories for your top 10 posts if your theme supports it.

Email and product​
• Welcome sequence: 4 emails over 10 days. Intro, quick wins, a shopping list email, and a “what to cook next” curation.
• Product ladder: start with the $9–$15 PDF. If it sells, create a $29 bundle with a seasonal add-on.
• Promote product gently inside the welcome email and once per month to the list.

Light link building that actually works​
• Roundup outreach to mid-tier food blogs. Offer one exclusive new photo or a tip for their roundup.
• Local angle PR: pitch one seasonal recipe with a short quote to local lifestyle outlets.
• Replace any spammy links with real citations over time.

Risk management​
• Don’t change URLs or delete posts without a redirect plan.
• Don’t add intrusive interstitials that violate ad network rules.
• Track a 6-week rolling average of sessions and EPMV so you see trend, not noise.

The deal math, with a little more pace

$150,000

Day-one net​
About $3,288 per month

Planned ramp​
Months 1–3 net about $3,300​
Months 4–6 net about $3,700​
Months 7–9 net about $4,100​
Months 10–12 net about $4,600

What that produces​
Average net during year 1 about $3,925 per month​
Cash flow in year 1 about $47,100​
Exit value if you sell on month-12 net at 3.3x to 3.6x annual about $182,160 to $198,720​
One-year ROI on a $150,000 purchase about 53% to 64%​
Profit equals exit plus cash flow minus purchase, roughly $79,260 to $95,820

Month-12 net about $5,200 with stronger refresh, slightly better EPMV, and a small product that sells
Average net during year 1 about $4,275 per month​
Cash flow in year 1 about $51,300​

Notes. Nets include normal tools and light help. Excludes taxes, migration costs, and marketplace fees. All of this assumes diligence checks out and traffic plus RPM hold after your changes.

• E-commerce:viral home décor Shopify brand. Entry ticket is digestible. Verify CAC, refunds, supplier terms, and whether profit holds when you scale paid.

emails.subject: 💰 Who wants this SBA Pre-Qualified: FDA Device w/ 380K Emails + 21 Patents Biz
emails.content:
Nano Thought

The SBA Lending Boom Is Real (And Here's Proof)

Hey y'all!

Every decent business in my inbox this week is SBA pre-qualified. This isn't random - SBA lending is expected to rise by 10-12%, hitting $55-56 billion in 2025.

Even crazier? Manufacturing SBA loans just jumped 74% compared to last year, with over 1,120 loans approved totaling $677 million. The banks are HUNGRY.

When you can get into a $900K business for just $90K down (10%), the math changes everything. Smart operators are stacking deals - buy one cash-flowing business, use that cash to qualify for the next.

If you've been waiting for "the right time" - this is it. Current SBA 7(a) rates range from 9.5% to 10.5% variable, but banks are competing hard for your business.

​Read more about the 2025 SBA lending surge here →​

This Week's Opportunities

Featured Deal: FDA-Approved Neck Pain Device

Patented Medical Device with Massive Untapped Database

Here's the star from Quiet Light's latest listings - a proven medical device with incredible IP protection.

The Numbers:

  • Annual Revenue: $708,369
  • Net Profit: $259,961 (36.7% margins)
  • Asking Price: $909,000 + ~$50K inventory
  • SBA Pre-Qualified (10% down = ~$90K)

What Makes This Special:

  • FDA Class I Medical Device (HSA/FSA eligible)
  • 21 design and utility patents across multiple countries
  • Nearly 7,000 reviews averaging 4+ stars
  • 380,000+ customer email list (COMPLETELY UNUSED)
  • Previous licensee hit $7M revenue with this exact product
  • Only requires 5 hours/week to run

Real-World Growth Strategy (Including SBA Payments):

Let's model this properly with loan payments included:

SBA Loan Structure:

  • Purchase Price: $909,000
  • Down Payment (10%): $90,900
  • Loan Amount: $818,100
  • Terms: 10 years at 10% interest
  • Monthly Payment: ~$10,800 ($129,600/year)

Year 1: Building While Paying the Bank

Starting Position:

  • Base business profit: $259,961
  • Less SBA payments: -$129,600
  • Net cash before improvements: $130,361

Hire Specialists (Month 1):

  • Part-time Email Marketing Manager: $2,500/month
  • Amazon PPC Specialist (contractor): $1,500/month
  • Meta Ads Manager (agency): $2,000/month + 10% of spend
  • Total new OpEx: $6,000/month ($72,000/year)

Email Marketing (Months 1-12)

  • Deliverable list: 15% of 380K = 57,000 contacts
  • Months 1-3: Cleaning, segmentation, re-engagement
  • Months 4-12: 1.5% monthly purchase rate = $8,550/month
  • Annual revenue: ~$77,000

Here's the secret sauce: You're not just selling your device. These are neck pain sufferers who also buy ergonomic pillows, standing desks, massage guns, and CBD creams. By sending two affiliate emails monthly promoting complementary products, you can generate an extra $3,000/month with zero inventory risk. The key is choosing products that solve related problems - if someone has neck pain, they likely have back pain too.

Amazon PPC (Months 2-12)

  • Start: $3K/month, scale to $8K by month 6
  • Average ROAS: 2.2x (specialist managing)
  • Additional revenue: $132,000
  • After fees and COGS (60% total): $52,800 gross profit

Meta Ads (Months 3-12)

  • Start: $2K/month, scale to $6K by month 9
  • Average ROAS: 1.8x
  • Additional revenue: $72,000
  • After costs (65% total): $25,200 gross profit

The game-changer for Meta ads is the "60-Second Relief Challenge" - a user-generated content strategy where customers film their first minute using the device. These authentic reaction videos ("Oh my god, I can feel it working!") get 40% lower CPMs than polished branded content. You pay creators $50 per video, run them as Spark Ads through their accounts, and watch your cost per acquisition drop by half. Real people showing real relief beats any professional ad campaign.

Year 1 Actual Cash Flow:

  • Base business profit: $259,961
  • New channel gross profit: $155,000
  • Less new OpEx: -$72,000
  • Less SBA payments: -$129,600
  • Year 1 net cash: $213,361

Year 2: Scaled Operations

Revenue Growth:

  • Email: $120,000 (list grows to 75K deliverable)
  • Amazon: $240,000 (at $15K/month spend, 2.3x ROAS)
  • Meta: $180,000 (at $12K/month spend, 2.0x ROAS)
  • Total new revenue: $540,000
  • Gross profit (40% margin): $216,000
  • OpEx increases to $96,000 (team expansion)

Year 2 Actual Cash Flow:

  • Base business profit: $259,961
  • New channel gross profit: $216,000
  • Less OpEx: -$96,000
  • Less SBA payments: -$129,600
  • Year 2 net cash: $250,361

24-Month Reality Check:

  • Total cash collected: $463,722
  • Business value at 3.5x (Year 2 profit before debt): $1,329,263
  • Less remaining loan balance: ~$770,000
  • Business equity value: $559,263
  • Total value (cash + equity): $1,022,985
  • Initial investment: $90,900

True ROI on $90,900 down: 1,025% over 24 months

Even after paying the bank $259,200 over two years, you've collected $463,722 in cash and built $559,263 in equity. The business essentially paid for itself while you improved it.

The real value? You own a proven medical device business with strong IP protection. Even modest improvements create value while you collect $260K+ annually.

The beauty? Previous operator already proved the $7M ceiling exists. You're not pioneering - just executing a proven playbook.

​View the full listing on Quiet Light →​

This is all hypothetical, run your own numbers!

Three More Hot Opportunities

1. Premium Science Blog - Traffic Monster

​Available on Flippa​

  • Annual Revenue: $1,400,000 (display ads)
  • Estimated Profit: ~$980,000 (70% margin typical for display)
  • Asking Price: $5M
  • The Deal: 18 years old, 9M+ monthly pageviews, 97% organic traffic
  • Why It's Hot: Completely passive income, survived every Google update, massive traffic you can monetize multiple ways

2. Digital Marketing Agency - Recurring Revenue Machine

​Listed on Website Closers​

  • Annual Revenue: $1,220,487
  • Net Profit: $289,813 (24% margin)
  • Asking Price: $870,000 (3.0x multiple)
  • The Deal: 85% recurring revenue, 40% YoY profit growth, SBA pre-qualified
  • Why It's Hot: Only $87K down with SBA, predictable cash flow, proven 15-year track record

3. Freebie & Deals Affiliate - Part-Time Goldmine

​Check on Quiet Light​

  • Annual Revenue: $36,973
  • Net Profit: $30,696 (83% margin!)
  • Asking Price: $90,000 (2.9x multiple)
  • The Deal: 100K email subscribers, only 1 hour daily management
  • Why It's Hot: Highest margins I've ever seen, truly passive, no SEO dependency

Thought Leader Theater

This Week: Alex Hormozi on Why "The Slow Way Is The Fast Way"

Hormozi emphasizes that finding solutions to business problems doesn't provide immediate relief. Patience is crucial during the implementation period. He shares that companies like Microsoft and OpenAI took six to eight years to reach prominence.

His key insight: Every "shortcut" you take today creates two problems tomorrow. The businesses obsessed with "growth hacking" often grow the slowest because they're constantly fighting fires.

This perfectly explains why that science blog (18 years old) and neck device (building since 2019) are such solid acquisitions. They've built real foundations, not houses of cards.

​Watch Alex break this down on The Game Podcast →​

Or check out his YouTube channel where he shares these insights weekly.

Next week we are launching a new workshop! Keep your eyes peeled.

Thanks y'all!

James

Want to reach 15,000+ business entrepreneurs and investors? Email hi@nanoflips.com

All investment strategies involve risk of loss. Nothing contained in this newsletter should be construed as investment advice.

Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

It's October 1st. Q4 starts TODAY.

Where the hell did 2024 go?

Feels like we can't catch our breath anymore. War everywhere, chaos in politics, AI changing everything faster than we can process it.

And yesterday OpenAI dropped Sora 2.

I think it's terrible for society.

Seriously. We're about to drown in fake content.

But I'm also a realist. And whether we like it or not, this is happening. So we might as well figure out how to use it.

Everyone's Missing the Actual Opportunity

You know those faceless YouTube channels that just run on autopilot?

​Lofi Girl makes between $30K-$135K monthly. From animated music that loops forever.

Some kid in the Philippines - 21 years old, makes $9K a month from AI kitten videos. I'm not making this up. He just churns out 1-2 videos a day using ChatGPT and some tool called KlingAI.

600,000 subscribers. Half a billion views.

From AI cats doing stupid things.

Here's what kills me - he's not even using the good stuff yet. He's using tools from 6 months ago that look like garbage compared to Sora.

The Math That Actually Matters

Forget the hype for a second.

Here's what I'm actually thinking about:

You can buy a small SaaS business right now for $50-100K. Maybe it's doing $2-3K monthly profit. Nothing sexy.

Now imagine you can create product demo videos in an afternoon instead of paying $2-5K to an agency.

Imagine you can test 10 different video ads this week instead of one.

Not revolutionary. Just... faster. Cheaper. More iterations.

That business doing $3K/month becomes $5K/month. Your multiple goes from 3x to 4x because you've got proven marketing channels.

You just made $100K.

That's the real opportunity. Not building the next YouTube empire. Just making existing businesses better with tools that didn't exist 12 months ago.

Why I'm Actually Paying Attention

​Small business optimism just hit levels we haven't seen since 2021.

The Fed cut rates three times in Q4.

​Online business sales are up 22% this year.

You know what this means?

People are buying again. After two years of sitting on their hands, entrepreneurs are moving.

And most of them have no idea what's possible with AI video yet.

Here's the Part That Makes Me Uncomfortable

I watched this NPR piece about "AI slop" taking over social media.

They're not wrong. It's mostly garbage.

But buried in there was this: These terrible AI videos are making real money. Thousands per month. Some hitting millions of views.

If terrible AI content works, what happens when someone who actually gives a shit uses these tools?

What happens when you use it to explain your product better? To reach Spanish-speaking customers? To test which messaging actually converts?

That's what I'm interested in.

The Clock Is Already Ticking

Everyone thinks they have more time than they do.

"I'll figure out AI next year."

"I'll buy a business when things calm down."

"I'll start that project after the holidays."

Meanwhile, some virtual YouTuber named Bloo already crossed $1M in revenue. It's literally an AI playing video games.

The creator built it to avoid burnout. Now the AI does the work while he sleeps.

This is happening RIGHT NOW. Not in some theoretical future.

What I'm Watching

Over the next few months, pay attention to:

  1. Businesses for sale that have weak marketing - These are goldmines if you know how to create content at scale
  2. SaaS tools under $250K - They're trading at 4.8x revenue but that multiple jumps when you add predictable acquisition channels
  3. Any business with educational potential - If you can teach it, you can create endless video content about it

The people who move on this in Q4 are going to look like geniuses by Q2 2025.

Not because they're smarter. Just because they moved while everyone else was still complaining about how AI is ruining everything.

(Which it might be. But that's a different newsletter.)

Remember - we're only here once.

The time's going to pass whether you do something with it or not.

Might as well take the swing.

Thanks y'all!

James

P.S. Yeah, I know this sounds a bit dystopian. Using AI to pump out content to buy businesses to pump out more content. I get it. But someone's going to do it. I'd rather it be people who are building real businesses and creating actual value than the spam farms.

The email list is the lowest hanging fruit here. They have 213,891 subscribers opening at 67.5%, but they're only running basic campaigns. No abandoned cart sequence, no browse abandonment, no proper segmentation. This is leaving serious money on the table.

Pinterest users are planning their trips 6+ months in advance, making it perfect for travel jewelry. A modest $1,500 monthly ad spend with organic pinning should easily hit 2x ROAS. Travel and jewelry are two of Pinterest's biggest categories - this is about as safe a bet as you can make in paid media.

The Math:

  • Revenue: $3,000/month × 12 = $36,000
  • Ad spend: -$18,000
  • COGS (23%): -$8,280
  • Annual profit: $9,720

The Final Numbers

Starting from $450,000 in annual profit, these conservative improvements add $367,054, bringing the total to $817,054 in annual profit. At a standard 4x multiple for growing ecommerce brands, that's a $3.27M valuation.

Buy for $2.3M (including inventory), implement basic modern ecommerce practices, sell for $3.27M in 18 months. That's a $970K profit on your investment, or about 42% ROI.

The beauty here is that none of this is revolutionary. It's just properly executing on channels that already exist. And if you decided not to flip it? With all channels firing, this could easily become a $10M revenue brand in three years.

Other Businesses This Week

emails.subject: 💸 You're making $200k and still one decision away from zero
emails.content:
Hey {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

I had dinner last week with a friend who's killing it at a tech company.

$280k base. Stock options. The whole package.

We're halfway through our second bottle of wine and he says something that stuck with me:

"I make more money than I ever thought I would. And I've never felt more financially insecure."

He's not wrong to feel that way.

Because here's what the World Economic Forum just reported: 48% of US employers are planning to downsize their workforce in the next five years because of AI.

Not just entry-level positions. Not just "low-skill" jobs.

They're coming for the $150k-$300k roles. The analysts. The managers. The consultants.

The people who thought their education and salary meant they were safe.

The Golden Handcuffs Are Getting Tighter

You're probably doing well.

Six figures. Maybe multiple six figures.

Nice house. Good benefits. Your LinkedIn looks impressive.

But let me ask you something:

If your company "restructured" tomorrow, how long would it take you to replace that income?

Three months? Six months? A year?

And how much of your lifestyle is built on that salary continuing forever?

The mortgage. The car payments. The private school. The lifestyle creep that happened so gradually you didn't even notice.

You've built a life that requires you to keep making what you're making.

That's not security. That's leverage. And your company holds it.

Your Comp Package Is Your Biggest Liability

Here's what nobody tells you about making good money as an employee:

You become REALLY expensive to keep around.

Your $200k salary + benefits + equity is nearly $300k all-in to your company.

You know what $300k buys them now? A team of AI tools and one person making $80k to manage them.

They're not going to fire you because you're bad at your job.

They're going to fire you because you're expensive. And they found a cheaper way.

Big Tech already reduced new graduate hiring by 25% in 2024.

But here's what they're not advertising: They're also quietly cutting mid-level and senior positions.

The ones that pay $150k-$400k.

Your salary isn't protecting you. It's painting a target on your back.

Real Wealth vs. Rich Salary

I sold my media company for over $30M.

You know what I learned? Making a big salary and building real wealth are completely different games.

Salary is trading time for money. Even if it's good money.

Wealth is owning things that make money whether you're working or not.

You're smart enough to know this already. That's why you max out your 401k. Why you have a brokerage account.

But here's what most high earners miss:

The fastest way to build wealth isn't climbing the ladder. It's buying assets that produce cash flow.

Like businesses. Even a little side hustle one.

The Numbers That Actually Matter

You're making $150k-$300k. That's great.

You know what's better? Owning a business doing $3k-$8k/month in profit.

That's $36k-$96k a year. In YOUR pocket. That you own.

And unlike your salary, it doesn't disappear if AI gets better or your company decides they need to "optimize costs."

I've helped dozens of people making six figures buy their first business.

Real businesses in the $50k-$250k range:

  • Content site doing $2,800/month profit, bought for $85k. Two years later doing $4,200/month. BLOWING UP on FB.
  • SaaS tool doing $4k/month, acquired for $120k. Owner scaled it to $6,500/month in 18 months.
  • Newsletter business doing $5k/month, bought for $150k. Runs it in 10 hours a week, now at $7k/month.

These people aren't gambling. They're being smart.

They saw the writing on the wall and decided to diversify their income before they had to.

What This Looks Like In Practice

Most of my clients who make $150k+ use this strategy:

Keep the job. Buy a business. Hire an operator or manage it part-time.

You're not betting the farm. You're de-risking your life.

Because if shit hits the fan at work? You've got something else.

And if work goes great? You're building wealth faster than your salary ever could.

One client bought a content business for $95k doing $3,200/month.

Kept his $180k job. Hired a VA for $2k/month to run most of it.

Now the business does $4,500/month. He nets about $2,500/month after the VA.

That's $30k a year in his pocket for something he spends maybe 5 hours a month on.

His salary is his income. His business is his wealth.

And he sleeps better knowing he's not 100% dependent on his company.

The Opportunity Cost of Waiting

Every month you don't own a business is a month you're leaving money on the table.

Not just potential profit. Actual wealth building.

Your peers who bought businesses three years ago? They're either running them full-time and making more than they ever did. Or they sold them for 3-5x what they paid.

Meanwhile, everyone else is hoping their company's stock options will vest before the next round of layoffs.

I'm not trying to be dramatic. I'm trying to be real.

You're too smart to put all your eggs in one basket. Especially when that basket is held by someone else.

What's Next

I'm launching something specifically for people in this exact situation.

High earners who want to diversify. Who see what's coming. Who are ready to build real wealth instead of just collecting a paycheck.

It's not ready yet. But it will be soon.

Think ongoing help, that can start and end whenever you want. For a couple hundred bucks a month.

Help finding a biz, help hiring for it, help avoiding a scam.

Or don't. Keep collecting your salary. Keep hoping the music doesn't stop.

But when 48% of companies start cutting, don't say nobody warned you.

We're here once. Buy something that's actually yours.

James

P.S. - The people who wait until they NEED to do this are the ones who make desperate decisions. The people who do this BEFORE they need to are the ones who build real wealth. Which one are you?

emails.subject: 💸 Stop looking at deals alone (you're missing the obvious)
emails.content:
Ok {{ subscriber.first_name }}!

I was on a call last week with someone who's been trying to buy a business for 6 months.

He's looked at probably 50+ deals.

Spent hours analyzing financials, traffic patterns, and growth potential.

But hasn't pulled the trigger on a single one.

Know what the problem was?

He was doing it all alone.

The Blind Spots We All Have

Here's the thing about looking at deals by yourself. You develop tunnel vision.

You either fall in love with a bad deal and ignore red flags. Or you talk yourself out of good deals because of imaginary problems. Or you miss obvious opportunities staring you right in the face.

I've been there. Hell, I'm STILL there sometimes.

That's why every single deal I look at now, I run by at least 2-3 other people who know what they're doing.

Not because I don't trust my judgment.

But because I know I have blind spots. We all do.

What I Learned Running Cohorts

When we used to run our 8-week cohorts, the craziest thing would happen.

People would come in thinking they needed ME to tell them what to buy.

But you know what actually helped them pull the trigger?

The other people in the cohort.

Someone would post a deal in Slack at 10pm. By morning, three other members had already torn it apart. Spotted the red flags, found the opportunities, shared similar deals they'd seen.

One person would say "I looked at this exact business model last month, here's what I learned."

Another would jump in with "Wait, I know someone who could run this for you."

The community did more deal vetting than I ever could alone.

And honestly? That's when people actually started BUYING businesses instead of just analyzing them to death.

The Pattern That Keeps Showing Up

I've helped over 100 people buy their first business.

You know what separates the ones who actually close deals from the ones who spin their wheels forever?

The people who close deals usually have someone else looking at stuff with them.

A business partner. A mentor. A coach. Hell, even just a friend who's been through it before.

Can you buy a business solo? Of course. I've done it plenty of times.

But it's way harder. Way slower. And you second guess yourself way more.

Why Most People Overthink This

Everyone wants to be the lone wolf entrepreneur.

Figure it all out themselves.

Prove they can do it solo.

I get it. I was the same way.

But you know what changed everything for me?

Realizing that the fastest path forward isn't doing everything myself.

It's having people who can see what I can't.

People who will tell me "James, that deal is garbage" or "Dude, why haven't you bought this yet?"

The Advantage of a Second Set of Eyes

Look, you can absolutely figure this out on your own.

But having someone look at deals with you just makes everything easier.

Find another person who's trying to buy a business. Partner up on deal review.

Got a friend who's built or bought a business before? Text them the listing.

Hell, reply to this email with a deal you're looking at and I'll give you my quick take.

The point is this. Another set of eyes helps you see clearly.

The deal you're talking yourself out of might be perfect.

The deal you're falling in love with might be a disaster.

Having someone who can spot what you're missing? That's the cheat code.

The Real Advantage

Speed beats perfectionism every single time.

The people who actually buy businesses aren't necessarily smarter than you.

They're not more qualified.

They're not seeing better deals.

They just usually have people helping them see clearly. And they move faster because of it.

You can do this alone. But you don't have to.

Thanks y'all!

James

P.S. Speaking of not going it alone, we're launching something new this week for a small beta group.

About 50 people already said they're interested when we teased it earlier, but we're probably only opening up 10-20 slots to start.

It's specifically built to solve this exact problem. Giving you that second set of eyes on deals so you can actually pull the trigger.

Details coming in the next few days. Keep an eye out.
